title: crate2: shooting the TOP crate destroys the BOTTOM crate (linkedSibling semantics inverted vs _shatterMesh)
description: The two-box crate stack sets `b.userData.linkedSibling = a` on the TOP crate, with the comment '// top breaks -> bottom still cover'. But the runtime's _shatterMesh treats linkedSibling as a mesh to DELETE when the holder breaks (main.js:33228-33229: scene.remove(sib); sib.geometry.dispose(); sib.material.dispose()). That hook exists for the `window` builder, where the pane's linkedSibling is its decorative highlight strip. So when the player shoots the top crate to break it, _shatterMesh(b) removes and disposes `a` — the bottom crate — doing the exact opposite of the comment: the lower cover vanishes. crate2 is used in B1 BE, B4 BE, B5 BW, B6 MW, B7 (3x), B9, B10, B11, B12, so this is visible in most levels.
evidence: b.userData.linkedSibling = a;  // top breaks -> bottom still cover  // …but _shatterMesh: const sib=mesh.userData.linkedSibling; if(sib){scene.remove(sib);if(sib.geometry)sib.geometry.dispose();if(sib.material&&sib.material.dispose)sib.material.dispose();}
fix: Remove the `b.userData.linkedSibling = a;` line (line 1380). linkedSibling is a 'remove this decorative child' hook, not a 'keep this as cover' link; the two crates should break independently. Each box already has its own coverHP. Optionally also store `a.userData.linkedTop = b` only if you intend to make bottom-break drop the top — but do NOT reuse linkedSibling for it.
risk: Removing the line cannot break anything that currently works (the current behavior is wrong). No save-compat or perf concern; the geometry is rebuilt per level. Leaves the top crate floating if the bottom breaks first (see crate2-bottom-break-floating), which is a separate, pre-existing issue.

title: setLUT3D disposes cache-owned LUT textures, corrupting the per-building LUT cache (use-after-dispose)
description: setLUT3D() unconditionally disposes the previously-active lut3dTexture whenever a new (or null) LUT is set. But the caller in main.js keeps a per-building cache (_lutCacheByBn, line 2080) and re-applies cached textures across building transitions. On a building change setLUT3D(newTex) disposes the OLD building's LUT even though it is still held in _lutCacheByBn. When the player returns to that building, _applyLutForBuilding hits the cache (_lutCacheByBn.has(key), line 2089) and calls setLUT3D() with a texture whose GPU resources were already freed, producing a broken/blank LUT (washed or wrong color grade) and likely a WebGL warning. The setLUT3D(null) path (LUT disabled per settings, line 2084/2105) disposes the active cached texture the same way.
fix: Stop disposing inside setLUT3D since the LUT textures are owned by main.js's _lutCacheByBn (and torn down elsewhere). Remove the `if (lut3dTexture && lut3dTexture.dispose) lut3dTexture.dispose();` block; just reassign lut3dTexture and passes.lut.lut. Alternatively, only dispose when the incoming texture is different AND the outgoing one is not present in any cache (the renderer can't know ownership, so simplest correct fix is: do not dispose). If a leak is feared, dispose cache entries explicitly from main.js teardown only.
risk: Removing the dispose could theoretically leak a LUT texture that was NOT cached, but every LUT path in main.js inserts into _lutCacheByBn before calling setLUT3D, so none are orphaned. No save-compat impact. Keeps build/probes green (pure runtime path).

title: Combo milestone FX fire twice per milestone (double toast, double money, double slowmo)
description: The comboKill wrapper calls _comboMilestoneFx on every (count%5===0 && count<=30). But the underlying comboKill (the function declaration at 35985) ALREADY calls _comboMilestoneFx on every count%5===0 (line 36005). So _comboMilestoneFx runs twice for combo counts 5/10/15/20/30: two STREAK/MASSACRE/etc banners overlap, P.money+=count*20 is added twice (line 32440), moneyPopup shows twice, the ascending fanfare SFX plays twice (phasing/doubled volume), the kill-beat flash double-triggers, and triggerKillCamSlowMo(.55,.50) fires twice at count>=10.
evidence: wrapper 32459-32461: `_origComboKill(isHead); if(P.combo&&P.combo.count%5===0&&P.combo.count<=30){ _comboMilestoneFx(P.combo.count); }` while the original comboKill at 36005 already does `if(P.combo.count%5===0&&typeof _comboMilestoneFx==='function')_comboMilestoneFx(P.combo.count);`
fix: Remove the duplicate milestone call inside the wrapper at lines 32460-32462 (the original comboKill already fires it). Keep the wrapper only if it adds something else; here it adds nothing else, so the whole wrapper at 32457-32463 can be deleted. Safest surgical change: delete lines 32460-32462 (the `if(...){_comboMilestoneFx(...)}` block) so the wrapper just forwards.
risk: Very low. After removing the duplicate, milestones fire exactly once (the design intent). No save-compat impact. Note: also fixes the related arg-drop bug below if you delete the whole wrapper.

title: Radial quick-select menu is non-functional — never exits pointer lock, mouse can't hover/click slots
description: openRadial builds DOM slots that rely on mouseenter (hover highlight) and mousedown (select+switchWeapon). But unlike showFullMap (31259) and showLoadoutViewer (32508), openRadial never calls document.exitPointerLock(). During gameplay pointer lock is active (locked=true), so the cursor is captured/hidden and cannot hover or click the slots. There is also no keyboard-number fallback while RADIAL.open. Net result: the player can open the radial (CapsLock) but can never select a weapon from it, then it closes on key release. The tutorial even advertises this feature ('Hold CAPS for radial weapon select', line 30817).
evidence: openRadial 31407 `const r=$e('radial');if(!r)return;` ... 31425 `slot.addEventListener('mousedown',()=>{ switchWeapon(i);closeRadial(); });` with no exitPointerLock; compare showFullMap 31259 `if(locked)try{document.exitPointerLock();}catch(_){}`
fix: In openRadial after RADIAL.open=true add `if(locked)try{document.exitPointerLock();}catch(_){}` and in closeRadial re-lock with `if(RADIAL.open===false&&G.started&&!P.dead&&!G.menuOpen)tryLock();` (or restore lock in the keyup handler). Alternatively (lower risk, keeps pointer lock) add a keydown handler that maps Digit1..DigitN to slots while RADIAL.open and select on key.
risk: Low-medium. Exiting pointer lock mid-combat momentarily frees the cursor; re-lock on close. The hold-to-open / release-to-close UX with CapsLock (a toggle key whose keyup timing is OS-dependent) may need testing, but the core fix (exit lock so slots are clickable) is what makes the feature work at all.

title: Endless mode fires a phantom 'WAVE 0' reward and double-schedules the first wave
description: startEndlessMode() sets ENDLESS.active=true and G.started=true immediately (lines 32913,32919) but only schedules the first wave via setTimeout(endlessNextWave,2200) (line 32949). tickEndless() runs every frame once ENDLESS.active && G.started, and its transition guard is `if(alive===0 && !ENDLESS._waveTransition)` (line 33005). ENDLESS.wave is still 0 and _waveTransition is undefined on the very first frame, so before the 2200ms timeout fires, tickEndless immediately triggers a wave-transition: it awards money (`moneyPopup(200,'WAVE 0')`), grants a free heal pack, and schedules a SECOND endlessNextWave at +3500ms. Net result: a spurious 'WAVE 0' reward popup + free heal pack at the start, and two queued endlessNextWave calls so the player effectively skips from wave 1 to wave 2 within seconds.
evidence: ENDLESS.active=true;ENDLESS.wave=0; ... setTimeout(()=>endlessNextWave(),2200);  // then in tickEndless: if(alive===0&&!ENDLESS._waveTransition){ENDLESS._waveTransition=true; const bonus=200+ENDLESS.wave*100; P.money+=bonus;moneyPopup(bonus,'WAVE '+ENDLESS.wave); P.healPacks=(P.healPacks||0)+1; ... setTimeout(()=>{ENDLESS._waveTransition=false;endlessNextWave();},3500);}
fix: Guard the transition on a started wave: change line 33005 to `if(alive===0 && ENDLESS.wave>0 && !ENDLESS._waveTransition){`. (Alternatively set ENDLESS._waveTransition=true in startEndlessMode and clear it inside the first endlessNextWave.) The `ENDLESS.wave>0` guard is the smallest surgical fix and prevents the phantom WAVE 0 reward and the double-schedule.
risk: Very low. Only changes behavior on the first frame(s) before wave 1 spawns; normal wave clears (wave>=1) are unaffected. No save-compat impact.

title: G._frame is read by 4 frame-throttle gates but is NEVER incremented anywhere — every throttle fires every frame
description: G._frame is used as a modulo divisor in four throttle conditions inside the animation loop: (G._frame|0)%20===0 -> applyScopePipRenderTargetSize() at 41578; (G._frame|0)%3===0 -> low-hp DOM opacity writes at 41689/41694 and 43743/43744/43747; and (G._frame|0)%stride===0 -> the scope PIP _renderScopeTarget() throttle at 44619. G._frame is never declared in createGameState (src/game/state.js has no _frame field) and is never written anywhere in the repo (grep for '._frame=' / '._frame++' / '._frame +=' across all src/*.js returns nothing; only G._frameAlt and G._frameSampleAt are incremented). Therefore (G._frame|0) is permanently 0, and 0%n===0 is always true. Consequences: (1) the scope-PIP render-to-texture runs EVERY frame regardless of _scopePipRenderStride()/_scopePipStatus.throttleInterval and the FPS stress-down logic at 41576-41577 — defeating an entire perf throttle while ADS'ing a scope; (2) applyScopePipRenderTargetSize() runs every frame instead of every 20; (3) the per-3-frame DOM-write throttles on the low-hp vignette run every frame. The intent (a real per-frame counter) is plainly there but the counter was never wired.
evidence: Reads: 41578 `if((G._frame|0)%20===0)applyScopePipRenderTargetSize();` · 41689/41694 `if((G._frame|0)%3===0){` · 43743 `if((G._frame|0)%3===0)_lhEl.style.opacity='0';` · 44619 `if(_shouldPip&&_contribAlpha&&((G._frame|0)%stride)===0){_renderScopeTarget(rtScope,scopeCamera);...}`. No write anywhere: grep across all src found only `G._frameAlt=(G._frameAlt|0)+1` (41659) and `G._frameSampleAt` (44661). createGameState in src/game/state.js defines no _frame.
fix: Add a single increment near the top of the animation loop, e.g. immediately after `_frameProfileBegin();` (line 41553) insert `G._frame=(G._frame|0)+1;`. This restores all four throttles at once (scope PIP stride, scope-RT resize cadence, low-hp DOM throttling). Verify _scopePipRenderStride() still returns >=1. Low risk; purely re-enables intended throttling.
risk: Re-enabling the scope-PIP stride means the PIP texture updates every Nth frame again (N=stride) — visually the scope content will update at the throttled cadence as originally designed; under high FPS this is imperceptible but worth a quick ADS-scope smoke check. No save-compat impact. Net perf win.

title: NECK/SPINE critical hits do no bonus (and SPINE does a penalty) because consumer divides crit mul by 2.0
description: _isCritHit returns body-shot crits NECK {crit:true,mul:2.0} and SPINE {crit:true,mul:1.7}. The shoot path (line 26417) applies damage as baseDmg * ... * (_critInfo.crit?(_critInfo.mul/2.0):1.0) where baseDmg=W.dmg for a body hit. The /2.0 normalization only makes sense for HEAD-derived crits (where baseDmg is already hsDmg=2x body). For a NECK hit this yields W.dmg*(2.0/2.0)=W.dmg (no bonus despite the 'NECK = 2x crit' comment). For a SPINE hit it yields W.dmg*(1.7/2.0)=0.85*W.dmg, i.e. a critical hit deals LESS than a normal body shot.
evidence: _isCritHit: "if(distToNeck<.10)return {crit:true,type:'NECK',mul:2.0};" and "return {crit:true,type:'SPINE',mul:1.7};". Consumer (line 26417): "const finalDmg=baseDmg*...*(_critInfo.crit?(_critInfo.mul/2.0):1.0);" with baseDmg=isHead?W.hsDmg:W.dmg.
fix: Make _isCritHit return multipliers relative to the actual baseDmg, OR fix the consumer at line 26417 to not divide body crits by 2. Surgical option in-scope: add an explicit field to the return, e.g. NECK -> {crit:true,type:'NECK',baseMul:2.0} and have the consumer use (isHead?(_critInfo.mul/2.0):_critInfo.mul). Simplest consumer fix at line 26417: replace the trailing factor with (_critInfo.crit?(isHead?_critInfo.mul/2.0:_critInfo.mul):1.0). This restores NECK=2x body and SPINE=1.7x body as the comments intend.
risk: Increases body-crit damage; could shift TTK/balance for neck/back hits. Low save-compat risk. Verify shotgun (idx 3) per-pellet does not over-amplify since each pellet recomputes crit.

title: comboKill wrapper drops the opts arg (source/closeRange), starving the story-combat feel system
description: Every kill site calls comboKill(isHead, {source, closeRange}) (e.g. lines 14490, 20165, 21433, 25239, 26451, 26557, 27664). The wrapper at 32458 is `function(isHead){ _origComboKill(isHead); ... }` — it never forwards the second argument. The real comboKill (36004) feeds opts.source and opts.closeRange into applyStoryCombatReward; with the wrapper in place those are always undefined, so applyStoryCombatReward receives source:'combo-kill' and closeRange:0 for EVERY kill regardless of weapon/range. This silently neuters the per-kill momentum/feel differentiation that the recent feel work added.
evidence: 32458 `comboKill=function(isHead){` and 32459 `_origComboKill(isHead);` (no opts), versus the definition 35985 `function comboKill(isHead,opts={})` and 36004 `applyStoryCombatReward(P,{source:(opts&&opts.source)||'combo-kill',killed:true,isHead,combo:P.combo.count,closeRange:(opts&&opts.closeRange)||0});`
fix: Delete the entire wrapper (32457-32463) — it is redundant once the double-milestone is removed and the original already handles milestones. If the wrapper must stay for some reason, change it to `comboKill=function(isHead,opts){ _origComboKill(isHead,opts); }` so opts is forwarded.
risk: Very low. Deleting the wrapper restores the original two-arg behavior. Confirm no other override of comboKill exists (only this one found).

title: Death cam freezes (no camera motion) when player dies with no alive enemy nearby
description: startDeathCam picks the nearest ALIVE enemy as the camera target. If none is alive (died to own grenade, environmental damage, or a bullet still in flight after the last enemy died), `best` stays null and DEATHCAM.killerPos is never set. updateDeathCam returns immediately every frame because of `if(!DEATHCAM.active||!DEATHCAM.killerPos)return;` (line 37111), so the camera just sits frozen at the moment of death for the full 1.7s before the defeat screen — reads as a hard freeze / broken death, not a cinematic. Secondarily, startDeathCam never resets DEATHCAM.killerPos to null first, so a stale killerPos from a previous death can leak into a later death where no enemy is found, aiming the cam at a wrong/old world position.
evidence:
let best=null,bestD=999; ... if(best){DEATHCAM.killerPos=best.group.position.clone(); ...}  // killerPos left as-is (null or stale) when best is null
function updateDeathCam(dt){ if(!DEATHCAM.active||!DEATHCAM.killerPos)return; ...
fix: At the top of startDeathCam set `DEATHCAM.killerPos=null;`. Then after the search, add a fallback when best is null: `if(!DEATHCAM.killerPos){const f=-Math.sin(P.yaw),fz=-Math.cos(P.yaw);DEATHCAM.killerPos=new THREE.Vector3(P.pos.x+f*2.2,WT,P.pos.z+fz*2.2);DEATHCAM.distance=2.2;}` so the cam always has a target (pulls back to a generic over-the-shoulder of the corpse) and never freezes.
risk: Purely additive; only changes behavior in the previously-broken no-enemy case. No save-compat impact.

title: Locomotion-feel camera wall-kick (wallKickPitch/wallKickRoll) is computed every frame then discarded
description: The locomotion feel layer writes addv.camera.wallKickPitch (line 344) and addv.camera.wallKickRoll (line 345). applyLocomotionFeelToPlayerAnim (line 419) adds these into playerAnimation.resolved.camera.wallKickPitch / .wallKickRoll via add(). But the camera assembly in main.js (line 42953 for pitch, line 42960 for roll) only reads _pa0.headPitch / _pa0.headRoll and never reads _pa0.wallKickPitch / _pa0.wallKickRoll. resolvePlayerAnimLayers folds the BASE wall-kick into headPitch/headRoll (playerAnimation.js lines 960 and 964) BEFORE the feel additive is applied, so the feel-layer's dedicated wallKickPitch/Roll contribution (scaled by wallKickWeight 1.18 and cameraWeight 1.10) lands in resolved.camera.wallKickPitch/Roll where nothing consumes it. The viewmodel equivalents (_pv.wallKickPitch/Roll, lines 372-376) ARE read in main.js (lines 43551-43552), so the asymmetry is clearly unintended. The feel layer also adds to headPitch (-s.wallKick*0.050, line 333) and headRoll (+s.wallKick*s.wallSide*0.056, line 334) which DO land, so wall-jump is not broken — but roughly the larger half of the intended feel-layer camera punch (pitch 0.060, roll 0.080) is silently lost.
evidence: locomotionFeelController.js: addv.camera.wallKickPitch = -s.wallKick * 0.060; addv.camera.wallKickRoll = s.wallKick * s.wallSide * 0.080;  | main.js camera.rotation.x assembly (line 42953) reads _pa0.headPitch ... but no _pa0.wallKickPitch; grep '_pa0.wallKickPitch' = 0 reads, while every other addv.camera key (footstepDip, dropkickPitch, slideRoll, gaitPitch, impactSettlePitch, etc.) has >=1 direct read.
fix: Either (a) in main.js camera assembly add `+(_pa0.wallKickPitch||0)` to camera.rotation.x (line 42953) and `+(_pa0.wallKickRoll||0)` to camera.rotation.y/z roll term (line 42960), mirroring the viewmodel path; or (b) in locomotionFeelController.js redirect the feel wall-kick into the consumed channels by folding line 344/345 amounts into addv.camera.headPitch / addv.camera.headRoll instead of separate wallKickPitch/Roll keys. Option (a) is the most faithful (restores the dedicated wall-kick camera punch); option (b) is lower-risk (no new camera read). Keep magnitudes as-is to avoid over-kicking.
risk: Option (a) adds a real camera pitch/roll punch on wall-jumps (~3-4.5deg) that players were not previously getting — visually a clear improvement but verify it does not exceed comfort under ADS (the viewmodel path already gates with P.adsVis<.92 at line 43546; consider a similar ADS damp). No save-compat or perf concern. Keep player-animation-feel-smoke.mjs green (it does not assert wall-kick camera values).

title: _attackBreakPulse/_weaponBreakPulse/_coverBreakPulse are decayed twice per frame (combatFeedback AND gunplayPolish both own them)
description: These three break-feedback pulses appear in the DECAY table of BOTH combatFeedback.js (lines 34-36, lambdas 6.4/5.8/5.4) and gunplayPolish.js (lines 44-46, identical lambdas). In the frame loop, tickPlayerCombatFeedback(P,dt) (main.js:41667) and tickGunplayPolish(P,dt) (main.js:41670) both run unconditionally and consecutively on the same P every frame. Each applies current*exp(-lambda*dt), so the pulse is multiplied by exp(-lambda*dt) twice => effective decay is ~2x too fast (at 60fps the per-frame survival drops from ~0.90 to ~0.82). gunplayPolish.recordGunplayOutcome is the sole writer (lines 1177-1179); both modules READ these pulses (combatFeedback snapshot attackBreak/weaponBreak/coverBreak at 123-125; gunplayPolish uses them in hudAlpha/recoilReturnBoost/xhairTighten). The shortened pulse is visible: _syncCombatFeedbackHud (main.js:22650) drives the CSS var --combat-attack-break and the combat-attack-break body class (22655) from attackBreakPulse/weaponBreakPulse, so the 'you broke their stance/weapon/cover' crosshair ring pop is cut to roughly half its intended on-screen duration. This is the only cross-module decay-key collision in the entire scope (verified by extracting every DECAY key across all five tick modules).
evidence: combatFeedback DECAY: _attackBreakPulse: 6.4, _weaponBreakPulse: 5.8, _coverBreakPulse: 5.4 (lines 34-36). gunplayPolish DECAY: _attackBreakPulse: 8.4-context lines 44-46 with same 6.4/5.8/5.4. Frame loop: 41667 tickPlayerCombatFeedback(P,dt,damp); 41670 tickGunplayPolish(P,dt,damp);. damp = target+(current-target)*exp(-lambda*max(0,dt)) so target 0 => current*exp(-lambda*dt) applied twice.
fix: Remove the three keys '_attackBreakPulse', '_weaponBreakPulse', '_coverBreakPulse' from ONE module's DECAY table. Prefer removing them from combatFeedback.js DECAY (lines 34-36) and keep them in gunplayPolish (which is the writer in recordGunplayOutcome). combatFeedback only reads them, so a single decayer in gunplayPolish restores the intended pulse lifetime. Do not change the lambdas. After the edit re-run the static probes to confirm green.
risk: Very low. Pure constant-table edit, no signature change, no save-compat impact. Slightly lengthens the break-feedback ring flash (back to intended); could feel marginally more persistent but that is the design intent. No other module decays these keys.

title: crate2: bottom crate's wall/vault AABB removed on break leaves the top crate floating; top break leaves bottom's collider orphaned
description: Only the BOTTOM box `a` owns linkedAABB/linkedVault (lines 1374-1375). When `a` breaks, _shatterMesh marks aabb.broken/vlEntry.broken so movement/AI/vault clear — but the TOP box `b` is never removed and is not linked to anything, so it floats in mid-air with no collider. Conversely the TOP box `b` has NO linkedAABB/linkedVault, so when `b` is destroyed (and, per the inverted-sibling bug, it also deletes `a`), the wall AABB and vault entry created for `a` are never marked broken — leaving an invisible solid collider + phantom vault prompt where both visible meshes are gone.
evidence: a.userData.linkedAABB = aabb; a.userData.linkedVault = vaultE;  (only on bottom box `a`)  …  const b = new THREE.Mesh(...); b.position.set(e.x + 0.1, WT + h*1.45, e.z - 0.05); … (no linkedAABB/linkedVault on `b`)
fix: Give each box its own AABB/vault entry: build a separate `aabbTop`/`vaultTop` for `b` and set b.userData.linkedAABB/linkedVault to them. Since the bottom is the only piece at floor/chest height, the simplest correct fix is to only register colliders for `a` AND make `b` non-blocking decoration (mark b.userData.noBlock) so it never needs its own collider — then the floating-top concern is purely visual. Pair this with removing the inverted linkedSibling.
risk: Adding a second AABB slightly increases wl/vl length (negligible). Changing b to noBlock would let players/AI clip the upper crate corner — acceptable since it sits above chest height. Keep nav-grid bake in mind; entries are processed in the same pass.

title: Environment-cohesion grade never reaches grouped signature props
description: _applyCoreEnvironmentCohesionPass() iterates `ob` with `if(!mesh||!mesh.isMesh||!mesh.material)continue;`. Every signature prop is built with `new THREE.Group()` and its child meshes are attached via `grp.add(...)`, while only the Group itself is pushed to `ob` (e.g. cargoContainer 3756, hangingChain 3786, marbleCol 3833, chand 3859, fountain fGrp 3983, gurney 4029, serverRack 4252, helm 4177, sofaY 4205). A Group is an Object3D, not a Mesh, so it is skipped — none of those child meshes receive the cohesion tint/roughness/specular/envMap polish that the flat shell and floor decals get. The marquee props (the most prominent objects on screen) are exactly the ones excluded from the versioned cohesion look, so they read as un-color-graded relative to the dressed room.
evidence: for(const mesh of ob){ if(!mesh||!mesh.isMesh||!mesh.material)continue; ... } — combined with `const grp=new THREE.Group();...scene.add(grp);ob.push(grp);` for every signature prop (only the group is in ob, never its meshes).
fix: In _applyCoreEnvironmentCohesionPass, recurse into groups: replace the flat loop with `for(const root of ob){ root.traverse(node=>{ if(!node.isMesh||!node.material)return; ... existing per-mesh body ... }); }`. Note classify() uses `mesh.position.y` which is LOCAL inside a group — switch to a world-position lookup (`node.getWorldPosition(_tmpVec)`) for the floor/decal height tests so grouped meshes classify correctly.
risk: Touching more materials per level; could shift the look of grouped props (intended). storeBase() guards against double-application so re-runs are safe. Keep the `coreVisualViewmodelPolish` skip. Verify build + probes stay green; this only mutates material params, no save/state shape.

title: Main HUD health bar width and color thresholds use raw HP, not HP/maxHp — bar overflows and mis-colors with the extraHp perk / health powerup
description: hudUpdate sets the HP fill as `width = round(P.hp) + '%'` and picks bar color from raw `h` (h>60 green / h>30 amber). #hp-fill is a percentage-width child of the fixed 180px #hp-bar. With the extraHp perk P.maxHp=125 (line 35952/31066) and the +50 health powerup pushes P.hp up to maxHp+50 (line 33075), so at full health the fill is width:125% and overflows the track, and the bar stays green until raw HP < 60 (=48% of max) instead of at a true fraction. The split-screen HUD does this correctly — hudUpdateSlot line 22524 uses min(100,(hp/maxHp)*100) and the co-op p1/p2 bars at 22598 do the same — so the single-player main bar is the inconsistent one.
evidence: const h=Math.max(0,Math.round(P.hp)); _hudSetText('hp-val',h); _hudSetStyle('hp-fill','width',h+'%'); _hudSetStyle('hp-fill','background',h>60?'#4cff88':h>30?'#ffcc44':'#ff4444');
fix: Mirror the split-HUD math: `const ratio=(P.hp||0)/Math.max(1,P.maxHp||100); const pct=Math.min(100,ratio*100); _hudSetText('hp-val',h); _hudSetStyle('hp-fill','width',pct.toFixed(1)+'%'); _hudSetStyle('hp-fill','background',ratio>.6?'#4cff88':ratio>.3?'#ffcc44':'#ff4444');` (keep the numeric readout as raw h).
risk: Low. Cosmetic-only; no save format change. Only behaviour change is the bar no longer overflowing and the color thresholds becoming fraction-based, which is the intended/standard behaviour and already used by the split HUD.

title: _resetKnifeRuntime leaks the stuck-knife pickup beacon (orphan VFX + GPU resources)
description: _resetKnifeRuntime removes each knife's k.grp from the scene and disposes k.grp geometry, but the stuck pickup beacon (k.beaconGrp) is parented to scene, NOT to k.grp (see _ensureKnifeStuckBeacon line 19602 `scene.add(g)`). The reset never calls _disposeKnifeBeacon, so a beacon for any knife that is stuck at reset time stays in the scene forever: a rotating additive ring/pulse/stem that keeps rendering at the last stuck position with no owner, and its geometry+materials are never freed. This fires on level transitions / retries / custom-map reloads while a thrown knife is stuck in a wall.
evidence: function _resetKnifeRuntime(){ ... for(const k of G.knives){ if(k&&k.grp){ scene.remove(k.grp); try{k.grp.traverse(o=>{if(o.geometry)o.geometry.dispose();});}catch(_){} } } G.knives.length=0; ...} — no _disposeKnifeBeacon(k) call; beacon is on scene not k.grp.
fix: In _resetKnifeRuntime, inside the `for(const k of G.knives)` loop, call `_disposeKnifeBeacon(k);` before/after scene.remove(k.grp). _disposeKnifeBeacon (line 19577) already removes from parent and disposes geometry+material, so one line fixes both the orphan VFX and the leak.
risk: Extremely low. _disposeKnifeBeacon is null-safe (early-returns if no beaconGrp) and is already called from _startKnifeReturn/_collectStuckKnife, so behavior is identical to the normal collect path. No save-compat or perf concern.

title: tickProjectiles fires triggerHitStop for any owner, but hitstop only affects player slot 0 (P)
description: triggerHitStop (def 33827) writes only to P._hitStop* (slot 0). In tickProjectiles the enemy-hit and kill branches call triggerHitStop unconditionally regardless of p.ownerSlot. In split-screen/duel, a projectile fired by P2 (ownerSlot 1) causes a global hitstop freeze on P1's camera/feel. triggerPlayerHitImpactFeedback is correctly slot-aware here, so this is an inconsistency within the same hit handler.
evidence: Lines: "if((isHead||dmg>120)&&typeof triggerHitStop==='function')triggerHitStop(isHead?44:34);" and on kill "if(typeof triggerHitStop==='function')triggerHitStop(isHead?46:36);" — no ownerSlot guard. Compare triggerHitStop: "P._hitStopUntil=performance.now()+dur;" (slot-0 only).
fix: Guard both triggerHitStop calls with (p.ownerSlot|0)===0, e.g. "if((p.ownerSlot|0)===0 && (isHead||dmg>120))triggerHitStop(...)". Same pattern already used implicitly by single-screen shoot(). Long term, parameterize triggerHitStop by slot.
risk: Behavior change only in split-screen/duel; single-player unaffected (ownerSlot always 0). No save-compat impact.

title: autoFocus perk focus regen applied multiple times (tickFocus wrapper duplicates work the original already does)
description: applyPerks2 sets P._focusRegen=1.35 when autoFocus is owned. The tickFocus wrapper (31091) adds an EXTRA regen of dt*.18*(P._focusRegen-1) when P._focusRegen>1, then calls _origTickFocus. But the original tickFocus (26982-26983) already multiplies regen by regenMul=(P._focusRegen||1)*(hasPerk('autoFocus')?1.25:1.0). So with autoFocus the focus bar regenerates from three stacked sources: the wrapper's extra term, the _focusRegen multiplier inside the original, and the additional 1.25 hasPerk multiplier inside the original. Focus fills far faster than the perk description implies.
evidence: wrapper 31093-31095: `if(P._focusRegen&&P._focusRegen>1.0&&!P.focusActive){ P.focus=Math.min(1,P.focus+dt*.18*(P._focusRegen-1)); }` then 31096 `_origTickFocus(dt);` — original 26982 `const regenMul=(P._focusRegen||1.0)*(hasPerk('autoFocus')?1.25:1.0);` 26983 `P.focus=Math.min(1,P.focus+dt*FOCUS_FEEL.regen*regenMul);`
fix: Delete the extra regen block in the wrapper (31092-31095) so only the original applies the multiplier; the wrapper then just forwards. Better: drop the wrapper at 31090-31097 entirely and rely on the original's regenMul (which already reads P._focusRegen and hasPerk('autoFocus')). Also reconcile the redundant double-count: the original multiplies by BOTH P._focusRegen (1.35) AND hasPerk('autoFocus') 1.25 — pick one source of truth.
risk: Low. Removing the wrapper slows autoFocus regen to the intended single-multiplier rate; only affects players who own the autoFocus perk.

title: Last Stand stores previous weapon but never restores it on revive — player stuck on pistol
description: When the player enters Last Stand, takeDamage saves the outgoing weapon (`const prev=pl.weaponIdx;pl._lastStandPrevWeapon=prev;` line 37200) and force-switches to the pistol via switchWeapon(1). tickLastStand reviving the player (line 37219-37224) sets hp=25 and _inLastStand=false but NEVER reads _lastStandPrevWeapon — so the player is permanently demoted to the pistol after surviving a Last Stand, even if they were carrying a rifle/shotgun. _lastStandPrevWeapon is a dead write (grep confirms it is written only at 37200 and read nowhere).
evidence: const prev=pl.weaponIdx;pl._lastStandPrevWeapon=prev; switchWeapon(1);  // revive path: P._inLastStand=false;P.hp=25; ... // never: switchWeapon(P._lastStandPrevWeapon)
fix: In tickLastStand's revive branch (right after `P.hp=25;`, line 37222) add: `if(typeof P._lastStandPrevWeapon==='number'&&P._lastStandPrevWeapon!==P.weaponIdx)switchWeapon(P._lastStandPrevWeapon,true);P._lastStandPrevWeapon=undefined;`. Guard with isPlayableWeaponIdx if you want to be defensive about a since-dropped weapon.
risk: Low. switchWeapon already normalizes idx and no-ops if dead/melee-out. Restoring at revive (player alive again) is safe. Keep the force=true so the swap actually plays.

title: Wrist-armband holo HP bar divides by hardcoded 100, ignoring P.maxHp (extraHp perk -> bar under-reports damage)
description: In _drawArmBandCanvas (the live first-person wrist-armband holographic HUD), HP fill is computed as hpRatio=clamp((P.hp||0)/100,0,1) and the bar color thresholds key off that same /100 ratio, while the numeric readout prints Math.round(P.hp). But applyPerks sets P.maxHp=125 when the 'extraHp' (Hard Target, +25 max HP) perk is owned (main.js:35952), and several other systems correctly divide by (P.maxHp||100) (e.g. main.js:21992, 30008, 22598). With the perk active: at full 125 HP the bar shows hpRatio=1.25 clamped to full while the printed number is 125 (mismatch between a 'full' 100-scale bar and a 125 number); as the player drops to 100/125 the bar still reads 100% green even though the operator is at 80% of max, so the armband visually under-reports damage and mis-colors the danger threshold. This is a SECOND, distinct location from the main-HUD maxHp bug the execution-region agent reported (main-hpbar-ignores-maxhp) — that one is the #hp DOM bar; this is the 3D armband canvas render path, an independent code site with the same root cause.
evidence: const hpRatio=Math.max(0,Math.min(1,(P.hp||0)/100));\n  ...\n  _drawHoloMetricBar(g,36,46,c.width-48,11,hpRatio,hpRatio>.6?'#5fff90':hpRatio>.3?'#ffd060':'#ff5048','HP',String(Math.round(P.hp||0)));
fix: Replace the hardcoded 100 with the player's max HP: const hpRatio=Math.max(0,Math.min(1,(P.hp||0)/Math.max(1,P.maxHp||100)));  This mirrors the AMMO line directly below it (which already divides by Math.max(1,W.mag||1)) and the other correct HP-ratio sites. One-line change, no save/perf impact.
risk: Trivial. Only affects the armband canvas fill ratio/color; the printed number is unchanged. No behavior change for the default 100-HP case (100/100 == 1.0).

title: Drone fire/up/down buttons never clear on pointercancel — drone can fire or climb forever
description: fire-btn, up-btn and down-btn set state.sticks.fireHeld / state.sticks.ascend on 'pointerdown' and only clear them on their own 'pointerup'. There is no 'pointercancel' (or pointerleave/blur/visibilitychange) handler, and no setPointerCapture. On touch devices a pointercancel (system gesture, scroll, OS interruption, app backgrounding) fires no pointerup, so fireHeld stays true / ascend stays ±1. The 34ms DRONE_INPUT loop (client.js:788-795) then keeps streaming {fireHeld:true,ascend:1} to the host, and host tickCompanionDrone (main.js:22216 `if(d.input.fireHeld)companionDroneFire();`) keeps firing every frame until the next button interaction. Note installStick() (client.js:681-682) correctly handles BOTH pointerup and pointercancel — these three buttons were missed.
evidence: client.js:745-749 `el('fire-btn').addEventListener('pointerdown',()=>{state.sticks.fireHeld=true;send(DRONE_FIRE,{held:true});}); el('fire-btn').addEventListener('pointerup',()=>{state.sticks.fireHeld=false;});` — no pointercancel. Same pattern for up-btn (750-751) and down-btn (752-753). Compare installStick which does both: client.js:681 `pad.addEventListener('pointerup', reset)` and 682 `pad.addEventListener('pointercancel', reset)`.
fix: For fire-btn add `el('fire-btn').addEventListener('pointercancel',()=>{state.sticks.fireHeld=false;});` and likewise add pointercancel handlers to up-btn and down-btn that set ascend=0. Optionally also reset all three on window 'blur'/'visibilitychange' (document.hidden) to clear held state when the companion tab loses focus. Cheap, isolated to the companion client.
risk: Very low. Adds release handlers only; no change to host or game logic. Companion is an optional secondary-device feature so blast radius is small.

title: Custom-map zone doors advance their open animation twice per frame (double dt)
description: The main loop ticks zone doors once at main.js:43947 (`G.levelData.tickZoneDoors(dt)`) and then ticks dyn props at main.js:43950 (`G.levelData.tickDynProps(dt,now)`). For custom maps, the compiler's `tickDynProps` ALSO calls `tickZoneDoors(dt)` internally (line 985). So `tickZoneDoors` runs twice per frame, applying the lerp `door.currentLift += delta * Math.min(1, dt*3.2)` two times — zone gates slide open at roughly double speed. Neither the procedural campaign level nor the B01 level's tickDynProps calls tickZoneDoors internally (they rely on the single main-loop call), so this redundancy is unique to the custom-map compiler and is an inconsistency with the rest of the engine.
evidence: compiler tickDynProps: `function tickDynProps(dt){ tickZoneDoors(dt); tickOpenableDoors(dt); ... }` while main.js loop already calls `if(G.levelData&&G.levelData.tickZoneDoors)G.levelData.tickZoneDoors(dt);` (43947) before `if(G.levelData&&G.levelData.tickDynProps)G.levelData.tickDynProps(dt,now);` (43950).
fix: Remove the redundant `tickZoneDoors(dt);` call from the compiler's tickDynProps (line 985), keeping `tickOpenableDoors(dt);` (which the main loop does NOT call separately). This matches the campaign/B01 contract where the main loop owns the zone-door tick.
risk: Low. tickOpenableDoors stays inside tickDynProps so openable doors are unaffected. Zone-door open animation simply runs at the intended single rate. No save-compat impact.

title: normalizeMarkers drops playerSpawn defaults (id/yaw/floorY) for partial input
description: `normalizeMarkers` does `const out = Object.assign(base, cloneJson(markers));` which overwrites `base.playerSpawn` with the input's (possibly partial) playerSpawn. It then does `out.playerSpawn = Object.assign(base.playerSpawn, markers.playerSpawn || {})` — but `base.playerSpawn` has ALREADY been replaced by the cloned input on the previous line, so the default fields are gone before the merge. For a pack with a partial playerSpawn (e.g. hand-authored or migrated JSON with just {x,z}), the result is exactly {x,z} with no id, yaw, or floorY. Verified empirically: `normalizeMarkers({playerSpawn:{x:5,z:10}})` returns `{x:5,z:10}` instead of merging the defaults `{id:'player_spawn',yaw:PI,floorY:0.4}`. The runtime compiler's repairPlayerSpawn masks yaw/floorY loss (defaults yaw=PI, floorY=map.floorY), but a deliberately-authored yaw=0 spawn would still be lost, and the id is dropped.
evidence: Lines 162-164: `const out = Object.assign(base, cloneJson(markers)); out.playerSpawn = Object.assign(base.playerSpawn, markers.playerSpawn || {});`. Empirical: normalizeMarkers({playerSpawn:{x:5,z:10}}) -> {"x":5,"z":10}.
fix: Merge defaults UNDER the input: `out.playerSpawn = Object.assign({}, defaultMarkers().playerSpawn, markers.playerSpawn || {});` (capture the fresh default spawn before the spread mutates base). This preserves id/yaw/floorY for partial spawns.
risk: Low. Only fills in missing default fields; full spawns (the editor always writes full spawns) are unchanged. No localStorage shape change.

title: encounterAlertLink and encounterPreferredState are written from authored data but never read anywhere — authored squad alert-coordination and preferred-state are dead
description: applyEncounterEnemySpec copies s.alertLink -> enemy.encounterAlertLink and s.preferredState -> enemy.encounterPreferredState (and applyEncounterRole sets encounterPreferredState='HOLD_CORNER' for 'anchor'). The B01 catalog authors alertLink on most enemies (e.g. b01_scout_fe_lane->['b01_fc_doorline'], b01_me_lane->['b01_mw_desk'], b01_bw_hold->['b01_bc_heavy','b01_bc_rifle']) and preferredState:'HOLD_CORNER' on anchors. A grep of main.js (and all src) shows NEITHER field is ever read. So authored alert propagation (one enemy waking its linked teammates) and authored preferred states do not happen — the cross-enemy 'coordinated reveal' the data implies is absent.
evidence: encounterBehavior.js:55 `if (Array.isArray(s.alertLink)) enemy.encounterAlertLink = s.alertLink.slice();` and :54 `enemy.encounterPreferredState = s.preferredState || null;`. `grep -rn 'encounterAlertLink|encounterPreferredState' src` returns ONLY encounterBehavior.js. campaignEncounters.js authors alertLink at lines 373,453,478 and preferredState:'HOLD_CORNER' at 421,489.
fix: If alert links are desired (cheap AAA feel — coordinated room wake): in main.js where an enemy first acquires the player / sets lastKnownPos, look up enemy.encounterAlertLink, resolve teammates by encounterSpecId in enemyMgr._list, and seed their lastKnownPos/alertTimer. For preferredState, in the AI state machine bias toward HOLD_CORNER (state 6) when enemy.encounterPreferredState==='HOLD_CORNER' and a threat is alive. If neither is wanted, delete the two writes to remove the misleading authoring surface.
risk: Wiring alert propagation changes encounter difficulty (rooms can wake as a unit). Make it opt-in and bounded (radius/once). Additive; no save-compat impact.

title: Boss-spawned adds mis-tagged to zone 2 when boss is in zone 0 (`||` swallows zoneId 0)
description: In EnemyManager._runBossPhase addSpawn, the spawn-clearance opts use the correct `Number.isFinite(boss.zoneId)?boss.zoneId:2` (line 12758), but the very next line tags the new enemy with `newE.zoneId=boss.zoneId||2`. Because `0||2===2`, a boss whose zoneId is 0 (front zone) produces adds tagged zoneId 2 (back). Those adds are then counted in the wrong zone by per-zone systems (squad grouping, awareness radius gating uses zoneId, encounter/cover slot zone filters), and the room-clear gate becomes inconsistent with where the enemies physically are.
evidence:
line 12758: zoneId:Number.isFinite(boss.zoneId)?boss.zoneId:2  // correct
line 12763: newE.zoneId=boss.zoneId||2;  // wrong: zoneId 0 -> 2
fix: Change line 12763 to `newE.zoneId=Number.isFinite(boss.zoneId)?boss.zoneId:2;` (mirror the opts on line 12758). Surgical one-token change, no save-compat impact.
risk: None to save format. Only affects which zone freshly boss-spawned adds are accounted to; corrects a desync. Bosses are usually placed in zone 2 so today the bug is latent, but it activates for any zone-0/zone-1 boss encounter.

title: loadProfileSlot does Object.assign(PROGRESS, partial) — would clobber PROGRESS with a partial shape (violates save-merge rule); whole profile-slot system is dead
description: loadProfileSlot(slot) does `Object.assign(PROGRESS, JSON.parse(raw))`, merging a stored slot directly onto the live PROGRESS object WITHOUT merging against defaults first. Per the project save-compatibility rule, persisted shapes must always be merged against defaults, never overwritten with a partial shape — and a slot saved by an older build (missing newer keys) would leave PROGRESS partially undefined after load. This is a latent save-corruption bug. It is currently masked because loadProfileSlot/saveProfileSlot/listProfileSlots all have ZERO callers (grep confirms) — the multi-profile feature is entirely unwired.
evidence: if(raw)Object.assign(PROGRESS,JSON.parse(raw)); // grep loadProfileSlot/saveProfileSlot/listProfileSlots => defs only, no callers
fix: If the feature ships, route loads through the same defaults-merge used for clearance_progress (deep-merge JSON.parse(raw) onto a fresh defaults clone, then assign) rather than Object.assign onto live PROGRESS. If not shipping, delete loadProfileSlot/saveProfileSlot/listProfileSlots (29817-29837) to remove the footgun.
risk: Save-compat: a naive merge could resurrect deleted keys; mirror the existing clearance_progress merge helper exactly. Deletion is zero-risk.

title: Level/mode transitions remove trail meshes from scene but never dispose their geometry/material (GPU leak on every building advance)
description: Multiple transition paths run `G.trails.forEach(t=>{if(t.line)scene.remove(t.line);if(t.mesh)scene.remove(t.mesh);});G.trails=[]` — they detach meshes from the scene graph but never call geometry.dispose()/material.dispose(). A proper helper, _disposeTrail(t) (40536), already exists and is used by the per-frame expiry loop (44274) and budget enforcer (40556). The most-traveled path is the building-advance handler at 35383, so this leaks every time the player clears a building (up to ~240 trail entries each with a PlaneGeometry/material, plus extra mats and atlas maps). Over a full 12-building campaign this accumulates orphaned GPU resources.
evidence: L35383 (advanceBuilding path): G.trails.forEach(t=>{if(t.line)scene.remove(t.line);if(t.mesh)scene.remove(t.mesh);}); — compare L44274 which uses _disposeTrail(t), and L40536 _disposeTrail which calls geometry.dispose()/material.dispose()/map.dispose().
fix: Replace each `G.trails.forEach(t=>{...scene.remove...})` cleanup with `for(let i=G.trails.length-1;i>=0;i--)_disposeTrail(G.trails[i]); G.trails.length=0;` (or `G.trails.forEach(_disposeTrail)` then reset). All 6-7 sites listed should route through _disposeTrail so geometry/material/atlas maps are freed.
risk: Low. _disposeTrail already handles line/mesh/extra/extraMats/atlas map. Only behavior change is freeing GPU memory that is otherwise dropped. No gameplay or save impact.

title: spawnDroppedMag leaks two BoxGeometries every reload (Group pushed as t.mesh, child geometries never disposed)
description: spawnDroppedMag builds a THREE.Group containing two child meshes (body, lip) and pushes `{mesh:grp,mat:magM,...,extraMats:[lipM]}` into G.trails. When the trail expires, _disposeTrail (line 40536) disposes t.mesh.geometry — but t.mesh is a Group, which has NO geometry, so neither the body BoxGeometry nor the lip BoxGeometry is ever disposed. Materials are handled (magM via t.mat at 40543, lipM via t.extraMats at 40541), so only geometries leak. Contrast addShell (line 24307) which pushes a single Mesh as t.mesh, so its geometry IS disposed. Every partial-mag reload leaks 2 BoxGeometries; over a long session this accumulates GPU buffers.
evidence: spawnDroppedMag: `const grp=new THREE.Group(); ... const body=new THREE.Mesh(new THREE.BoxGeometry(...),magM);grp.add(body); const lip=new THREE.Mesh(new THREE.BoxGeometry(...),lipM); ... G.trails.push({mesh:grp,mat:magM,vel,spin:...,timer:3.0,maxTime:3.0,isDroppedMag:true,extraMats:[lipM]});`. _disposeTrail: `if(t.mesh){scene.remove(t.mesh);if(t.mesh.geometry)t.mesh.geometry.dispose();...}` — grp.geometry is undefined.
fix: Either dispose child geometries in _disposeTrail for grouped trails (`if(t.mesh){scene.remove(t.mesh);t.mesh.traverse&&t.mesh.traverse(o=>{if(o.geometry)o.geometry.dispose();});...}`), or in spawnDroppedMag attach a disposer/flag so the trail loop traverses the group. Cleanest surgical fix: in _disposeTrail, replace the single geometry dispose with a traverse when t.mesh has children, e.g. `if(t.mesh){scene.remove(t.mesh);if(t.mesh.geometry)t.mesh.geometry.dispose();else if(t.mesh.traverse)t.mesh.traverse(o=>{if(o.geometry)o.geometry.dispose();});...}`.
risk: Very low; traverse-dispose is a no-op for non-group meshes. Verify no other code re-uses the disposed geometries (these are freshly created per mag, so safe).

title: Riot charge and shielded body-block move the enemy, then the ATTACK switch-case moves it AGAIN the same frame
description: The archetype pre-state hooks (lines 11337-11407) run BEFORE the `switch(this.state)` at 11422 and there is no break/return between them. For a riot in ATTACK within 6m, line 11341 issues a sprint rush via _moveWithVelocity; the code then falls through into `case ATTACK` which runs the default circular-strafe _moveWithVelocity at 11673 (and _maybeReposition/juke). Two competing velocity integrations per frame: the strafe overwrites/dilutes the committed melee rush, so the riot wobbles sideways instead of bull-rushing. Same double-move for shielded (body-block move at 11376 then ATTACK strafe). The drone swarm hook at 11404 has the same shape but drone has its own early-return ATTACK fire path so it is less affected.
fix: When the riot melee-charge (or shielded body-block) hook actually drives movement, set a flag and have the ATTACK case skip its strafe/juke movement block for that enemy this frame — e.g. set `this._archetypeMovedThisFrame=true` in the hook and guard the ATTACK 'else' strafe branch (line 11658-11677) with `&& !this._archetypeMovedThisFrame`. Reset the flag at top of update(). Keeps shooting logic intact; only suppresses the conflicting second move.
risk: Riot will commit harder to the charge (intended, more threatening). Verify riot still fires while charging (the ATTACK fire block after the move stays reachable). Low risk to other archetypes since the guard only trips when a hook moved the enemy.

title: Enemy-thrown (demolitions) grenades route through explodeGrenade and friendly-fire other enemies, awarding the player money/kills
description: spawnEnemyGrenade pushes a projectile with fromEnemy:true (thrown by 'demolitions' enemies, line 11694, aimed at the player's cover). updateGrenades detonates ALL non-smoke/non-flash grenades — including fromEnemy ones — through explodeGrenade(). explodeGrenade has no source check: it damages every enemy in radius and, on kill, calls awardKillMoney(e,false) + cinematicKill, plus self-damages the player. So an enemy frag that lands near other guards damages/kills them and silently pays the player money (and triggers a cinematic kill flash) for kills the player did not make.
evidence: } else { explodeGrenade(explosionPos); spawnExplosionFx(explosionPos); }  // reached for k.fromEnemy===true too; explodeGrenade loops all enemies and calls awardKillMoney(e,false) on any kill
fix: Either (a) pass the source into explodeGrenade and skip awardKillMoney/cinematicKill when fromEnemy (still allow damage if friendly-fire is intended), or (b) gate enemy-killed-by-enemy credit: in explodeGrenade add a `byPlayer` param defaulting true and only run awardKillMoney/cinematicKill when byPlayer; call `explodeGrenade(explosionPos,!k.fromEnemy)`. Simplest surgical change: in updateGrenades pass the flag and guard the award block.
risk: Low–medium. Must not change damage-to-player behaviour. If enemy-grenade enemy-on-enemy damage is intended, keep the damage and only suppress player credit. Verify demolitions encounter balance after the change.

title: Zone-door gate-id regex uses \\. (literal backslash) instead of \. so the float-formatted '.0' suffix never matches
description: In b01MegaplexZoneDoorIndexFor the two regex literals `/mega_zone_gate_22(?:\\.0)?_/` and `/mega_zone_gate_-22(?:\\.0)?_/` are clearly trying to optionally match a float-formatted coordinate '22.0'. Inside a regex literal, `\\.` is a LITERAL backslash followed by any-char, not an escaped dot. So the group `(?:\\.0)?` matches '\<anychar>0', never '.0'. A gate whose id is e.g. 'mega_zone_gate_22.0_left' will fail this test. The two other paths (explicit ud.zoneDoorIndex, and the closed_zone_gate positional z>=0 fallback) usually mask this, so it is a latent bug: a gate part that relies solely on the gateId pattern (no zoneDoorIndex, floorplanRole != 'closed_zone_gate') will return null and not be registered as a lift door, so it would not animate open / would not become a navigable opening.
evidence:
if(/mega_zone_gate_22(?:\\.0)?_/.test(gateId))return 0;
    if(/mega_zone_gate_-22(?:\\.0)?_/.test(gateId))return 1;
fix: Replace `\\.` with `\.`: `/mega_zone_gate_22(?:\.0)?_/` and `/mega_zone_gate_-22(?:\.0)?_/`. (Single backslash-dot to match a literal period.)
risk: Could newly match gate ids that previously fell through to the positional fallback; behavior should be equivalent or more correct. Verify gate ids actually contain '22.0' formatting; if they only ever use integer '22' the optional group is simply moot and the fix is harmless.

title: Resuming a saved coop (or non-custom) run silently loads it as solo
description: saveRunState() faithfully records `mode:G.playMode||'solo'` (35846). The main loop's exit-zone check (44361) calls advanceBuilding() in ANY building-progression mode whose exit is unlocked, and coop is a campaign mode (see damagePlayer coop branch at 37188). advanceBuilding() calls saveRunState() (37061), so a coop run can persist runSave.mode='coop'. But resumeRunState() only special-cases `r.mode==='custom'` (35869); every other value (coop, demo, anything future) falls through to the campaign path (35878) which restores state into the solo P only and calls startBuilding() in whatever G.playMode happens to be set at the time (often 'solo' from the prior menu). The Continue button (refreshMenuContinue 38922) labels it 'CONTINUE · BLDG N' giving no hint it was coop. Net: a coop save resumes as solo, dropping P2 entirely with no warning.
evidence:
saveRunState: mode:G.playMode||'solo'  (35846)
resumeRunState: if(r.mode==='custom'){...return true;}  // only custom handled (35869)
G.building=r.building;... (campaign fallthrough, 35878) — never re-establishes coop/split-screen
fix: Either (a) refuse to persist a resumable run for non-resumable modes — in saveRunState guard early `if(G.playMode!=='solo'&&G.playMode!=='custom')return;` so coop/duel/demo never write runSave; or (b) handle r.mode==='coop' explicitly in resumeRunState by re-entering the coop start path. Option (a) is the surgical, low-risk choice and matches that coop has no resume UI.
risk: Low. Option (a) only narrows what gets written to localStorage; existing solo/custom saves unaffected and still merge against defaults. Verify endless/range/duel never reached saveRunState (they don't go through advanceBuilding's solo branch, but coop does).

title: B02/B03 boss reveal cues omit tone/duration args, rendering with tone='story' (3300ms) instead of 'boss' (3800ms)
description: The boss cues for B01 (line 75) and the campaignCuePack default (line 40) pass tone='boss', durationMs=3800. But B02 (line 107) and B03 (line 139) call cue('boss','TARGET LINE', title, body) with no tone/duration, so they default to tone='story' and durationMs=3300. _renderStoryExperienceCue sets root.dataset.tone=cue.tone (main.js line 34361), which drives the boss-colored styling. So the dramatic boss-reveal banner on Continental Lobby and Club Obsidian is styled as a plain 'story' cue and shown for a shorter time than every other building's boss reveal — a visible inconsistency at the climax moment of two of the first three levels.
evidence: Line 75: `boss: cue('boss','TARGET LINE','Foreman Guard Exposed','...','boss',3800)`. Line 107: `boss: cue('boss','TARGET LINE','Manager Suite Exposed','The bagman is behind the guard line. Clear the suite.')` — no tone/duration. Line 139 same pattern for B03.
fix: Add `, 'boss', 3800` to the cue() calls at lines 107 and 139 to match B01 and the campaignCuePack default.
risk: Trivial. Pure data fix; matches existing buildings. No probe asserts these.

title: bench backrest placed at un-rotated -z offset, so rotated benches (rotY=π/2) have a detached/misplaced backrest
description: In `bench`, the seat mesh is positioned at (e.x,e.z) and rotated by e.rotY correctly. The backrest `bk` is positioned at bx=e.x, bz=e.z - d*0.5 + 0.05 (an offset along WORLD -z) and only THEN rotated in place (bk.rotation.y=e.rotY). For benches with rotY=π/2 the backrest should sit along the rotated -d axis (world -x), not world -z. Many benches use rotY:Math.PI/2 with back:true (lines 2237, 2247, 2430, 2431, 2675, 2713, 3146, 3147), so their backrests end up offset 90° from the seat and clip into adjacent space.
evidence: const bx = e.x, bz = e.z - d*0.5 + 0.05; bk.position.set(bx, WT + h + 0.35, bz); if (e.rotY) { bk.rotation.y = e.rotY; }
fix: Rotate the local backrest offset by e.rotY before applying: const c=Math.cos(e.rotY||0), s=Math.sin(e.rotY||0); const off=-d*0.5+0.05; bk.position.set(e.x + s*off, WT+h+0.35, e.z + c*off); bk.rotation.y = e.rotY||0; (matches the offset convention used elsewhere, e.g. tall stripes at line 676-678).
risk: Cosmetic prop placement only; no collider involvement (backrest is decoration, not pushed to wl). Low risk. Verify the rotY=0 benches still look identical (s=0,c=1 reduces to current offset).

title: Alarm setpiece shows the same 'Alarm Silenced' cue twice (silenced + reward paths reuse cset.silenced with different keys)
description: For the alarm setpiece (B01), when the player silences the relay and clears zone 1, SETPIECE._relaySilenced and SETPIECE.rewardGiven both become true. The 'silenced' branch (lines 422-426) enqueues cset.silenced with key `setpiece:1:alarm:silenced`; the 'rewardGiven' branch (lines 427-430) enqueues the SAME cset.silenced object with key `setpiece:1:alarm:reward`. Different keys defeat the seen-dedup, so the identical 'PRESSURE/RELAY SAFE — Alarm Silenced' banner displays twice back-to-back.
evidence: Line 425 `enqueueCue(s, cloneCue(cset && cset.silenced, {...}), `setpiece:${building}:${kind}:silenced`);` and line 429 `enqueueCue(s, cloneCue(cset && cset.silenced, {...}), `setpiece:${building}:${kind}:reward`);` — both reference cset.silenced.
fix: Either drop the reward-path enqueue (lines 427-430) since 'silenced' already covers the success message, or give the reward branch a distinct cue (e.g. a payout/clear cue) instead of reusing cset.silenced. Minimal: gate the reward enqueue with `if (!s.lastSetpieceSilenced)` so it only fires when silenced didn't already.
risk: Very low. Removes a redundant banner. No state-shape change.

title: _pulseCloseCombatFeedback writes P._knifeThrowImpactPulse for the 'knife_throw' branch, but nothing ever reads it — knife-throw hit feedback is computed and discarded
description: In _pulseCloseCombatFeedback, the kind==='knife_throw' branch is the only writer of P._knifeThrowImpactPulse (verified by grep across all of src/: exactly one reference, the write). Every sibling pulse (_knifeImpactPulse, _knifeStabPulse, _meleeWhipImpact) is read elsewhere to drive viewmodel/camera, but _knifeThrowImpactPulse is never sampled or decayed. The knife-throw close-impact pulse intended to kick the camera/viewmodel on a thrown-knife landing is effectively a no-op — the throw lands with no extra felt feedback even though the code thinks it applied some.
fix: Either (a) consume it: in the viewmodel/camera tick that already reads _knifeImpactPulse, add a small contribution from P._knifeThrowImpactPulse and decay it with damp(...,0,...,dt) like the others; or (b) if no throw-specific feel is wanted, delete the line and rely on the shakeX/shakeY/dmgPitch already applied above it. The shake/pitch still apply, so impact is low.
risk: Option (a) adds a new visible kick on thrown-knife hits (intended) — keep magnitude small to avoid over-shake. Option (b) is zero-risk cleanup. No save/build impact either way.

title: KeyF focus toggle has no e.repeat guard — holding F rapidly flip-flops focus mode on key auto-repeat
description: KeyF is overloaded: pickup (22398, returns), open door (22399, returns), and otherwise toggleFocus (22421). The focus branch lacks an `!e.repeat` guard, so holding F (when not near a pickup/door) fires keydown repeatedly and toggleFocus() flips P.focusActive on every auto-repeat event, strobing focus mode on/off. Other tap actions in the same handler that should fire once correctly guard with !e.repeat (e.g. Space jump 22393, dodge logic, KeyT takedown 22422). Focus is bound as the 'F' key in both the help legend (28621) and keymap (29611 focus:'KeyF'), confirming it's meant as a tap toggle.
evidence: if(e.code==='KeyF'&&!P.dead&&!G.menuOpen)toggleFocus();  // no `&&!e.repeat`
fix: Add the repeat guard: `if(e.code==='KeyF'&&!P.dead&&!G.menuOpen&&!e.repeat)toggleFocus();`
risk: Very low. Prevents an unintended strobe; no other code depends on repeat-firing toggleFocus.

title: Heavy-stab hit flash uses lifetime 0.30 but fade divisor is hardcoded 0.22 — opacity starts pinned >1
description: doMelee/checkMeleeHit sets MELEE.hitFlashTimer to 0.30 for heavy stabs and 0.22 for light (line 14476). In updateKnife the fade computes `f=Math.max(0,MELEE.hitFlashTimer/.22)` (line 14519) with a hardcoded .22 denominator. For a heavy stab f begins at 0.30/0.22 ≈ 1.36, so hf.style.opacity is set to the string '1.36...'. CSS clamps opacity to 1, so the flash visually holds at full opacity for the first ~0.08s of the heavy flash instead of starting its fade, making the heavy hit flash linger flat rather than easing out.
evidence:
14476: MELEE.hitFlashTimer=heavy?0.30:0.22;
14519: if(hf){const f=Math.max(0,MELEE.hitFlashTimer/.22);hf.style.opacity=String(f);}
fix: Store the flash duration when arming it (e.g. `MELEE.hitFlashDur=heavy?0.30:0.22;` at 14476) and divide by it in updateKnife: `const f=Math.max(0,MELEE.hitFlashTimer/(MELEE.hitFlashDur||.22));`. Or simply clamp/normalize with the heavy value. This restores a smooth ease-out for the heavy hit flash.
risk: Trivial; only changes the heavy hit-flash fade curve. Does not affect save data or probes.

title: Hit-FX throttle uses global P instead of the firing player pl (cross-player desync in P2/duel)
description: The blood/particle de-dupe throttle reads and writes P._suppressHitFxUntil, hardcoding player 1. But shoot() supports _slot===1 where the firing player is pl=P2. When P2 fires a body hit, it reads and stamps P1's _suppressHitFxUntil, so P2's hit-particle throttling is governed by P1's recent shots (and vice-versa). Everywhere else in the function the per-player object `pl` is used; this is the lone place that leaks to the global P.
evidence: `if(allowFx&&!(P._suppressHitFxUntil&&performance.now()<P._suppressHitFxUntil)){ addParticle(hitPt,isHead); if(isHead||killed||Math.random()<.35)addBlood(hitPt,isHead); if(!isHead&&!killed)P._suppressHitFxUntil=performance.now()+70; }` — uses P, not pl.
fix: Replace both `P._suppressHitFxUntil` references on lines 26440 and 26443 with `pl._suppressHitFxUntil`.
risk: Minimal. In single-player pl===P so behaviour is identical; only fixes split-screen/duel. No save-compat or perf concern.

title: Combo HUD fill divisor hardcoded to 4.8 but body-kill combo timer is 4.35 — bar never reads full
description: comboKill sets P.combo.timer to 4.8 for headshots but 4.35 for body kills (line 35988). comboTick computes the combo bar width as `P.combo.timer/4.8*100` unconditionally (line 36275). After a body-shot kill the bar maxes out at ~90.6% and visibly never fills to 100%, an inconsistency a player can notice on every non-headshot combo refresh.
evidence: P.combo.timer=isHead?4.8:4.35; ... fill.style.width=Math.max(0,P.combo.timer/4.8*100).toFixed(0)+'%';
fix: Track the window length on the combo object: in comboKill set `P.combo.window=isHead?4.8:4.35;` and in comboTick divide by `(P.combo.window||4.8)`. Alternatively normalize both timers to 4.8 if the shorter body-kill window is unintentional.
risk: Cosmetic only; no save/perf impact.

title: Editor material cache grows unbounded with route waypoint index keys
description: The editor's `material()` cache key incorporates the caller-supplied `key`, and route dots use `material(\`route-dot:${type}:${color}:${index}:...\`, ...)`. Because `index` is part of the cache key, each distinct waypoint index produces a new cached MeshStandardMaterial that is never disposed (disposeGroup only disposes geometry, not the shared matCache materials, and the cache is never cleared on openPack). For a session that edits long routes the matCache accumulates one material per (type,color,index,state) tuple. Bounded by the longest route ever rendered, so it is a slow leak, not a runaway one, but it is dead retained memory with no functional benefit (each route-dot material is otherwise identical to its siblings).
evidence: `material(\`route-dot:${type}:${color}:${index}:${selectedRoute ? 'selected' : 'idle'}\`, {...})` plus material() doing `matCache.set(cacheKey, mat)` with no eviction and disposeGroup only disposing geometry.
fix: Drop `${index}` from the route-dot cache key (line 1283) so all idle/selected dots of a given type+color share one material: `material(\`route-dot:${type}:${color}:${selectedRoute ? 'selected' : 'idle'}\`, ...)`. Optionally clear matCache in openPack.
risk: Very low. The internal material() cacheKey still differentiates by opacity/emissive/color, so visuals are unchanged.

title: Body-presence damp lambda selector reads raw P._bodyPresenceVis (undefined on first frame)
description: The `current` argument is guarded (`Number.isFinite(P._bodyPresenceVis)?P._bodyPresenceVis:0`), but the lambda-selection ternary reads `P._bodyPresenceVis` directly: `target>P._bodyPresenceVis?12:18`. On the very first frame P._bodyPresenceVis is undefined, so `target>undefined` evaluates to false and the slower lambda (18) is chosen even when the rig should be appearing (target rising). It self-corrects on frame 2. No crash, no NaN (the guarded current is used in the actual damp), just a one-frame-slower fade-in.
evidence: Line 17782: `P._bodyPresenceVis=damp(Number.isFinite(P._bodyPresenceVis)?P._bodyPresenceVis:0,target,target>P._bodyPresenceVis?12:18,dt);` — the lambda selector dereferences the unguarded global.
fix: Reuse the guarded current in the selector: `const cur=Number.isFinite(P._bodyPresenceVis)?P._bodyPresenceVis:0; P._bodyPresenceVis=damp(cur,target,target>cur?12:18,dt);`
risk: Trivial; deterministic improvement on the first visible frame only. No probe risk.

title: Operator-precedence bug builds an invalid fillStyle (evaluates to number 0) in _skylineTex window dots
description: In the original _skylineTex generator, the window-dot fillStyle is assembled as `'rgba('+r|0+','+gn|0+','+b|0+','+a+')'`. JS '+' binds tighter than '|', so this parses as a chain of string-concats bitwise-OR'd together, and the whole expression collapses to the NUMBER 0 (verified in node: it returns 0, not a string). Assigning g.fillStyle=0 is an invalid color so the canvas silently keeps the previous fillStyle, and the warm window dots are not drawn as intended. This is ONLY a latent bug: _skylineTex is dead code — grep shows it is never referenced; the live skyline is _skylineTexB / _skylineTexBExt / _skylinePerBuilding (line 1598), which correctly use template literals (lines 1387-1392). Hence visibleImpact=none.
fix: Either delete the dead _skylineTex IIFE (lines 876-918) entirely, or if kept, parenthesize: `g.fillStyle='rgba('+(r|0)+','+(gn|0)+','+(b|0)+','+a+')';`.
risk: None — texture is unused. Deletion is safest and removes a one-time canvas allocation at module load.

title: polishM MeshStandardMaterial built every level but only ever added for bn===1 ultra
description: `polishM` is constructed unconditionally inside addCinematicRealismLayer() for every building and quality, but is only attached to the scene/ob when `bn===1 && quality==='ultra'` (line 2536). In all other cases the material is created and immediately orphaned. It is a raw `new THREE.MeshStandardMaterial`, not an _aaMat cached material, and cleanup() only disposes materials reachable through `ob`. So on every non-(B1-ultra) level load a MeshStandardMaterial (with shader program once compiled if ever) is allocated and never disposed.
evidence: const polishM=stabilizeOverlayMaterial(new THREE.MeshStandardMaterial({...}),5); ... if(bn===1&&((SETTINGS&&SETTINGS.quality)==='ultra'))addFloorOverlay(0,0,RW*.86,RD*.86,polishM,0,WT+.034);
fix: Only build polishM inside the same guard that uses it: `let polishM=null; if(bn===1&&((SETTINGS&&SETTINGS.quality)==='ultra')){ polishM=stabilizeOverlayMaterial(new THREE.MeshStandardMaterial({...}),5); addFloorOverlay(0,0,RW*.86,RD*.86,polishM,0,WT+.034); }`.
risk: Trivial; pure construction-site move. No behavior change for B1-ultra. Build/probes unaffected.

title: visualStats.dressingObjects double-counts B1 pallets
description: Inside addAAVisualDressing the B1 pallet loop does `visualStats.dressingObjects+=9` (line 2642). At the end of the function `visualStats.dressingObjects+=ob.length-startCount` (line 2702) adds the total number of meshes pushed during the function — which already includes those 9 pallet meshes. So for bn===1 the dressingObjects telemetry is inflated by 9. Diagnostic-only (visualStats), no gameplay effect, but the number is wrong and could mislead any perf/density tuning that reads it.
evidence: line 2642: visualStats.dressingObjects+=9;   line 2702: visualStats.dressingObjects+=ob.length-startCount;
fix: Remove the redundant `visualStats.dressingObjects+=9;` on line 2642 (the catch-all at 2702 already counts those meshes), or zero startCount handling. Simplest: delete line 2642.
risk: None — pure stat correction. Verify no probe asserts an exact dressingObjects value for B1.

title: _spawnDropkickImpactFx creates a base slashMat that is cloned per slash but never used or disposed
description: slashMat is created with new THREE.MeshBasicMaterial(...) at 27498, then slashMat.clone() is used for each of the 3 slash planes. The cloned materials are tracked in G.trails (mat:slash.material) and get disposed by _disposeTrail, but the ORIGINAL slashMat is never assigned to a mesh nor pushed to G.trails, so it is an orphaned material allocated on every dropkick-impact spawn and never disposed. Same pattern in _spawnSlideSkidFx (base mat at 27723, mat.clone() per puff) and _spawnDropkickLandingFx (dustMat at 27553, dustMat.clone() per puff). These are GPU material leaks proportional to dropkick/slide frequency.
evidence: 27498: const slashMat=new THREE.MeshBasicMaterial({...}); 27500: const slash=new THREE.Mesh(...,slashMat.clone()); // slashMat itself never added/disposed. _disposeTrail only frees the per-trail t.mat.
fix: Either dispose the base after cloning (slashMat.dispose(); at the end of the slash loop / after the puff loop in each function), or build the material inline per element instead of clone(), or reuse a single cached module-level material. Lowest risk: add slashMat.dispose() after the for-loop in _spawnDropkickImpactFx (27509), dustMat.dispose() after the loop in _spawnDropkickLandingFx (27562), and mat.dispose() after the loop in _spawnSlideSkidFx (27736).
risk: Low. Disposing the base material is safe because each mesh uses an independent clone(); the base is not referenced by any live object. Verify no later code reads slashMat/dustMat/mat after the loop (it does not).

title: Debug snapshot reports G.wave (stuck at its init value 1) while the live counter is ENDLESS.wave
description: createGameState() initializes G.wave:1 / G.wavesTotal:2 / G.waveActive:false (src/game/state.js:72) as vestigial campaign-wave fields, and nothing in the runtime ever reassigns G.wave. The actual endless-mode wave counter is ENDLESS.wave (incremented at main.js:32953 and gating enemy-type unlocks at 32958-32964). The window.__game.debug snapshot at main.js:44959 reads `wave:G.wave`, so the debug/telemetry surface always reports a frozen 1 regardless of how deep the endless run is — it should read ENDLESS.wave (or G.building for campaign). Two parallel 'wave' truths exist (G.wave dead, ENDLESS.wave live) and the diagnostic reads the dead one. Low impact because it is debug-only, but it is a genuine competing-state desync that would mislead anyone reading the snapshot.
evidence: // debug snapshot:  wave:G.wave,   (G.wave is set to 1 once in createGameState and never updated)\n// live counter:    ENDLESS.wave+=1;  (main.js:32953)
fix: In the debug snapshot at main.js:44959 read the live source: `wave: (typeof ENDLESS!=='undefined'&&ENDLESS.active)?ENDLESS.wave:G.building`. If G.wave/G.wavesTotal/G.waveActive truly have no campaign consumer, consider dropping them from createGameState to remove the dead parallel state.
risk: Debug-only field; no gameplay or save impact. Verify ENDLESS is in scope at that line (it is a module global).

title: Muzzle flash decay uses wall-clock setTimeout (32-52ms), ignoring focus-mode timeScale and risking flicker overlap
description: _pulseMuzzleFlashForSlot (called from shoot() at line 26111) sets the muzzle light intensity then schedules `setTimeout(()=>{light.intensity=0;mat.opacity=0;},suppressedMul<.5?32:52)`. Two issues: (1) the flash decays in real wall-clock time, so during focus-mode bullet-time (P.timeScale down to ~0.125) the muzzle flash vanishes far too quickly relative to perceived game time, breaking the slow-mo gunfire fantasy. (2) Each shot schedules its own off-timer; if a future faster-firing/unsuppressed auto weapon fires below the 52ms interval, an earlier timer would zero the light mid-flash causing flicker. Current playable fire rates (M4 .10s, MP9 .075s suppressed→32ms) don't overlap today, so #2 is latent; #1 is the live, visible one in focus mode.
evidence: `light.intensity=(3.0+(Math.random()*1.0))*suppressedMul; mat.opacity=0.55*suppressedMul; ... setTimeout(()=>{light.intensity=0;mat.opacity=0;},suppressedMul<.5?32:52);`
fix: Drive the flash decay from the frame loop in game-time rather than setTimeout: store a per-slot flash timer (e.g. muzzleFlashT) set in _pulseMuzzleFlashForSlot and decay it in the render loop using the focus-scaled dt, mapping intensity/opacity off that timer. This keeps the flash readable during bullet-time and removes the overlap-flicker risk. Low-risk incremental change.
risk: Touches a hot path (every shot). Must ensure the decay still fully zeroes intensity so the light doesn't linger. Keep the same peak values to avoid retuning lighting.

title: Hostage 'discipline broken' cue uses a fixed dedup key so only the first hostage hit ever surfaces a cue
description: On a hostage hit, progress increments (main.js setpieceCheckHostageHit, line 36230). updateStoryExperience enqueues cset.trigger with the constant key `setpiece:${building}:hostage:hostage-hit` (line 419). After the first hit the seen-map suppresses all subsequent hostage-hit cues, so hitting a 2nd/3rd civilian produces no further story feedback even though each is a fresh mastery failure. May be intended (single warning), but it contradicts the per-hit progress comparison `progress > s.lastSetpieceProgress` which implies per-event firing.
evidence: Line 418 `if (kind === 'hostage' && progress > s.lastSetpieceProgress)` then line 419 enqueues with fixed key `:hostage-hit`. The progress guard re-arms each hit but the constant key blocks re-enqueue.
fix: If per-hit feedback is desired, fold progress into the key: `setpiece:${building}:${kind}:hostage-hit:${progress}`. If a single warning is intended, drop the misleading `progress > lastSetpieceProgress` comparison and document it.
risk: Very low. Only affects repeat-hostage-hit feedback in B02. No state-shape change.

title: player._shotCadenceScore is event-updated but never decayed per frame, so it 'sticks' between shots
description: _shotCadenceScore is raised via Math.max in recordShotFiredFeedback (line 86), reduced only on a miss (x0.45 in recordShotOutcomeFeedback line 111), and read in buildCombatFeedbackSnapshot (line 170, exposed as snapshot.cadenceScore). It is NOT present in any DECAY table and tickPlayerCombatFeedback never touches it, so once set it holds its peak value until the next fire/outcome event rather than easing back toward neutral over time. It is clamped (clamp01) and recomputed on every shot, so there is no NaN/crash risk; the consequence is purely that the displayed cadence score can read 'good' for a while after the player has stopped maintaining tempo. Minor feel inconsistency, not a functional bug.
evidence: Line 86: player._shotCadenceScore = Math.max(player._shotCadenceScore || 0, cadenceScore * (.45 + ads * .35)); Line 111 (miss): player._shotCadenceScore = (player._shotCadenceScore || 0) * .45; No occurrence of _shotCadenceScore in any DECAY object or tick loop (grep confirms only these three references exist project-wide).
fix: Optional: add '_shotCadenceScore' to the DECAY table in combatFeedback.js with a gentle lambda (e.g. ~1.6-2.5) so cadence relaxes toward 0 between shots, matching the other event-pulse fields. Low priority; only do if cadence-score visuals feel sticky.
risk: Low. Adding a decay key changes only how fast a clamped display value relaxes; no save-compat or crash risk. Could slightly reduce cadence-driven crosshair confidence between bursts.

title: bed headboard offset not rotated (latent — all current beds use rotY:0)
description: Same class of bug as the bench backrest: the headboard is positioned at e.z + d*0.5 - 0.20 (world +z) then rotated in place. If a bed is authored with a non-zero rotY the headboard will detach from the bed. Currently all `bed` entries (B5 FE/MW) pass rotY:0, so this is latent, not active — flagged for consistency/future-proofing alongside the bench fix.
evidence: head.position.set(e.x, WT + h + 0.20, e.z + d*0.5 - 0.20); if (e.rotY) { head.rotation.y = e.rotY; }
fix: Rotate the +d/2 head offset by e.rotY like the bench fix: const c=Math.cos(e.rotY||0), s=Math.sin(e.rotY||0); const off=d*0.5-0.20; head.position.set(e.x - s*off, WT+h+0.20, e.z + c*off); head.rotation.y=e.rotY||0; (apply the same to base/top if you ever want a rotated bed — those use full BoxGeometry so they rotate correctly already).
risk: Latent only; zero behavioral change for existing rotY:0 beds. Trivial.

title: desk L-shape: second bar hard-codes rotY:0 and uses world-axis lx/lz offsets, so a rotated desk would break (latent)
description: `desk` builds an L from two `bar` calls. The first bar inherits e.rotY (via {...e}); the second bar hard-codes rotY:0 and offsets by world-space e.lx/e.lz. If a desk were authored with rotY != 0 the L would split apart (first arm rotated, second arm not). No desk in the data passes rotY today, so latent. Also worth noting the first bar spreads `...e` which carries e.t:'desk' and any stray fields into `bar` (harmless).
evidence: ELEMENT_BUILDERS.bar(ctx, { ...e, x: e.x + (e.lx || 1.55), z: e.z + (e.lz || 1.20), w: 0.7, d: 1.8, h: 1.05, rotY: 0, top: 0xc8a040, glow: e.glow });
fix: If desks should support rotation: rotate the (lx,lz) offset by e.rotY and pass rotY:e.rotY to the second bar. If desks are intentionally axis-aligned forever, leave a comment noting rotY is unsupported. Low priority since unused.
risk: Latent; no current desk uses rotY. Zero risk to leave as-is.

title: arch rotY rotates each piece about its own center, not the arch center (latent — no arch passes rotY)
description: When e.rotY is set, the arch builder does [post1,post2,lin,ac].forEach(p => p.rotation.y = e.rotY) but the posts were positioned at e.x±w/2 in world space. Rotating each piece about its own local origin (not the arch's center) leaves the posts at the same XZ while spinning them, producing a broken arch. The inline comment even acknowledges 'Rotate whole arch as a group: simpler — re-rotate each piece.' All arch entries pass no rotY today, so latent.
evidence: if (e.rotY) { [post1, post2, lin, ac].forEach(p => p.rotation.y = e.rotY); }
fix: To support rotation, recompute each piece's position by rotating its local offset (±w/2, etc.) about (e.x,e.z) by e.rotY, then set rotation.y. Or wrap the four meshes in a THREE.Group placed at (e.x,WT,e.z), add children at local offsets, and rotate the group. Low priority (unused).
risk: Latent; zero risk if left unchanged.

title: forklift collider AABB uses hard-coded depth 2.0 vs body depth 1.9, and ignores the forks that protrude +1.2 in z
description: The forklift body BoxGeometry is 1.4(w) x 1.05(h) x 1.9(d), but the wall AABB uses Math.abs(...)*1.4/2 and *2.0/2 (depth 2.0, not 1.9). Minor over-size on depth. More noticeably, the fork tines mesh is placed at e.z + 1.2 (0.45 beyond the AABB half-depth of ~1.0), so the visible forks stick out past the collider — bullets/players pass through the forks. Cosmetic/collision mismatch; forklifts are sparse (B1 FW/FE, B9 FE).
evidence: const ax = Math.abs(c)*1.4/2 + Math.abs(s)*2.0/2; const az = Math.abs(s)*1.4/2 + Math.abs(c)*2.0/2;  // body d is 1.9; fork at e.z+1.2 lies outside AABB
fix: Use the real body depth (1.9) and extend the AABB forward to cover the forks, e.g. base footprint on a 1.4 x ~2.6 envelope offset toward +z, or add a second small AABB for the fork tines. Low priority.
risk: Slightly enlarging the forklift collider could marginally tighten nearby pathing; keep the change small. Cosmetic otherwise.

title: getVisualProfile out-of-range fallback uses ((building-1)%8)+1, wrapping into the wrong building's grade
description: VISUAL_TARGETS has 12 entries (buildings 1..12). The fallback for an unknown building is `VISUAL_TARGETS[((building - 1) % 8) + 1]`, which wraps modulo 8, not 12.
