For building values 9..12 the primary lookup VISUAL_TARGETS[building] succeeds, so the bug is dormant for the normal campaign. But any caller passing building 13+ (e.g. custom maps / demo indices) wraps into buildings 1..8 only and can never reach the 9..12 grades, and building 0 or negative would map to an unexpected slot. The modulo base (8) is inconsistent with the 12-entry table.
evidence: const profile = VISUAL_TARGETS[building] || VISUAL_TARGETS[((building - 1) % 8) + 1] || VISUAL_TARGETS[1];
fix: Change the modulo base to the table size: `VISUAL_TARGETS[(((building - 1) % 12) + 12) % 12 + 1]` (the extra +12%12 also fixes negatives), or simply `% 12`. Keeps all 12 grades reachable for out-of-range building ids.
risk: Only affects out-of-range building ids; normal 1..12 path unchanged. No save-compat or build/probe impact.

title: applySkyBackgroundFromEquirect mutates the shared HDR equirect mapping and never restores backgroundBlurriness to 0
description: Two small statefulness issues: (1) backgroundBlurriness is only set when blurriness>0 (`if (... && blurriness > 0)`). If a building requests blur and a later building requests blur=0, scene.backgroundBlurriness is never reset, so the previous building's blur persists on the new sky. (2) tex.mapping is forced to EquirectangularReflectionMapping here; the same _equirectByBn texture is the PMREM source, but since PMREM was already generated in loadBuildingEnvironment, mutating mapping post-hoc is benign — flagging only the blurriness latch as a real carry-over.
fix: Always assign backgroundBlurriness when the property exists: `if ('backgroundBlurriness' in scene) scene.backgroundBlurriness = Math.max(0, blurriness || 0);` so a building with blur=0 clears a prior building's blur.
risk: Only changes sky blur carry-over between buildings; visible only if some buildings set skyBlurriness>0 and others 0. No build/probe impact.

title: SSR groundReflector getter is hard-wired to return null, so the SSR pass never gets a real ground reflector
description: createRenderSubsystem is given getGroundReflector:()=>null. tickPhotography then sets passes.ssr.groundReflector from resolveGroundReflectorFn() each frame, which always returns null. The SSR pass code path that mixes a planar ground reflector is therefore never exercised — SSR runs reflector-less. The comment in rendering.js (line 552) anticipated main.js wiring a real getter ('tickPhotography assigns groundReflector each frame') but the getter was left as ()=>null. Either SSR ground reflections are intentionally dropped (then the per-frame reflector plumbing in tickPhotography is dead), or a real getter was meant to be supplied.
evidence: getGroundReflector:()=>null,  // main.js 15281 — rendering.js comment says tickPhotography assigns groundReflector each frame, but source is always null
fix: If planar ground reflections are wanted, wire getGroundReflector to return G.levelData.groundReflector (the wet-floor/marble reflector) when present. If not, this is acceptable but the groundReflector assignment in tickPhotography (rendering.js 754-758) can be removed as dead. Confirm intent before adding a reflector — it has perf cost.
risk: Enabling a ground reflector adds a render cost and could regress perf on high/ultra; only do if a reflector object exists. Leaving as-is is safe. No build/probe impact.

title: Adaptive lighting controller rewrites renderer.toneMappingExposure every frame, silently overriding the debug setToneMappingExposure API
description: _makeLevelLightingController.tick() lerps renderer.toneMappingExposure toward base.exposure*(1+lampNear*.035-ads*.014) every frame (lines 2394-2398) and tickLighting is called each frame (line 44105). The debug API setToneMappingExposure (line 45347) writes the same property but is reverted on the very next frame, so manual exposure tweaks via the debug console appear to 'not stick'. base.exposure is captured once at controller construction (line 2271) from renderer.toneMappingExposure at that instant, so any external exposure change is also discarded on the next level build. This is the intended 'adaptive control wins' design but is an easy source of confusion when tuning visuals; not a crash.
evidence:
const exposureTarget=base.exposure*(1+lampNear*.035-ads*.014);
      renderer.toneMappingExposure+=(exposureTarget-renderer.toneMappingExposure)*step*.50;   ...   setToneMappingExposure:(v)=>{if(renderer&&typeof v==='number')renderer.toneMappingExposure=v; ...}
fix: Optional: have the lighting controller read a mutable base-exposure source (e.g. an outer let _exposureBias) that the debug setter updates, instead of a snapshot, so manual exposure overrides survive. Or document that exposure is adaptive and should be tuned via the controller base, not the debug setter.
risk: Low. If you let the debug setter feed base.exposure, ensure it can't drift unbounded across level rebuilds. No save-compat impact.

title: buildLevel mutates shared module textures' repeat each load
description: addCinematicRealismLayer mutates the repeat of shared module-level textures: `scuffTex.repeat.set(Math.max(2,RW/12),Math.max(3,RD/12))` (scuffTex = _authoringFloorScuffMap() = shared _floorScuffTex) and `_grimeStreakTex.repeat.set(2.4,1.25)`. _grimeStreakTex is also returned by _authoringGrimeMap() and used by the grime decal material (line 2487) and grimeWallM (2521). Because UV repeat is a per-texture (not per-material) property, the last level built dictates the repeat for every reuse of that texture — including any other code paths sharing it. Loading B1 (RW=44,RD=64) vs B7 (RW=28,RD=64) leaves the scuff tiling stuck at whatever level loaded last when the texture is reused before this code re-runs.
evidence: try{scuffTex.repeat.set(Math.max(2,RW/12),Math.max(3,RD/12));}catch(_){} ... if(!_optionalPubAssets.grimeStreak)try{_grimeStreakTex.repeat.set(2.4,1.25);}catch(_){}
fix: Clone the texture before setting repeat (as is already done for floor maps via _cloneConcreteFloorMaps and for window slices), or accept it as cosmetic. Lowest-risk: clone scuffTex/grimeTex per material that needs a distinct repeat: `const scuffTex=_authoringFloorScuffMap().clone(); scuffTex.needsUpdate=true;` then set repeat on the clone. Dispose the clones in cleanup() (push their owning meshes — already happens) but clones aren't auto-disposed by the material .dispose(), so add them to a disposal list.
risk: Cloning textures increases GPU texture count slightly. If skipped, only a subtle tiling-scale inconsistency. Keep probes green.

title: Cohesion classify() uses local mesh.position.y for floor/decal height tests
description: classify() decides decal/wet/prop role partly via `mesh.position.y<=WT+.075` and `mesh.position.y<=WT+.08 && (gp.height||0)<=.025`. For any mesh whose position is relative to a parent (would matter once the grouped-prop traversal in env-cohesion-skips-grouped-props is fixed, and also already matters for the floor-overlay meshes added via addFloorOverlay which set y on the mesh directly — those are fine since top-level). The latent bug surfaces the moment grouped meshes are included: a sheet mesh at local y=0.013 inside a group sitting at world y=2.4 (mezzanine) would be wrongly classified as a floor decal and get polygonOffset/renderOrder 4 + noReflect.
evidence: if(transparent&&mesh.position.y<=WT+.075)return ...; ... if(mesh.position.y<=WT+.08&&(gp.height||0)<=.025)return 'decal';
fix: Use world Y: at top of classify resolve `const wy = mesh.parent && mesh.parent!==scene ? mesh.getWorldPosition(_tmpV).y : mesh.position.y;` (reuse a module scratch Vector3) and test against `wy`. Pair this with the grouped-prop traversal fix.
risk: Adds a getWorldPosition per classified mesh (cheap, one-time at level build). Must ensure world matrices are current — call scene.updateMatrixWorld(true) once before the cohesion pass if not already updated.

title: Demolitions cover-aware grenade target uses best.peekDx/peekDz without the ||0 guard used elsewhere
description: Line 11419 builds `_demolitionsTarget` as `new THREE.Vector3(best.x+best.peekDx*1.2,0,best.z+best.peekDz*1.2)`. The same coverSlots array is read defensively at line 10839 as `s.peekDx||0`. Baked slots (_bakeCoverSlots) always define peekDx/peekDz, but if any authored level-data coverSlot lacks them, `best.peekDx` is undefined → `x + undefined*1.2` = NaN. That NaN target is then passed into spawnEnemyGrenade at line 11699, throwing the grenade to NaN world coords (vanishes / lands at an undefined spot). Inconsistent with the guarded sibling read.
evidence:
this._demolitionsTarget=best?new THREE.Vector3(best.x+best.peekDx*1.2,0,best.z+best.peekDz*1.2):null;  // line 11419 (no ||0)
vs: const px=s.x+(s.peekDx||0),pz=s.z+(s.peekDz||0);  // line 10839 (guarded)
fix: Mirror the guard used at 10839: `this._demolitionsTarget=best?new THREE.Vector3(best.x+(best.peekDx||0)*1.2,0,best.z+(best.peekDz||0)*1.2):null;`
risk: Pure hardening; identical behavior for baked slots which always have peekDx. No save-compat or perf concern.

title: Being shot while on PATROL jumps straight to CHASE without setting lastKnownPos, so CHASE can immediately bounce back to PATROL
description: takeDamage line 8102 does `if(this.state===PATROL)this.state=CHASE;` but never sets this.lastKnownPos. In the CHASE case (line 11457) if the enemy has no LOS and horizDist>14, it falls into `if(this.lastKnownPos){SEARCH}else{PATROL}` — with lastKnownPos still null it drops straight back to PATROL, so an enemy shot from beyond 14m and out of sight can flip CHASE→PATROL the very next frame, looking like it 'forgot' it was just shot. The ALERT path (line 11427) correctly sets lastKnownPos; this damage-triggered path skips it.
fix: On the damage-triggered wake, seed a last-known position toward the shooter so CHASE has something to pursue: in takeDamage, when waking from PATROL, set `this.lastKnownPos=this.group.position.clone().addScaledVector(this.staggerDir,-4);` (staggerDir points away from attacker, so -4 along it heads toward the shot's origin) and bump alertFlashTimer. Or route through ALERT (this.state=ALERT;this.alertTimer=.2) so the existing ALERT logic runs.
risk: Makes shot-while-patrolling enemies investigate instead of dozing off — improves reactivity. Low risk; staggerDir is already normalized at line 7906. No save-compat impact.

title: _markShotVisual recoil side has an 18% random sign-flip that can kick recoil toward the peek-out side
description: Line 10912 computes the shot recover side as `(this.peekAmt>.10?(this._peekSideSign||1):(this.strafeDir||1))*(Math.random()<.18?-1:1)`. When peeking, _peekSideSign encodes which way the body leaned out of cover; the trailing random `*-1` (18% chance) flips the recoil/recover lean to the WRONG side ~1 shot in 6, momentarily reading as the enemy recoiling back INTO cover the wrong direction. It is subtle but inconsistent with the deliberate peek-side bias the rest of the system maintains.
evidence: const side=(this.peekAmt>.10?(this._peekSideSign||1):(this.strafeDir||1))*(Math.random()<.18?-1:1);  // line 10912
fix: Only apply the random flip when NOT actively peeking, where there is no committed side: `const base=this.peekAmt>.10?(this._peekSideSign||1):(this.strafeDir||1)*(Math.random()<.18?-1:1);` i.e. move the random term inside the strafe branch so a peek shot always recoils consistent with the peek side.
risk: Very low — purely a recoil-pose polish tweak; does not affect aim/damage. Keeps probes green.

title: Generic melee fallback sets hMesh/bMesh rotation directly, then the trailing lerp re-pulls bMesh toward bodyRX
description: The generic (no-kind) melee branch assigns this.bMesh.rotation.x=-lurch*.30 directly (line 9711). But this.bMesh.rotation.x is then lerped toward the accumulated bodyRX at line 10064 (this.bMesh.rotation.x+=(bodyRX-this.bMesh.rotation.x)*ls) in the same frame, partially undoing the just-set value (ls is ~0.5-1 at 20Hz urgentPose). The kind-specific branches above (knife_*, gun_bash) instead route torso motion through bodyRX or set bMesh via the dedicated this.bMesh path consistently. This fallback is reachable by plain melee (kind defaults to 'melee', line 7975) and by dropkicks (which set meleeHitTimer but leave _meleeImpactKind as 'melee'), producing muddier-than-intended torso snap on those hits. Also note hMesh/bMesh/lArmGrp are dereferenced without the if(this.hMesh) guards the other branches use (they exist on all rigs incl. drones, so not a crash).
fix: Drive the torso through bodyRX in the generic branch (e.g. bodyRX-=lurch*.30) instead of writing this.bMesh.rotation.x directly, so it composes with the lerp at 10064 like the other branches. Leave the head write (it is lerped back in the 9832 else only when no hit timer is active, which is correct).
risk: Low. Only changes the visual quality of plain-melee/dropkick torso reaction; no gameplay or save impact.

title: Training-range target dummies are pushed directly into enemyMgr._list and reset by hand-poking bMesh/hMesh y positions
description: startRange creates dummies via `new Enemy(...)` and pushes them straight into `G.enemyMgr._list` (line 38700), bypassing the manager's spawn path. tickRange respawns dead dummies by directly writing `t.bMesh.position.y=.76; t.hMesh.position.y=1.48; t.group.scale.setScalar(1); t.group.rotation.set(0,0,0)` and manually walking materials to reset opacity/transparent (38713-38728). This duplicates whatever the Enemy class's own spawn/reset does and will silently desync if the Enemy rig's rest-pose y offsets, group scale, or death-fade material handling ever change (e.g. an enemy whose hMesh rest y is not 1.48, or with extra meshes that fade). At timeout it sets t.removeNeeded=true on directly-injected list members, relying on the manager's removeNeeded sweep to dispose them.
evidence: G.enemyMgr._list.push(dummy); ... t.bMesh.position.y=.76; t.hMesh.position.y=1.48; ... _mats.forEach(m=>{if(m.opacity!==undefined)m.opacity=1;m.transparent=false;});
fix: Prefer a manager-owned spawn/reset API (e.g. enemyMgr.spawnDummy / enemy.resetToSpawn) so the rest pose, scale and material-fade reset live in one place. If kept inline, read the rest y offsets from the Enemy instance (capture them at spawn) instead of hardcoding .76/1.48 so it can't drift from the rig.
risk: Refactor touches range mode only (secondary mode). Low visible impact today; this is drift-resistance. Don't change hardcoded values blindly without confirming current rig offsets.

title: _setMaterialOverride sets scene.overrideMaterial globally with no scene-change/cleanup reset
description: _setMaterialOverride assigns `scene.overrideMaterial` (clay/normal/wire), which three.js applies to EVERY mesh in the scene including the first-person viewmodel, muzzle/tracer/decal VFX and any 3D HUD elements, and it survives a level change (it is never reset in cleanup() or on quitToMain). It is a dev-only debug entry (exposed via installPerfDebug setMaterialOverride at 45896), so impact is contained to debug usage, but a forgotten 'wire'/'clay' override persists across deploys and would make the whole game render in debug material until manually cleared. The cached overrideMats are also never disposed (minor, intentional cache).
evidence: scene.overrideMaterial=VIS_DEBUG.overrideMats[next];  // never reset on cleanup / level change; affects viewmodel+VFX+HUD meshes too
fix: Optional hardening: reset `scene.overrideMaterial=null` (and VIS_DEBUG.materialOverride='none') inside level cleanup / quitToMain, or restrict the override to the level root rather than the whole scene. Low priority since it is debug-only, but cheap to guard.
risk: Debug-only path; change is low risk. Don't dispose the cached override materials if you want re-toggle to stay instant.

title: Enemy muzzle-flash hidden via wall-clock setTimeout that can fire after the enemy is removed/disposed
description: Each enemy shot schedules `setTimeout(()=>{ ... e.muzzleFlashH.material.opacity=0; ... },55)` to hide the flash. (1) Dead enemies are filtered+removed in the same update at line 12935 (`forEach(e=>e.remove())`), and remove() disposes the muzzle-flash materials (traverse at 11866-11870). A pending 55ms timeout then touches a disposed material — harmless (no throw) but operates on a freed object and the closure retains the Enemy+group, briefly preventing GC. (2) The flash is set to full opacity for a fixed wall-clock 55ms with NO per-frame decay, so at high FPS it pops on/off as a hard step (less premium) and at very low FPS it may render for several frames or be missed entirely. The flash duration is decoupled from the frame loop unlike the rest of the VFX (G.trails are timer-driven in the loop).
evidence: line 12919: `setTimeout(()=>{ if(e.muzzleFlashH){e.muzzleFlashH.material.opacity=0;e.muzzleFlashH.visible=false;} ... },55);` plus remove() disposing materials at 11866-11870 and the dead-enemy filter+remove at 12935 in the same update tick.
fix: Drive the flash fade in the frame loop instead of setTimeout: stamp `e._muzzleFlashUntil=performance.now()+55` on fire and, in EnemyManager.update (or Enemy.update), lerp opacity toward 0 / set invisible once `now>e._muzzleFlashUntil`, guarding `if(!e.dead && e.muzzleFlashH && e.muzzleFlashH.material)`. This removes the dangling timeout, ties the flash to render frames, and lets you add a 1-2 frame decay for a punchier AAA flash.
risk: Low. Must guard against the disposed material; keep the existing instant pop intensity so it does not look weaker. No save-compat impact.

title: Dead-leader promotion can pick a `_roomFlowDormant` member, then immediately ignore the whole squad that tick
description: When the leader dies, the new leader is chosen with `this.members.find(m=>!m.dead)` (line 12225), which does NOT exclude `_roomFlowDormant` members. The very next computation `aliveMembers=this.members.filter(m=>m&&!m.dead&&!m._roomFlowDormant)` (line 12241) DOES exclude dormant. If the only non-dead member is dormant, a dormant enemy becomes leader (and gets markSquadLeader's red band attached while it is supposed to be inactive), and aliveMembers is empty so update() returns early — the squad effectively orphans onto a dormant leader and stops issuing orders even though it may reactivate later, with a leader band visible on a dormant unit.
evidence: line 12225: `const alive=this.members.find(m=>!m.dead);` (no _roomFlowDormant filter) vs line 12241: `this.members.filter(m=>m&&!m.dead&&!m._roomFlowDormant)`.
fix: Make the promotion filter match the aliveMembers filter: `const alive=this.members.find(m=>!m.dead&&!m._roomFlowDormant);`. If none, return early as today. Keeps the leader band off dormant units and the leader consistent with the squad's active set.
risk: Low. Only changes leader selection edge case when all non-dead members are dormant. No save-compat impact.

title: _cameraPunch captures oldFov then restores via setTimeout — rapid repeat calls would permanently inflate FOV (latent; function is dead)
description: _cameraPunch(amount) does oldFov=camera.fov; camera.fov+=amount*4; ...setTimeout(()=>camera.fov=oldFov,80). If called twice within 80ms, the second call captures the ALREADY-inflated fov as its 'oldFov', and the first timeout restores to the pre-first value while the second restores to the inflated value — net FOV creep. Also fights the loop's own FOV management (sprint/ADS) since it mutates camera.fov directly and calls updateProjectionMatrix outside the frame's FOV pipeline. Currently latent: _cameraPunch has no callers (grep). _cameraDip (29729) is likewise dead.
evidence: const oldFov=camera.fov;camera.fov+=amount*4;camera.updateProjectionMatrix();setTimeout(()=>{camera.fov=oldFov;camera.updateProjectionMatrix();},80);
fix: If used, drive a kick via the existing per-frame FOV system (add to a P._fovKick that decays in the loop) instead of mutating camera.fov + setTimeout, so it composes with sprint/ADS FOV and can't creep. Otherwise delete _cameraPunch/_cameraDip (29719-29731) as dead.
risk: If wiring, must integrate with whatever owns camera.fov in the loop to avoid two writers fighting. Deletion is zero-risk.

title: addShell / addMuzzleRing / addMuzzleSmoke derive direction from global camera, wrong for P2 in split-screen
description: These VFX use the module-global `camera` (P1) to compute right/forward and to billboard, even when the firing weapon belongs to P2. The eject point itself is correct (gunGroup.localToWorld), but the ejection right-vector, muzzle forward, and corona billboard face P1's view. In split-screen, P2's brass flies toward P1's right and the muzzle ring faces P1, not P2.
evidence: addShell: "const right=new THREE.Vector3(1,0,0).applyQuaternion(camera.quaternion);"; addMuzzleRing: "const fwd=new THREE.Vector3(0,0,-1).applyQuaternion(camera.quaternion);"; addMuzzleSmoke similarly. Call site (26301-26303) passes only gun, no slot/cam.
fix: Thread the firing camera into these helpers (e.g. addMuzzleRing(originLocal,gunGroup,cam=camera)) and pass _slot===1?cameraP2:camera from the shoot path; use that cam for right/fwd vectors and _orientVfxBillboard. Low priority unless split-screen polish matters.
risk: Single-player unaffected (camera===firing cam). Touching shoot-path signatures has minor regression surface; keep default param = camera.

title: Gamepad dpad-left/right sets lean and also switches weapon when ADS+LB held
description: When adsHeld is true, btn[14]/btn[15] (dpad L/R) set GAMEPAD._gpLeanLeft/_gpLeanRight (34193-34201). Separately, `if(slot===0&&lbHeld&&pressed(14))switchWeapon(prev)` (34243) fires regardless of adsHeld. So holding ADS + LB and tapping dpad-left both peeks (lean) AND cycles to the previous weapon in the same input, which is conflicting/unintended. The smoke/flash branch is correctly guarded with `&&!adsHeld`, but the LB weapon-cycle branch is not guarded against the lean state.
evidence: if(adsHeld){ if(btn[14]&&btn[14].pressed){...GAMEPAD._gpLeanLeft=true;} ... }  // later: if(slot===0&&lbHeld&&pressed(14)){switchWeapon(nextPlayableWeaponIdx(P.weaponIdx,-1));}
fix: Add `&&!adsHeld` to the LB+dpad weapon-cycle conditions (lines 34243 and 34248), e.g. `if(slot===0&&lbHeld&&!adsHeld&&pressed(14))`, so peeking while ADS does not also swap weapons. This matches the existing guard pattern used for smoke/flash.
risk: Low. Only changes gamepad binding behavior when ADS+LB are simultaneously held; preserves all other bindings.

title: Duel keeps accepting damage/scoring after a winner is decided
description: When DUEL.scores[scorer] reaches winTarget, DUEL.winner is set and quitToMain() is scheduled at +2600ms. But duelApplyDamage has no guard for `DUEL.winner>=0`, so for the 2.6s before quit both players can keep dealing damage and scoring further points (clamped by Math.min so no overflow, but extra 'POINT' toasts and respawn timers fire on top of the win banner). Reads as a minor polish bug: the win moment is cluttered by continued scoring.
evidence: if(DUEL.scores[scorer]>=DUEL.winTarget){DUEL.winner=scorer; ... setTimeout(()=>quitToMain(),2600);}  // no early-out on DUEL.winner>=0 at top of duelApplyDamage
fix: At the top of duelApplyDamage add `if(DUEL.winner>=0)return;` (after the playMode/active check) so no further damage/score is processed once the match is decided.
risk: Very low. Only affects the post-win window; clamping already prevents score overflow.

title: Endless reuses boss-bar but never resets boss-name/phase styling, and depends on the phantom-wave bug
description: endlessNextWave repurposes #boss-name/#boss-fill/#boss-phase/#boss-bar to show wave info. Combined with the endless-phantom-wave0-reward bug, the first thing the player can see is the boss bar populated for 'WAVE 0' before wave 1 spawns. Independent of that bug, the boss bar is shown with `boss-bar.classList.add('show')` but there is no corresponding hide when endless mode ends/quits in this function's vicinity, and the bar retains boss-specific CSS classes if a real boss was previously fought in the same session before starting endless.
evidence: $e('boss-name').textContent='WAVE '+ENDLESS.wave; $e('boss-fill').style.width='100%'; $e('boss-phase').textContent='× '+ENDLESS.waveTotal; $e('boss-bar').classList.add('show');
fix: Primary fix is the endless-phantom-wave0-reward guard (ENDLESS.wave>0). Additionally ensure the boss-bar is hidden on endless exit (quitToMain/restart already clear ENDLESS.active at 38366/38535 — add `$e('boss-bar')?.classList.remove('show')` there if not already handled), and strip any boss-only modifier classes before reusing the bar for waves.
risk: Low. HUD-only; verify the boss-bar hide path on quit isn't duplicated.

title: Dodge roll i-frames (450ms) are shorter than the roll duration (500ms)
description: DODGE.dur=.50 (500ms) but DODGE.iframeUntil is set to performance.now()+450 in tryDodge. takeDamage only grants invulnerability while `now<DODGE.iframeUntil`, so the final ~50ms of the visible roll is vulnerable. The perk description ('dodge with i-frames') implies the whole roll is protected. Minor but can produce 'I rolled and still got hit at the end of the roll' moments.
evidence: const DODGE={active:false,t:0,dur:.50,...}; DODGE.iframeUntil=performance.now()+450;
fix: Set iframeUntil to cover the roll: `DODGE.iframeUntil=performance.now()+Math.round(DODGE.dur*1000)+60;` (a small recovery buffer), or intentionally keep a vulnerable recovery tail and document it. Lowest risk: `+500`.
risk: Slightly more generous dodge; balance-only. No state/save impact.

title: Dark-room setpiece dims ceiling lights by *0.25 but setpieceEnd never restores intensity
description: The 'dark' setpiece multiplies every ceilingLight intensity by 0.25 (line 36087) and adds a flashlight. setpieceEnd (line 36253) removes the flashlight and hostages but does NOT restore the dimmed ceiling-light intensities. In practice this is masked because setpieceEnd runs at the next startBuilding where the whole level (and its light objects) is rebuilt fresh — so the dim never visibly carries over. It is still a latent leak/desync: if a 'dark' setpiece is ever ended mid-building, or the same levelData/ceilingLights array is reused, the lights stay at 25% permanently.
evidence: if(G.levelData&&G.levelData.ceilingLights){for(const L of G.levelData.ceilingLights){L.intensity*=.25;}}  // setpieceEnd: no inverse restore
fix: Before dimming, cache the base intensity per light (`L.userData._setpieceBaseInt=L.intensity;`) and in setpieceEnd restore: `if(SETPIECE.kind was dark) for(L of ceilingLights) if(L.userData._setpieceBaseInt!=null){L.intensity=L.userData._setpieceBaseInt;delete L.userData._setpieceBaseInt;}`. Capture SETPIECE.kind before nulling it at the top of setpieceEnd.
risk: Low; only matters in the (currently nonexistent) mid-building setpiece-end path. Avoids a future bug if setpiece lifetime changes.

title: _activeWeaponSocketNames returns USP GLB nodes for weaponIdx 6 (P226) without a .visible guard
description: At line 16549 the guard is `if((P.weaponIdx===1||P.weaponIdx===6)&&deagleGlbRig&&...uspNodes)`, returning the USP GLB's uspNodes for the P226 (idx 6). But idx 6 renders SPP_MESHES (procedural P226, made visible at 27169), not the USP GLB — for idx 6 `deagleGlbRig.visible` is false. The parallel function at line 20519 correctly adds `&&deagleGlbRig.visible` to the same idx1||idx6 check; this one omits it, so socket-name lookups for the P226 can return USP node names that don't correspond to the visible weapon.
evidence: if((P.weaponIdx===1||P.weaponIdx===6)&&deagleGlbRig&&deagleGlbRig.userData&&deagleGlbRig.userData.uspNodes){ return Object.keys(deagleGlbRig.userData.uspNodes); }   // line 20519 has the extra `&&deagleGlbRig.visible` guard this one lacks
fix: Add `&&deagleGlbRig.visible` to the condition at line 16549 to match the guard used at line 20519, so the P226 (idx6) does not report USP socket names. Used for diagnostics/attachment sockets, so impact is low.

title: Two reload-progress computations omit the P.RELOAD_TIME>0 guard that every other site uses (latent NaN/-Infinity into viewmodel pose)
description: Reload progress rt is computed in ~20 places as `P.reloading&&P.RELOAD_TIME>0?1-(P.reloadTimer/P.RELOAD_TIME):0`. Two sites drop the `P.RELOAD_TIME>0` half of the guard: line 40084 (`const rt=P.reloading?1-(P.reloadTimer/P.RELOAD_TIME):0;` inside the charging-handle pose) and line 40149 (`const rt=1-(P.reloadTimer/P.RELOAD_TIME);` inside `if(P.reloading){...}` for the main reload animation). If P.RELOAD_TIME is ever 0 while P.reloading is true, these evaluate to 1-(x/0) = NaN (x=0) or -Infinity (x>0), which then flows into _poseViewmodelPart rotations/positions and buildReloadFeelSnapshot(progress:rt), corrupting the viewmodel that frame. In practice startReload always sets P.RELOAD_TIME=finalReload>0 (main.js:27063), and main.js:46175 sets RELOAD_TIME=Math.max(...,.9) for the busy-stub, so the reloading=>RELOAD_TIME>0 invariant is currently held — but it is held by convention, not by these two call sites, which is exactly the kind of inconsistency that breaks when a new reload entry point (or a save-resume that sets reloading without RELOAD_TIME) is added. The 18 sibling sites defending against this make the two unguarded ones a clear inconsistency.
evidence: 40084:      const rt=P.reloading?1-(P.reloadTimer/P.RELOAD_TIME):0;\n40149:    const rt=1-(P.reloadTimer/P.RELOAD_TIME); // 0->1 progress\n// vs the canonical 18 sites: const rt=P.reloading&&P.RELOAD_TIME>0?1-(P.reloadTimer/P.RELOAD_TIME):0;
fix: Make the two outliers match the canonical guard: line 40084 -> `const rt=(P.reloading&&P.RELOAD_TIME>0)?1-(P.reloadTimer/P.RELOAD_TIME):0;` and line 40149 -> wrap or guard: `const rt=P.RELOAD_TIME>0?1-(P.reloadTimer/P.RELOAD_TIME):0;` (it is already inside if(P.reloading)).

title: Shared #dmg-flash overlay element multiplexes red damage / green heal / white flashbang via setTimeout-restored background — a damage hit inside the restore window shows the wrong color
description: The single #dmg-flash DOM element is repurposed for three effects, each mutating its background then scheduling a setTimeout to restore rgba(255,0,0,.25): heal flash (22880-22881, green, restored after 220ms) and flashbang (23058-23061, white, restored after 2200ms). takeDamage (37165) only sets opacity='.9' and does NOT set the background, relying on it being red. If the player takes damage during a flashbang's 2200ms restore window (very plausible — flashbangs are thrown mid-fight), the damage flash renders WHITE instead of red, misreading as another flashbang. Same for the 220ms heal window.
evidence: L37165: pl.hp-=amt;pl.dmgFlash=.2;if(slot===0)$e('dmg-flash').style.opacity='.9'; (no background reset)  L23059-23061: flash.style.background='rgba(255,255,255,.95)';...setTimeout(()=>{...flash.style.background='rgba(255,0,0,.25)';},2200);
fix: In takeDamage (and the split-HUD damage path), explicitly set the red background before raising opacity: `const df=$e('dmg-flash'); df.style.background='rgba(255,0,0,.25)'; df.style.opacity='.9';`. Better: give each effect its own overlay element/class so they don't fight over one node.
risk: Low. One-line background reset on the damage path; no timing or gameplay change.

title: Resumed run restores G.difficulty but menu difficulty buttons keep their stale active highlight
description: resumeRunState() restores G.difficulty=r.difficulty (35886/35872) from the saved run. But the menu .menu-mode difficulty buttons set G.difficulty on click (38934) and carry the visual .menu-mode-active class independently — refreshMenuContinue (38922) updates only the Continue button label, never re-syncs the difficulty button highlight to the saved run's difficulty. So a player who saved a 'hard' run, then on next launch sees 'normal' highlighted (default), can resume into a hard run while the UI implies normal. The authoritative value (G.difficulty) is correct after resume; only the menu highlight drifts. Pure cosmetic desync between persisted state and menu chrome.
evidence:
resumeRunState: G.difficulty=r.difficulty||'normal'; (35886)
menu buttons: btn.addEventListener('click',()=>{...G.difficulty=btn.dataset.diff;}); (38931-38935) — no reverse sync from G.difficulty back to button active-state on menu show / continue.
fix: In refreshMenuContinue() (38922) or a menu-show hook, when PROGRESS.runSave exists, reflect its difficulty: `document.querySelectorAll('.menu-mode[data-diff]').forEach(b=>b.classList.toggle('menu-mode-active', b.dataset.diff===(PROGRESS.runSave?.difficulty||G.difficulty)));`. Low effort, removes the misleading highlight.
risk: Very low, cosmetic only. Ensure the selector `.menu-mode[data-diff]` does not also match the operator buttons (which reuse .menu-mode but use data-op) — scoping on [data-diff] avoids that.

title: Armband emitter opacity computed >1 while reloading (no clamp)
description: The procedural armband emitter pulse during reload is `_emitM.opacity=.55+(P.reloading?.40+.20*Math.sin(now*9):0)`, whose peak is .55+.40+.20 = 1.15, exceeding the valid [0,1] opacity range. three.js clamps internally so there is no crash and the visible result is a flat saturated emitter (the top .15 of the sine swing is clipped, killing the intended pulse at the bright end). Same shape, smaller magnitudes, on _ledM_R/_ledM_L (max .95, fine).
evidence: Line 44501: `_emitM.opacity=.55+(P.reloading?.40+.20*Math.sin(now*9):0);` — max value 1.15.
fix: Clamp or rebalance so the pulse stays sub-1, e.g. `_emitM.opacity=THREE.MathUtils.clamp(.55+(P.reloading?.30+.18*Math.sin(now*9):0),0,1);` keeping headroom so the sine actually modulates at the bright end.
risk: Cosmetic; only affects the procedural armband path (hidden when authored hands own the wrist computer). No probe risk.

title: deploySmoke leaks the base cloud material (cloudM) — only the 24 clones are disposed
description: deploySmoke creates a base MeshBasicMaterial `cloudM`, then clones it 24 times (m=cloudM.clone()) for the billboards. Each clone is pushed into G.trails and disposed by _disposeTrail when its timer expires. The original cloudM is never added to the scene and never disposed, so one MeshBasicMaterial is orphaned per smoke deployment. The shared texture (_vfxDustPuffTex) is safe because clones lack atlasOwnedMap so _disposeTrail won't dispose the shared map.
evidence: const cloudM=new THREE.MeshBasicMaterial({map:_vfxDustPuffTex,...}); for(let i=0;i<24;i++){ const m=cloudM.clone(); ... G.trails.push({mesh:b,mat:m,...}); }  // cloudM itself never disposed
fix: Either dispose the base after cloning (`cloudM.dispose();` after the loop — clones already own their own GPU material; disposing the un-uploaded base is safe), or build per-billboard materials inline without a base. Single MeshBasicMaterial per smoke is tiny, so low priority.
risk: Very low. cloudM is never rendered, so disposing it post-loop cannot affect visuals. Do not dispose its .map (shared texture).

title: Gun-bash impact dereferences h.object.userData.enemy without a null/dead guard (drone-fire path guards it)
description: _resolvePistolWhipImpact takes the first raycast hit and immediately does `const enemy=h.object.userData.enemy; enemy.lastPlayerDir.set(...)` with no check that enemy exists or is alive. In practice every mesh returned by EnemyManager.getMeshes() has userData.enemy set (bMesh/hMesh line 6401/6414, limb proxies line 7450), so this does not currently throw, and takeDamage() self-guards dead enemies. But it is the only ray-hit consumer in this region without the defensive guard the drone-fire path uses (line 22238: `const enemy=h.object&&h.object.userData&&h.object.userData.enemy; if(enemy&&!enemy.dead){...}`). Any future mesh added to getMeshes() without userData.enemy would crash here.
evidence: const h=hits[0];const enemy=h.object.userData.enemy; enemy.lastPlayerDir.set(fwd.x,0,fwd.z).normalize();  // no `if(enemy && !enemy.dead)` guard
fix: Guard the block: `const enemy=h.object&&h.object.userData&&h.object.userData.enemy; if(enemy&&!enemy.dead){ enemy.lastPlayerDir.set(...); ... }` matching the drone-fire pattern. Defensive only.
risk: Very low; pure hardening. No behaviour change today.

title: Per-knife stuck silhouette materials never disposed (geometry-only cleanup)
description: _ensureKnifeStuckSilhouette creates fresh MeshBasicMaterial instances per stuck knife (bladeM, edgeM, gripM, plus gripM.clone() for the pommel) and parents the silhouette to k.grp. All knife teardown sites — _collectStuckKnife (19821), the return-complete branch (20063), and _resetKnifeRuntime (19835) — traverse k.grp disposing only `o.geometry`, never `o.material`. So each throw→stick→collect cycle leaks ~6 MeshBasicMaterial instances. (Note: this is correct for the SHARED viewmodel materials tkBladeM/tkEdgeM/etc. which must not be disposed; the bug is specifically the per-instance silhouette/beacon-style materials. _disposeKnifeBeacon does dispose beacon materials correctly; the silhouette path does not.)
evidence: _ensureKnifeStuckSilhouette: `const bladeM=new THREE.MeshBasicMaterial(...); ... const pommelLine=new THREE.Mesh(..., gripM.clone());` then `k.grp.add(g)`. Teardown: `k.grp.traverse(o=>{if(o.geometry)o.geometry.dispose();});` — no material disposal.
fix: In the three knife-grp teardown traversals (19821, 20063, 19835), also dispose materials, e.g.: `k.grp.traverse(o=>{if(o.geometry)o.geometry.dispose();const m=o.material;if(Array.isArray(m))m.forEach(x=>x&&x.dispose&&x.dispose());else if(m&&m.dispose)m.dispose();});`. WARNING: the in-flight/spawned projectile (spawnKnifeProjectile -> _buildKnifeMesh) reuses the SHARED module materials tkBladeM/tkEdgeM/tkHandleM/tkWrapM/tkBandM/tkGlintM — disposing those would break later knives. Safer: dispose only materials on meshes whose userData.role starts with 'stuck-' (the silhouette parts) and leave _buildKnifeMesh meshes alone. Given the shared-material hazard, prefer the targeted role-based disposal.
risk: Medium-risk fix if done naively (blanket material dispose would dispose shared viewmodel materials and blank out subsequent thrown knives / the equipped throw viewmodel). Use the role-scoped disposal. Low gameplay/visible impact; this is a slow accumulation, not a per-frame leak.

title: tickDynProps unit-normalization heuristic and default param disagree on units (fragile, currently masked)
description: tickDynProps signature is `(dt,now=performance.now())` and immediately does `const nowMs=now>100000?now:now*1000;`. The sole live call site (line 43950) passes the frame loop's `now`, which is `performance.now()*0.001` (SECONDS). For seconds input the heuristic uses `now*1000` (correct ms) and only breaks after ~100000s (~27.7h) uptime. But the DEFAULT parameter `performance.now()` is MILLISECONDS: if tickDynProps were ever called with no `now` argument during the first 100s of page life, `now<100000` would be true and `nowMs=now*1000` would be 1000x too large, instantly desyncing the room/light cull throttles (260ms/180ms) and the pulse phase `t=nowMs*.0025`. The magnitude-sniffing of units is brittle and the default param is inconsistent with the only caller.
evidence:
function tickDynProps(dt,now=performance.now()){
    const nowMs=now>100000?now:now*1000;
fix: Make units explicit. Either change the default to seconds: `now=performance.now()*0.001` and always do `const nowMs=now*1000;`, or drop the heuristic and require callers to pass seconds. Removing the `>100000` branch eliminates the ~27.7h overflow edge too.
risk: None for the live caller (already seconds). Pure robustness hardening. Verify no other code path calls tickDynProps with ms.

title: _weaponStatRadar divides by w.spread and w.reloadTime with no zero-guard (latent NaN/Infinity)
description: _weaponStatRadar computes range:Math.min(1,(.10/w.spread)/3) and accuracy:Math.min(1,1-w.spread*30) and handling:Math.min(1,(.5/w.reloadTime)). If any weapon has spread===0 (e.g. a future hitscan/precision weapon) range becomes Infinity and Math.min clamps it to 1, but if reloadTime===0 handling is Infinity->clamped, and accuracy can go negative. It is dead today (never called), so no current crash, but it would emit out-of-range/NaN radar values the moment it is wired to the loadout radar UI.
evidence: 28952: range:Math.min(1,(.10/w.spread)/3), 28953: accuracy:Math.min(1,1-w.spread*30), 28954: handling:Math.min(1,(.5/w.reloadTime))
fix: When wiring the radar, guard the divisors: use Math.min(1,(.10/Math.max(w.spread,1e-4))/3), clamp accuracy with Math.max(0,...), and Math.max(w.reloadTime,1e-3) for handling. Until then it is inert.
risk: None while uncalled. If wired, missing guards produce malformed radar charts (clamped to 1 or negative).

title: _hpLabel returns 'unknown' for ratio exactly 0 (dying band is half-open and excludes 0)
description: HP_LABELS.dying is [.15,.0] and the loop matches with ratio<=range[0] && ratio>range[1] i.e. ratio>0. So a fully-drained enemy (ratio===0) does NOT match 'dying' and falls through to 'unknown'. Minor and currently dead (_hpLabel has no callers), but it is an off-by-edge in a state-label helper that would mislabel a dead/at-zero enemy if wired into AI transitions.
evidence: 28859: if(ratio<=range[0]&&ratio>range[1])return k;  with dying:[.15,.0] -> ratio>0 required, so ratio===0 returns 'unknown' (28861).
fix: Make the lowest band inclusive of zero: special-case the final band with ratio>=range[1], or change the loop to ratio<=range[0] && (ratio>range[1] || range[1]===0 && ratio>=0). Inert until _hpLabel is called.
risk: None while uncalled. If wired, the fix prevents a misclassified 'unknown' AI state at 0 HP.

title: Low-HP heartbeat setInterval runs forever and is never cleared
description: A setInterval(...,1100) at 31367 polls every 1.1s for the life of the page and calls sfxHeartbeat when low HP. It is never cleared. This is benign (cheap, self-gated) but is an unmanaged timer that fires regardless of menu/pause/level-transition state, and creates a WebAudio node pair each beat while low.
evidence: 31367 `setInterval(()=>{if(G.started&&!P.dead&&P.hp/(P.maxHp||100)<.30)sfxHeartbeat();},1100);` — no clearInterval anywhere.
fix: Acceptable as-is, but prefer driving the heartbeat from the frame loop (it already gates on G.started/!P.dead) or store the id and clearInterval on teardown for cleanliness. Low priority.
risk: Very low. Behavioral no-op if left.

title: Duel arena declares floorY:WT but standard levels use floorY:0 (default) — possible foot/floor clip
description: buildDuelArena sets floorRegions=[{...,floorY:WT}] (WT=0.4) and positions the floor mesh at y=WT+h/2-0.02 (top surface ~WT+0.33=0.73). Standard buildLevel() does NOT add a whole-room floorRegion, so _floorYAt() returns its default 0 for the room while the standard floor box (main.js:2800 `box(0,WT/2,0,RW,WT,RD,fM)`) has its top at WT=0.4. The duel arena thus uses a DIFFERENT ground-height convention than every campaign level: standard rooms drive player ground Y to 0, duel drives it to WT. Depending on how P.pos.y maps to feet, this can leave the player's feet/shadow offset relative to the visible duel floor (sinking into it or hovering). Players spawn at y=0.2 then snap to floorY=WT.
evidence: duelArena.js:11 `const floorRegions=[{x0:-40,x1:40,z0:-40,z1:40,floorY:WT}];` and duelArena.js:21-22 `floor.position.set(0, WT + h / 2 - 0.02, 0)` with h=0.35. Standard convention: cover-graph floorYAt returns 0 when no region matches; buildLevel adds no room-wide region; main.js:2800 floor box top = WT.
fix: Make the duel arena follow the campaign convention: either set floorRegions floorY to 0 (matching default rooms) and position the floor mesh so its top sits at y=0 like standard floors, OR confirm by playtest that WT is intended here. Lowest-risk surgical option: change `floorY: WT` to `floorY: 0` and set the floor mesh top to 0 (floor.position.set(0, -h/2-0.02, 0)) to mirror the standard sub-floor box, then verify spawns (y is re-derived from floorY by physics anyway).
risk: Medium-uncertain: duel mode was presumably tested as-is, so the WT convention may be deliberate. Confirm with a quick playtest before changing — wrong direction would push the player through the floor. Only affects PvP duel mode.

title: getAC() lazily constructs an AudioContext but no code ever calls ctx.resume(); if the context is created outside a user gesture (or auto-suspended) all sfx/music are silent
description: getAC() returns AC || (AC = new AudioContext()) and never resumes it. Grep across src shows zero .resume() calls on the audio context. Today this usually works because musicInit() (the first audio touch on the main flow) is called right after tryLock() inside click/pointerlock gesture handlers (e.g. lines 32583/32860/35893), so creation lands inside a user gesture and the context starts 'running'. But it is fragile: any code path that triggers a SFX before that gesture (or a browser that creates the context suspended even within the gesture, e.g. iOS Safari), leaves AC in 'suspended' state forever — the entire procedural soundtrack and all sfx are silent with no error.
fix: Make getAC resilient: 'export function getAC(){ if(!AC) AC=new AudioContext(); if(AC.state==='suspended') AC.resume(); return AC; }'. Also call getAC().resume() once inside tryLock()/pointerlock handlers as a belt-and-suspenders gesture unlock. This is idempotent and cannot regress the currently-working desktop path.
risk: resume() returns a promise that can be ignored; calling it when already running is a no-op. Zero save/build impact. Confidence is medium-low only because the current desktop gesture timing already makes it work in practice — the fix is hardening, not a guaranteed live bug.

title: M4 optic profile uses socket-driven lensLocal but a hardcoded lensY for the gun-Y offset
description: _currentOpticProfile (M4 branch) returns `lensLocal:_scopeLensLocalM4` (updated each frame from the authored/procedural socket by _syncAuthoredM4Sockets / construction) AND a separately hardcoded `lensY:authoredM4?.24:.078`. _opticGunY() uses the hardcoded lensY (`-(profile.lensY||.078)`) while other code paths read lensLocal.y. If the authored scope socket Y drifts from .24 (or the procedural lens from .078) the gun's vertical ADS offset won't track the actual lens position, biasing the sight picture slightly. The two values are only guaranteed equal by construction, not by code.
evidence: Line 18478 `lensLocal:_scopeLensLocalM4,` line 18479 `lensY:authoredM4?.24:.078,`. _scopeLensLocalM4 is reassigned at runtime in _syncAuthoredM4Sockets (line 18843 `_scopeLensLocalM4.copy(scope);`) but lensY stays constant. _opticGunY (line 18553) returns `-(profile.lensY||.078)`.
fix: Derive lensY from the live socket vector to keep them in lockstep: `lensY:authoredM4?(Number.isFinite(_scopeLensLocalM4.y)?_scopeLensLocalM4.y:.24):.078` (or simply `lensY:_scopeLensLocalM4.y`). The pistol branch already does this (`lensY:_scopeLensLocalPistol.y`).
risk: Changes the M4 ADS vertical offset to follow the socket; could shift the existing tuned ADS pose by the socket-vs-.24 delta. Re-verify ads-scope-gunplay and focus-ads-viewmodel probes plus the on-screen ADS framing before committing. Keep procedural .078 fixed if the procedural lens vector isn't socket-synced.

title: _companionLightAction restore captures already-dimmed intensity if it overlaps its own restore window (currently shielded by the 8.5s rate limit)
description: _companionLightAction snapshots current light intensities, dims them to *0.18, and schedules a 1.6s restore. If it ran again before that 1.6s elapsed, clearTimeout cancels the pending restore and the fresh `saved` snapshot captures the already-dimmed 0.18*orig as the 'restore' target — permanently darkening those lights (and dimming further to 0.0324*orig). Today this cannot fire because the command is gated by _companionRate('light',8500) (line 21852), so the 8.5s cooldown always exceeds the 1.6s restore window. It is a latent desync that breaks the moment the cooldown is lowered below 1.6s.
evidence: const saved=lights.map(L=>({L,intensity:L.intensity})); for(const L of saved)L.L.intensity=(L.intensity||1)*.18; COMPANION_ROOM.lightRestore=setTimeout(()=>{for(const s of saved){if(s.L)s.L.intensity=s.intensity;}},1600);
fix: Restore immediately before re-dimming, or store baseline per-light: e.g. keep a Map of original intensities keyed by light and only snapshot when not already dimmed (`if(COMPANION_ROOM.lightRestore){ run-the-pending-restore-now } then snapshot`). Or set restore to the cached original rather than the current value.
risk: Very low today (unreachable due to rate limit). Harden only if the light cooldown is ever reduced.

title: A* straight-line shortcut `_navGridLineOpen` samples a thin diagonal and can cross a 1-cell-thick wall corner
description: navAStar (cover-graph.js, wrapped by _navAStar at main.js 12182) short-circuits with a straight path when `_navGridLineOpen` reports clear (line 141). That check samples only `steps=max(|dx|,|dz|)` interpolated points with Math.round, so on diagonals it tests a single cell per major-axis step and can tunnel diagonally past a 1-cell-thick (0.5m) wall corner, returning a 2-point straight path that clips geometry. Enemies then walk a hair into/through a thin wall corner before the next recalc. Low visible impact because the per-enemy _tryMove collision still blocks actual penetration, but it produces brief stutter/wall-hugging at diagonal corners.
evidence: lines 116-123: `const steps=Math.max(Math.abs(dx),Math.abs(dz)); ... const ix=Math.round(sx+dx*t); const iz=Math.round(sz+dz*t); if(ng.blocked[ix+iz*ng.nx])return false;` — supercover-incomplete; diagonal moves skip the off-axis neighbor cell.
fix: Either bump sampling density (`steps=Math.ceil((Math.abs(dx)+Math.abs(dz)))` or sample at half-cell increments), or for diagonal steps also test the two orthogonal neighbor cells (a + b) before declaring the segment open. Lowest risk: increase steps to the Manhattan distance so each grid cell along the line is checked.
risk: Low. Slightly more work in the (one-time-per-recalc) line check; could make A* fall through to full search marginally more often, which is the safe direction. No save-compat impact.

title: _finishTakedownImpact schedules checkZoneClears via setTimeout that can run after building transition
description: _finishTakedownImpact ends with `setTimeout(()=>checkZoneClears(),90)`. checkZoneClears reads G.enemyMgr/G.zoneClears/G.exitUnlocked. If the takedown finishes within ~90ms of an exit/advance (e.g. the takedown WAS the final kill and the player advances), this deferred call can run mid-transition and operate on a partially-reset G state. checkZoneClears guards with `if(!G.enemyMgr||!G.zoneClears||G.exitUnlocked)return;` so it is mostly safe, but it can still re-fire onZoneCleared/awardBuildingMoney edge effects if exitUnlocked hasn't been set yet at the 90ms mark.
evidence: setTimeout(()=>checkZoneClears(),90);
fix: Either call checkZoneClears() synchronously at the end of the impact (the 90ms delay buys nothing functional since the kill/_list removal already happened via takeDamage(9999)), or add a guard `if(!TAKEDOWN.active&&G.started&&!P.dead)checkZoneClears();` inside the timeout. Lowest risk: call it synchronously.
risk: Very low; checkZoneClears is idempotent-ish via its guards. Synchronous call removes a 90ms latency on the ROOM/BUILDING CLEAR beat after an execution (slight feel improvement).

title: knife-throw enemy hit calls enemy.takeDamage without the null guard the author uses one line earlier
description: In the enemy-hit branch, line 20155 defensively guards `if(enemy&&enemy.lastPlayerDir)`, signalling the author considers enemy possibly falsy, yet line 20158 then calls `enemy.takeDamage(...)` unconditionally. If a returned mesh ever lacked userData.enemy this would throw a TypeError inside the frame loop. In practice every mesh from enemyMgr.getMeshes() (bMesh/hMesh line 6401/6414, limb proxies line 7450) sets userData.enemy, and the established shoot()/ricochet path at line 25228 is also unguarded, so this is consistent with the codebase and not a live crash today — but the local guard inconsistency is a latent hazard if mesh sourcing changes.
evidence: Line 20155: `if(enemy&&enemy.lastPlayerDir)enemy.lastPlayerDir.set(...)` then line 20158: `const killed=enemy.takeDamage(isHead?999:200,isHead,true);` with no enemy check.
fix: Wrap the damage/kill block in `if(enemy){...}` (mirroring the guard on 20155). If enemy is falsy, fall through to treat the hit like a world surface (or just skip). Keep the existing recall: `k.grp.position.copy(h.point); _startKnifeReturn(k,h.point,{hitReturn:true}); continue;` outside the guard so the knife still returns.
risk: Low. Adding a guard only prevents a crash that currently can't happen given mesh invariants; no gameplay change in the normal case. Safe and cheap hardening.

title: STABLE_RENDERING_MODE=true makes the ENTIRE post-processing chain dead at runtime (no bloom, AO, color grade, vignette, SMAA, sharpen, SSR, DoF, LUT)
description: Line 470 hardcodes `const STABLE_RENDERING_MODE=true`. The composer gate at line 15502 is `useComposer = !!(_renderStack && _renderStack.composer && G._useComposer!==false && !STABLE_RENDERING_MODE)` — since STABLE_RENDERING_MODE is always true, `!STABLE_RENDERING_MODE` is always false, so useComposer is ALWAYS false and every frame falls through to _renderFrameDirect (line 15538), bypassing EffectComposer. On top of that, `_forceStableVisualSettings` (471-502) hard-overrides postEnabled, aoQuality, bloomQuality, colorGrade, filmGrain, chromaticAberration, sharpen, smaa, vignette, phase2SSR/LUT/DoF/Volumetrics/Reflections all to off and forces rendererMode='webgl', pixelRatioCap 1.0, scopePipEnabled false. The rendering.js subsystem builds bloom/GTAO/grade/SMAA/sharpen/SSR/bokeh/LUT passes (rendering.js 526-651) that NEVER execute. The game currently renders with only ACES tone mapping + RoomEnvironment IBL + MSAA. Enabling even a conservative subset (bloom on emissives + color grade + vignette) is the single highest-visible-impact change available — emissive signage/holograms/muzzle flashes would bloom, blacks would get filmic grade, and the frame would read dramatically more cinematic the instant it loads.
evidence: L470: const STABLE_RENDERING_MODE=true;  L15502: const useComposer=!!(_renderStack&&_renderStack.composer&&G._useComposer!==false&&!STABLE_RENDERING_MODE);  L472-485: postEnabled:false, aoQuality:'off', bloomQuality:'off', colorGrade:false, ... vignette:false
fix: This is clearly a deliberate stability kill-switch (likely from the WebGPU/black-frame saga). Do NOT blindly flip to false. Surgical option: leave STABLE_RENDERING_MODE for the WebGPU disable, but carve out a 'safe post' subset that runs on WebGL — e.g. in _forceStableVisualSettings keep bloomQuality:'medium', colorGrade:true, vignette:true (leave SSR/DoF/GTAO/LUT/TAA off) and change line 15502 gate so the composer runs when only the cheap, proven-stable passes are enabled. Verify against scripts/render-smoke.mjs + scripts/visual-runtime-acceptance.mjs that frames are non-black before/after on the target machine.
risk: HIGH operationally: STABLE_RENDERING_MODE was set to guard against a real rendering regression (black frames / instability per project memory). Re-enabling the full composer could reintroduce that. Mitigate by enabling only bloom+grade+vignette (no SSR/TAA/GTAO which had documented r170 uniform edge cases) and gating behind the existing render-health self-test.

title: Per-building patrol retag is a permanent no-op (ROOM_PATROL_KIND keyed by floorplan ids, looked up with flow ids) — _makeCampaignRoutes() output is entirely dead
description: campaignEncounters._cloneNativeCampaignEncounterFromB01 remaps every encounter's `room` to a FLOW id (b02_intake_peek, b02_relay_cage, ...) BEFORE calling mergeNativeEncounterTactics(raw, bn). Inside that merge, line 294 does `ROOM_PATROL_KIND[e.room]`, but ROOM_PATROL_KIND is keyed by FLOORPLAN-SPACE ids (dock_intake, relay_cage, alarm_relay_room, ...). Flow ids never match floorplan ids, so `kind` is always null. Result: the building-specific patrol retag `u.patrol = _routePatrolTag(bn, kind)` never fires, and the kind-based coverHint defaults (objective->relay_desk, signature->vestibule_face, flank->drum_spool) never apply. B02-B12 enemies keep B01's literal patrol routes (cage_left_arc, drum_lateral, ...) at B01 coordinates instead of the intended per-building routes. Consequently the ENTIRE _makeCampaignRoutes() generator in encounterPatrolRoutes.js (b02_arrival_route ... b12_overwatch_route, the bulk of ENCOUNTER_PATROL_ROUTES) is dead data that nothing ever references.
evidence: encounterPatrolRoutes.js:61-83 generates `b${bn}_${kind}_route`; nativeEncounterTactics.js:201-203 `_routePatrolTag(bn,kind)` returns the same name; nativeEncounterTactics.js:294 `const kind = ROOM_PATROL_KIND[e.room] || null;` with ROOM_PATROL_KIND (205-215) keyed dock_intake/relay_cage/... while e.room is 'b0X_intake_peek'/'b0X_relay_cage'. Runtime-verified: getCampaignEncounterDef(2).encounters[drum].enemies[0].patrol === 'drum_lateral' (B01 base route), coverHint === undefined; the generated b02_flank_route is never assigned.
fix: Make the room-key namespaces agree. Cheapest fix in scope of the data files: in nativeEncounterTactics.js, key ROOM_PATROL_KIND by the flow-room SUFFIX (intake_peek->arrival, relay_approach->mid, alarm_relay->objective, drum_flank->flank, relay_cage->signature) and change line 294 to strip the `bXX_` prefix from e.room before lookup, e.g. `const kind = ROOM_PATROL_KIND[String(e.room).replace(/^b\d{2}_/, '')] || null;`. Alternatively delete _makeCampaignRoutes() from encounterPatrolRoutes.js if per-building routes are not wanted. Verify with node import that getCampaignEncounterDef(2) flanker.patrol becomes 'b02_flank_route'.
risk: Activating the retag changes enemy patrol paths for B02-B12 (the generated routes must be sane for each building's geometry — they are derived from CAMPAIGN_ROUTE_CENTERS_BY_BN which look plausible). Low crash risk; medium gameplay/positioning risk. No save-compat impact. No probe currently covers this, so add an assertion.

title: applyHudTheme sets --hud-* CSS vars that nothing in the project reads (inert theming feature)
description: applyHudTheme() writes --hud-primary/--hud-secondary/--hud-accent/--hud-bg/--hud-text on documentElement, and a setTimeout at load applies the 'classic' theme. Grep across index.html and all src shows ZERO consumers of var(--hud-primary) etc. The entire HUD_THEMES system (29303-29336: classic/cyber/blood/forest) is therefore inert — selecting a theme changes nothing on screen.
evidence: root.style.setProperty('--hud-primary',theme.primary); ... setTimeout(()=>{try{applyHudTheme('classic');}catch(_){}},0);  // grep for var(--hud-primary|secondary|accent|bg|text) => no matches anywhere
fix: Either (low-risk visible win) wire the HUD CSS so it actually consumes these vars — e.g. point the live crosshair/hitmarker/ammo accent colors at var(--hud-accent, #ffd060) and the HUD panel backgrounds at var(--hud-bg) in the inline <style> in index.html / the HUD style block — then expose a theme selector; or delete the dead theming block. Wiring it makes 4 selectable palettes light up instantly.
risk: If wired, must keep a fallback (var(--hud-accent,#ffd060)) so existing default look is unchanged when no theme set. Pure deletion is zero-risk but loses a near-finished feature.

title: KILLCAM third-person orbit is fully dead — never triggered, would also never restore the camera
description: The whole 'KILLCAM ORBIT' subsystem (KILLCAM object, triggerKillcamOrbit(), updateKillcam()) is wired into the frame loop (line 41603 calls updateKillcam) but triggerKillcamOrbit() is never called from anywhere in the codebase. grep confirms the only references are the definition and the loop call. So KILLCAM.active is never set true and the cinematic orbit never plays. This is a half-wired AAA feature that does nothing. Separately, even if it were triggered it is broken: on completion updateKillcam only sets active=false with a comment '// Snap camera back to player' but never restores camera.position/quaternion (KILLCAM.startCamPos/startCamQuat are stored at 26934-26935 but never read), and G._killcamLockedInput is set/cleared but never consumed by any input handler. So the feature is both dead AND incorrect.
evidence: Definition only, no callers: `function triggerKillcamOrbit(enemy){ if(KILLCAM.active||!enemy||DEATHCAM.active)return; ... }` and on finish `if(ph>=1||!KILLCAM.target){ KILLCAM.active=false;G._killcamLockedInput=false; // Snap camera back to player\n return; }`. grep for triggerKillcamOrbit across src/ returns only this definition. KILLCAM.startCamPos/startCamQuat are assigned but never read anywhere (grep).
fix: Decide intent. To ship the feature: call triggerKillcamOrbit(enemy) from the kill path (e.g. inside the killed-branch around line 26445-26486, gated to special kills like last-of-zone or boss to avoid spam), AND in updateKillcam's completion branch actually restore the saved transform: `camera.position.copy(KILLCAM.startCamPos);camera.quaternion.copy(KILLCAM.startCamQuat);` before clearing active, and make a real input handler honour G._killcamLockedInput. To drop it: delete the KILLCAM object, triggerKillcamOrbit, updateKillcam and the loop call at 41603. Do NOT leave it half-wired.
risk: If enabling: orbit positions the camera every frame in updateKillcam which runs in the loop; must confirm ordering vs the normal camera update so it isn't immediately overwritten, and gate triggers tightly or it will spam/feel jarring. If deleting: trivial, just remove dead symbols. Either way build/probes stay green since nothing depends on it.

title: FX_CAP clamps multi-pellet FX to 1, contradicting the comment ('first 3 pellets') — shotgun shows a single tracer/impact
description: The comment says 'only spawn full FX on the first 3 pellets' but the code is `const FX_CAP=Math.min(numShots,1);` — i.e. only the FIRST pellet gets a tracer, surface impact, blood, ricochet, breakable/cover damage and surface SFX. For the TAC-12 shotgun (pellets:7, per src/data/weapons.js line 6) all 7 pellets still apply damage (the enemy-hit branch at 26392 is not gated by allowFx), but the trail (26566), the surface-impact branch (26489 `else if(allowFx)`), spawnSurfaceImpact, ricochet, breakable/explosive/cover-HP handling all only run for pellet 0. Result: a shotgun blast visually reads as a single bullet — only one tracer and one wall impact instead of a satisfying pellet spread. This badly undersells the shotgun's punch.
evidence: `// For multi-pellet weapons, only spawn full FX on the first 3 pellets ...` immediately followed by `const FX_CAP=Math.min(numShots,1);`. Then `const allowFx=pellet<FX_CAP;` and `} else if(allowFx){ ...surface impact, decals, ricochet, breakable... }` and `if(allowFx){ ...addTrail... }`.
fix: Change line 26343 to match the stated intent and restore visible spread: `const FX_CAP=Math.min(numShots,3);` (gives 3 tracers/impacts for shotgun while keeping a GC cap). For an even punchier shotgun consider allowing all pellet tracers but capping the heavier surface decals: e.g. trails for all pellets, addImpact/spawnSurfaceImpact only for pellet<3.
risk: Slightly more meshes per shotgun shot (up to 3 tracers + 3 impacts vs 1). The comment already deemed 3 acceptable; full-auto guns are single-pellet so unaffected. Keep at 3 to respect the GC budget the comment cites.

title: Scripted cinematic building-intro flythrough is fully implemented but never triggered
description: startBuildingIntro (31818) sets up a 4-phase camera flythrough, a cinematic whoosh SFX, and a building-name overlay; tickIntro (32293) runs it every frame gated on INTRO.active. But startBuildingIntro is never called anywhere (only INTRO.active=true is inside startBuildingIntro itself). So the intro never fires — the loop ticks tickIntro every frame for nothing, and a polished, AAA-feeling level-reveal is dark. References BUILDING_INFO[G.building-1].name which exists.
evidence: grep: only occurrences of startBuildingIntro are its definition (31818) and INTRO.active=true (31820) inside it; no caller. tickIntro is called at 41613 but immediately returns since INTRO.active is false.
fix: Call startBuildingIntro() at building start — e.g. inside startBuilding after the level is built and camera positioned (near 35396/35405) and guard with a setting/first-time flag so it can be skipped. Ensure G._introLockedInput is honored by the input/movement code (it sets the flag but verify movement actually reads it). Low-risk visible payoff for the moment you enter a level.
risk: Medium — must verify G._introLockedInput actually suppresses player movement/look during the 4.5s, and that camera control is cleanly handed back (tickIntro restores at 32307-32312). Test that it doesn't fight the existing spawn camera.

title: Floating damage numbers fully removed — spawnDmgNumber() is a no-op that just clears the DOM container, yet 3 hit sites still build+discard a world position every hit
description: spawnDmgNumber (33699) reduces to `const c=$e('dmg-numbers'); if(c)c.innerHTML='';` — it never renders a number. It is still called from three hit-resolution paths: hitscan (25230), projectile (25555), and secondary/penetration (26549). Each caller does `h.point.clone().add(new THREE.Vector3(0,.4,0))` — a Vector3 clone + allocation to compute a position that is immediately thrown away, plus a DOM write (innerHTML='') per bullet hit, for zero visual payoff. The #dmg-numbers container (index.html:257) and its CSS (game.css:361) still exist, so the feature is fully scaffolded but the spawn logic was stripped. Floating damage/headshot numbers are a hallmark of AAA hit feedback; restoring them is low risk and high visible impact.
evidence: L33699-33702: function spawnDmgNumber(worldPos,amt,isHead,killed,labelExtra){ const c=$e('dmg-numbers'); if(c)c.innerHTML=''; }  — callers L25230/25555/26549: spawnDmgNumber(h.point.clone().add(new THREE.Vector3(0,.4,0)),dmg,isHead,killed)
fix: Reimplement spawnDmgNumber to project worldPos to screen (camera.project), create a short-lived absolutely-positioned span in #dmg-numbers with the amount (gold for headshot, white for body, larger pulse on kill), animate opacity/translateY via CSS class + setTimeout removal (cap concurrent nodes, e.g. 24). Keep the innerHTML='' wipe OUT of the per-hit path. Reuse the existing kill-confirm color tokens for consistency.
risk: Low. Container/CSS exist; isolated to a UI overlay. Cap node count to avoid DOM growth under sustained fire. No save-compat or perf hot-path concern beyond the cap.

title: campaignCuePack only defines a 'pressure' setpiece, but no building ever sets setpiece.kind='pressure' — buildings 4-12 get zero setpiece story cues
description: campaignCuePack (used for buildings 4-12) authors setpieces.pressure ({start,trigger,silenced}). updateStoryExperience looks up cues.setpieces[setpiece.kind] (line 404). SETPIECE_DEFS in main.js (lines 36025-36034) only ever sets kind to 'alarm'|'hostage'|'ambush'|'sniper'|'dark'|'survival' — never 'pressure'. So for buildings 4-8 (which DO run real setpieces: sniper/dark/survival/ambush/alarm), cues.setpieces[kind] is undefined, cset is undefined, cloneCue(undefined) returns null, and no SETPIECE_LIVE / REINFORCEMENTS / PRESSURE-BROKEN story cue ever shows. The hand-written 'pressure' cue block is dead for every building. Buildings 1-3 are fine because they author the matching kind keys (alarm/hostage/ambush).
evidence: campaignStoryExperience.js setpieces.pressure block (lines 30-36) keyed 'pressure'; updateStoryExperience line 404: `const cset = cues.setpieces && cues.setpieces[kind];`. main.js SETPIECE_DEFS 4:{type:'sniper'},5:{type:'dark'},6:{type:'survival'},7:{type:'ambush'},8:{type:'alarm'} — grep for kind:'pressure'/type:'pressure' returns nothing in main.js.
fix: In campaignCuePack, key the setpiece pack by the actual kind each building uses instead of the generic 'pressure'. Simplest robust fix: change the lookup in updateStoryExperience line 404 to fall back to a generic pack, e.g. `const cset = (cues.setpieces && (cues.setpieces[kind] || cues.setpieces.pressure)) || null;` so the authored 'pressure' copy is reused for any unmapped kind. Buildings 4-8 then surface their setpiece cues. Keeps story-experience-static-probe green (it only asserts B1-3).
risk: Low. Additive; only affects buildings whose setpiece cue is currently absent. No save-compat impact (cues are transient). Verify the generic 'pressure' copy reads acceptably for sniper/dark/survival kinds.

title: Authored 'overwatch_catwalk' behavior and 'sniper' role are unhandled — the signature-room overwatch enemy is a plain default scout in all 12 buildings
description: campaignEncounters b01_be_scout (the catwalk overwatch in every signature room) is authored with `type:'scout', role:'sniper', behavior:'overwatch_catwalk'`. applyEncounterRole only handles 'lookout'/'anchor'/'flanker' — 'sniper' falls through with no nudge. applyEncounterEnemySpec's behavior switch handles peek_from_cover/patrol_then_alarm/guard_objective/hold_angle/suppress_lane/flank_after_contact/rush_when_player_reloads/ambush_on_crossing/push_after_contact/reposition/patrol_route — but NOT 'overwatch_catwalk'. main.js keys long-range tuning on enemy.type==='sniper'/'marksman', not encounterRole, and this enemy's type stays 'scout'. Net: the intended elevated marksman reads/plays like a generic close-range scout (peekRate=1, holdRiskCap=0.45, scout HP/range/burst).
evidence: campaignEncounters.js:504-515 `{ id:'b01_be_scout', type:'scout', role:'sniper', behavior:'overwatch_catwalk', ... }`. Runtime-verified: applyEncounterEnemySpec(...overwatch_catwalk+sniper...) leaves type='scout', peekRate=1, holdRiskCap=0.45, encounterPreferredState=null. 'overwatch_catwalk' appears in ENCOUNTER_BEHAVIORS (campaignEncounters.js:42) but in no handler.
fix: Either (a) change the authored enemy type to 'sniper'/'marksman' so existing type-based AI applies (campaignEncounters.js b01_be_scout `type:'sniper'`), and/or (b) handle role 'sniper' in applyEncounterRole (raise attackRange/lower peekRate/raise holdRiskCap, set encounterPreferredState='HOLD_CORNER') and add a `b==='overwatch_catwalk'` case in applyEncounterEnemySpec mirroring 'hold_angle' plus a longer ideal range. Lowest-risk visible win: bump peekRate down and holdRiskCap up for this role so it actually holds the overlook.
risk: Changing type to sniper changes HP/damage/burst/visuals — re-balance the signature room. Adding a role/behavior branch is additive and low-risk. No save-compat impact.

title: MUSIC_PROFILES has only 8 entries but the game has 12 buildings; reverb has 12 — late buildings get the wrong music key/tempo
description: MUSIC_PROFILES (line 13071) defines per-building tempo/scale/key for buildings 1-8 only. reverbSetBuilding's profiles array (line 13103) defines 12 entries (adds border crossing, cathedral, karelia freighter, spire). musicSetBuilding clamps with Math.min(bn-1, MUSIC_PROFILES.length-1), so buildings 9-12 silently reuse building 8's 'A-minor blues' @140bpm 'server farm' music while their reverb correctly switches to cathedral/tunnel/etc. The adaptive-score feature is half-wired: it stops scaling per-building exactly where the reverb keeps going. A player reaching buildings 9-12 hears the wrong, mismatched score (fast blues over a cathedral reverb wash).
fix: Add 4 more entries to MUSIC_PROFILES (indices 8-11) matching the 4 extra reverb environments — e.g. {tempo:100,scale:[0,2,3,5,7],rootHz:100,name:'border-crossing'},{tempo:66,scale:[0,2,3,5,7,8,11],rootHz:84,name:'cathedral-harmonic'},{tempo:112,scale:[0,1,5,7,8],rootHz:92,name:'freighter-phrygian'},{tempo:134,scale:[0,3,5,6,7,10],rootHz:98,name:'spire-blues'}. No structural change needed; musicSetBuilding's clamp keeps working.
risk: Pure data addition, no save-state or build impact. Worst case is a subjectively wrong key choice for buildings 9-12 (still strictly better than reusing building 8). Keep array a plain literal so the static probes stay green.

title: Hard 22m vision cap in canSee() defeats sniper/marksman attackRange (up to ~27m)
description: canSee() returns false for any target beyond 22m for ALL enemy types (single hardcoded `if(dist>22)return false`). But sniper attackRange is `22+diff*1.2` (≈26.8m at diff 4) and marksman is `20+diff*1.0` (≈24m). The CHASE→ATTACK transition at line 11462 requires `horizDist<=this.attackRange && cs`; since cs is forced false past 22m, a sniper/marksman can never engage at the upper half of its own stated range. It is dragged inward (CHASE at 11457 with no LOS sends it to SEARCH/closer) until within 22m, so the 'long sightline' fantasy and the LONG SIGHTLINE toast (line 11472) are undercut. The archetype's defining trait (reach) is silently clamped.
evidence:
const dist=Math.sqrt(dx*dx+dz*dz);if(dist>22)return false;  // line 10327
// vs TS sniper rng:22+diff*1.2, marksman rng:20+diff*1.0 (lines 6298,6307)
fix: Make the vision cap per-archetype. Replace the constant 22 with a per-enemy sight distance, e.g. `const _sight=this.attackRange+ (this.type==='sniper'||this.type==='marksman'?6:2); if(dist>Math.max(22,_sight))return false;` so snipers/marksmen see across their full engagement band while others keep ~22m. Keep the existing smoke/wall sampling unchanged.
risk: Slightly longer canSee raycasts for snipers (more sample steps at long range) but only for 1-2 archetypes; the spatial wall index already bounds cost. Could make snipers engage from farther — that is the intended buff. Re-run the 32 static probes; no save-compat impact.

title: Player grenade kills skip P.kills++, killfeed and combo — every other kill source credits them; grenade kills are 'silent'
description: explodeGrenade, on a lethal blast, calls only addBlood + awardKillMoney + cinematicKill + checkZoneClears. It does NOT increment P.kills, push a killFeed entry, or call comboKill. Every other lethal path does the full set: gun (26448-26451), gun-bash (21433), knife throw (20162-20165), ricochet (25237-25239), dropkick (27662-27666), takedown (36620-36623), and even the explosive-barrel path whose comment literally says 'same as grenade explosion' actually does more — line 33162: `killFeed(false,{dist:d});P.kills++;comboKill(...);P.money+=20`. Net effect: frag-grenade multi-kills don't count toward the run kill stat, never appear in the killfeed (player can't tell the grenade got the kills), and break the player's combo chain instead of extending it.
evidence: if(killed){ addBlood(e.group.position.clone(),false); awardKillMoney(e,false); cinematicKill(e.group.position.clone()); setTimeout(()=>checkZoneClears(),60); }  // no P.kills++, no killFeed, no comboKill
fix: Inside the `if(killed)` block add the canonical trio used by the barrel path: `P.kills++; killFeed(false,{dist:d}); comboKill(false,{source:'grenade-kill',closeRange:THREE.MathUtils.clamp(1-d/5,0,1)}); applyStoryMomentumShock(e,pos,{source:'grenade-kill'});` (d is already computed in the loop).
risk: Low. Adds stat/feed/combo credit that the rest of the game already grants. comboKill on a multi-kill could chain a large combo — desired for frag clears. No save-compat concern.

title: Two competing writers drive the same #low-hp vignette element with different thresholds in the same frame
description: The low-HP red vignette element ($e('low-hp')) is written by TWO independent blocks in the same frame. Block A (41684-41699) sets opacity from hpRatio (P.hp/P.maxHp) with threshold 0.30 and folds in P._criticalHitPulse. Block B (43740-43747) sets opacity from an absolute P.hp<35 check with a sin() pulse. Because Block B runs later in the loop it wins on most frames, so the critical-hit-pulse contribution and the maxHp-relative ratio logic in Block A are effectively dead for the final visible value. They also disagree on threshold semantics (30% of maxHp vs a hardcoded HP<35), so on a non-100-maxHp build the two systems light up at different HP values. Both blocks are additionally gated on the dead G._frame%3 (see g-frame-never-incremented), so neither is actually throttled.
evidence: Block A: 41695 `const lowHpOpacity=hpRatio<.30?.85*(1-hpRatio/.30):0;` 41696 `$e('low-hp').style.opacity=!spawnVisualGrace?String(Math.max(lowHpOpacity,criticalVisual*.26)):'0';` — Block B: 43741 `const _lhEl=$e('low-hp');` 43744 `}else if(!spawnVisualGrace&&!P.dead&&P.hp<35&&((G._frame|0)%3)===0){ const _lhP=.55+.45*Math.sin(now*4.5); _lhEl.style.opacity=String(_lhP*(1-P.hp/35)*.92);` Both target id 'low-hp'.
fix: Pick one owner. Simplest: delete/neutralize Block A's low-hp opacity write at 41695-41696 (keep its criticalVisual computation only if Block B consumes it), and let Block B own the element — but make Block B use hpRatio (P.hp/(P.maxHp||100)) instead of the hardcoded 35 so it matches the rest of the HUD, and fold criticalVisual into it. Alternatively delete Block B and keep Block A (which already includes critical-hit pulse). Either way remove the dead G._frame%3 gate or replace with G._frameAlt&1.
risk: Visual-only. Risk is a brief change in when/how strongly the red vignette appears; verify at HP just below 30% and at a critical hit. No save/perf concern.

title: Overhead-slam combo (s===2) animation + slash FX are unreachable — MELEE.slash is never 2
description: MELEE.slash is assigned ONLY at line 14276: `style==='heavy_stab'?3:(MELEE.comboCount%2)`. For light slices comboCount cycles 0->1->0 via line 14271 `(comboCount+1)%2`, so comboCount%2 is 0 or 1; for heavy it is forced to 3. Therefore MELEE.slash is always one of {0,1,3} and NEVER 2. Every `s===2` branch keyed off `MELEE.slash%4` is dead: the full hand-authored 'COMBO 2: Overhead power slam' viewmodel animation in updateKnife (windup/crash/impact-hold/recovery), the spawnSlashFx 'overhead slam — downward arc + impact starburst' branch, and the rests[2] idle pose. A polished overhead attack was authored but can never trigger. The 'cd2' combo pip (line 14304) also only lights when comboCount===3 (heavy), never via a real combo-2.
evidence:
14276: MELEE.slash=style==='heavy_stab'?3:(MELEE.comboCount%2);  // {0,1,3} only
14271: MELEE.comboCount=(elapsed<MELEE.COMBO_WINDOW)?((MELEE.comboCount+1)%2):0; // 0 or 1
14347 spawnSlashFx: else if(s===2){ ...overhead slam... }  // s never 2
15630 updateKnife: }else if(s===2){ ...COMBO 2: Overhead power slam... }  // never runs
fix: Decide intent and wire it, low-risk + high-visible: change the light-attack combo to a 3-step chain so the authored slam plays. At line 14271 use `(MELEE.comboCount+1)%3` (cycle 0,1,2) and keep slash=comboCount%4 at 14276 (or set MELEE.slash=MELEE.comboCount). Verify comboMult at 14408 `1+(MELEE.comboCount%2)*.10` still gives sane scaling for comboCount===2 (it would give 1.0; consider `(MELEE.comboCount)*.06`). Alternatively, if a 2-hit chain is intended, delete the dead s===2 blocks and the rests[2] entry and fix the misleading '4-hit combo chain' comment at line 13326.
risk: Enabling combo-2 changes melee feel/timing and damage cadence; must keep the 32 static probes green. The slam animation has longer dur (s===2 windup to t<0.16 etc.) but MELEE.dur for light is set at 14291 to a short value (.31/.34) so the slam keyframes would be time-compressed — re-tune MELEE.dur for the slam case if enabled. If only deleting dead code, no gameplay risk.

title: tickHealthRegen (passive out-of-combat HP regen) is never called; CONFIG.player.hpRegen/hpRegenDelay also unused
