description: tickHealthRegen(dt) implements slow passive regen (1.5 hp/s after 5s without damage) but has no caller (grep: only the definition). The only regen actually wired into the loop is tickSlideRegen (33848, called at 41664) which ONLY regens while sliding. So a player standing still out of combat never recovers HP. CONFIG.player.hpRegen:1.5 and hpRegenDelay:5.0 (29525-29526) are likewise read nowhere — the function hardcodes its own 5000ms / 1.5 instead of referencing CONFIG. This is a half-wired survivability feature and a constants-defined-but-ignored contradiction.
evidence: function tickHealthRegen(dt){...P.hp=Math.min(P.maxHp,P.hp+dt*1.5);}  // grep tickHealthRegen => 1 (def only). grep CONFIG.player.hpRegen => no matches. Loop only calls tickSlideRegen at 41664.
fix: If passive regen is intended, add `if(typeof tickHealthRegen==='function'&&G.started)tickHealthRegen(dt);` next to the tickSlideRegen call at line 41664, and have it read CONFIG.player.hpRegen / hpRegenDelay*1000 instead of the hardcoded 1.5/5000 so the two stay in sync. If not intended, delete tickHealthRegen (29881-29888) and the orphan CONFIG fields.
risk: Enabling passive regen changes game balance/feel — confirm design intent before wiring (it makes the game noticeably easier). Pure deletion is safe.

title: OBJECTIVE_DEFS stealth/timer objectives fail the wrong building mastery (B07/B10 mismatch)
description: OBJECTIVE_DEFS (31868) declares B07='quiet the deck' stealth and B10='reach the bell tower' timer, and tickObjective sets G.mastery.failed=true on alarm (32166) / on timeout (32203). But the campaign's actual mastery for B07 is 'yacht_no_heal' (No-Heal Boarding, CAMPAIGN_LEVELS line 37266) and for B10 is 'cathedral_silent_choir' (don't fire in the nave, line 37273). So being seen on the yacht fails the player's No-Heal mastery even though no heal was used, and the bell-tower timer expiring fails the Silent-Choir mastery even though the player never fired in the nave. Two parallel objective systems write to the same G.mastery.failed flag with unrelated conditions.
evidence: OBJECTIVE_DEFS 31871 `7: {kind:'stealth',...}` 31873 `10:{kind:'timer',timerS:90,...}`; tickObjective 32166 `if(G.mastery)G.mastery.failed=true;` (stealth alarm) and 32203 `if(G.mastery)G.mastery.failed=true;` (timer expiry). Campaign mastery for B07 is yacht_no_heal (37266) and B10 is cathedral_silent_choir (37273).
fix: Either (a) gate the G.mastery.failed writes in tickObjective behind a check that the active building's mastery.id matches this objective's intent, or (b) decouple objective failure from mastery entirely (these objectives already have their own o.failed/announce flow at 32239) and let only the genuine mastery conditions (heal use at 37163, firing-in-nave detection) toggle G.mastery.failed. Remove lines 32166 and 32203's `if(G.mastery)G.mastery.failed=true;` for buildings whose mastery is unrelated.
risk: Low. Mastery is meta-progress (PROGRESS.mastery); current behavior wrongly denies it. No save shape change.

title: Enemy HP never scales with difficulty — _adjustEnemyHp / DIFF_HP_MUL / DIFFICULTY_MODIFIERS are all dead, descriptions promise tougher enemies
description: _adjustEnemyHp(e) (30975) multiplies enemy maxHp/hp by DIFF_HP_MUL but is never called anywhere (grep finds zero callers). DIFFICULTY_MODIFIERS.enemyHp (30867/30873/30879) and DIFF_HP_MUL (30974) are never read by gameplay. The only real difficulty scaling is player-damage-taken (_difficultyDamageScale 37123) and score multipliers (35202/36996/38463). So on Hard/Lethal the enemies hit the player harder but have IDENTICAL health to Normal, directly contradicting DIFFICULTY_MODIFIERS descriptions ('Tougher AI', enemyHp 1.30/1.65) and DIFF_DESCRIPTIONS. The Veteran/Expert promise of tougher enemies is unfulfilled.
evidence: 30975-30980 `function _adjustEnemyHp(e){ ...const mul=DIFF_HP_MUL[G.difficulty||'normal']||1.0; e.maxHp=Math.round(e.maxHp*mul); e.hp=e.maxHp; }` with no caller; 30867 `enemyHp:1.0,...` / 30873 `enemyHp:1.30,...` / 30879 `enemyHp:1.65,...` never referenced.
fix: Call _adjustEnemyHp(e) from the Enemy spawn/init path (e.g. right after each `new Enemy(...)` in waves, or inside the Enemy constructor after hp/maxHp are set, gated by G.difficulty!=='normal'). Pick ONE multiplier table as source of truth (DIFF_HP_MUL) and delete the duplicates (DIFFICULTY_MODIFIERS.enemyHp, DIFF_DESCRIPTIONS) or wire them in. Take care boss hp is handled separately (don't double-scale lieutenants which already *=1.5 at 32982).
risk: Medium — changes combat balance on Hard/Lethal and could affect leaderboards/mastery times. Apply behind difficulty!=='normal' and verify boss/lieutenant aren't double-scaled.

title: AGILITY powerup (fastReload) has zero effect — never read as a powerup
description: POWERUP_DEFS includes {id:'fastReload',name:'AGILITY',desc:'+100% reload speed · 15s'}. _grantPowerup pushes {id:'fastReload'} onto POWERUPS.active and shows a toast. But reload speed only ever consults the PERK system: `const reloadMul=hasPerk('fastReload')?.70:1.0;` (lines 27056,27089). Nothing calls hasActivePowerup('fastReload'). The powerup is fully spawnable (spawnPowerupPickup picks a random def) and grants a buff that is never read, so picking up AGILITY does nothing but flash a toast and advertise '+100% reload speed'.
evidence: {id:'fastReload',name:'AGILITY',desc:'+100% reload speed · 15s',dur:15,col:0x40ff80}  // reload only checks: const reloadMul=hasPerk('fastReload')?.70:1.0;  (no hasActivePowerup('fastReload') anywhere)
fix: In the reload-duration computation (lines 27056 and 27089), multiply reloadMul by an additional factor when the powerup is active, e.g. `if(typeof hasActivePowerup==='function'&&hasActivePowerup('fastReload'))reloadMul*=0.5;` to deliver the advertised +100% reload speed. (Choose 0.5 for the buff to roughly match the '+100% speed' wording.)
risk: Low. Only shortens reload while the temporary buff is active; does not touch perk path or save shape.

title: Hand-authored COVER_HINT_ANCHOR_PATCH_BY_BN values for buildings 2-7 and 10 are silently overwritten at module load by the computed loop
description: COVER_HINT_ANCHOR_PATCH_BY_BN is hand-authored at lines 7-55 with tuned per-building anchors (e.g. B2 relay_desk:[-13.9,2.45], drum_spool:[14.35,0.12], spine_pinch:[0.35,2.25]). The module-load loop at 167-199 does `COVER_HINT_ANCHOR_PATCH_BY_BN[bn] = { ...(existing||{}), <computed> }`, and the computed object always re-sets the SAME keys (spine_pinch, relay_desk, drum_spool, intake_apron, west_lane_fork, east_stack, fe_stack, cage_pillar_west, cage_center_low, vestibule_face, desk_rail). Because computed keys come AFTER the spread, they win. Verified: every hand-authored anchor for B2,B3,B4,B5,B6,B7,B10 is overwritten (0 survive); B8,B9,B11,B12 use distinct names (rack_face/cold_row/customs_lane/etc) that survive but aren't in the computed set. These anchors are consumed live by _resolveCoverAnchor in encounterBehavior.js (line 162-164) to bias enemy cover selection, so the designer's manual tuning is discarded and replaced by route-center approximations that can differ by several meters (B2 relay_desk: authored [-13.9,2.45] vs computed objective_preview center ~[-7.15,-1.0]).
evidence: Lines 176-190 set spine_pinch/relay_desk/drum_spool/etc unconditionally; line 176 spreads existing first: `COVER_HINT_ANCHOR_PATCH_BY_BN[bn] = { ...(COVER_HINT_ANCHOR_PATCH_BY_BN[bn] || {}), intake_apron: ..., ... relay_desk: objective || [-14,2], ... }`. Only the `if (bn===1)` block (191-198) re-pins values after; bn 2-12 keep computed. encounterBehavior.js:163 `if (patch && patch[hint]) return patch[hint];`.
fix: Invert the merge so hand-authored values take precedence: build the computed defaults first, then spread the authored map on top, e.g. `COVER_HINT_ANCHOR_PATCH_BY_BN[bn] = { <computed defaults>, ...(authored[bn] || {}) };` (capture the original authored map into a const before the loop so the spread isn't reading the already-mutated object). This preserves the tuned B2-B10 anchors and still fills gaps with route-derived fallbacks.
risk: Low-medium. Changes enemy cover bias positions back to the authored intent for B2-B10 (a behavior change vs current shipped values). Confirm authored anchors are still inside valid room bounds. No save-compat / no build-graph impact; validate-campaign / validate-room-flow do not check these.

title: SUPPRESS / HOLD_CORNER / PEEK_FIRE state enums are declared but never assigned to this.state
description: The tactical FSM constants HOLD_CORNER=6, PEEK_FIRE=7, SUPPRESS=9 are defined and documented as states layered on ATTACK, but a repo-wide grep for `state\s*=\s*(SUPPRESS|HOLD_CORNER|PEEK_FIRE)` returns ZERO assignments. The suppress mechanic actually runs via the per-enemy flags this.suppressUntil / this.suppressBurstsLeft (set in EnemyManager._tryFormPairs line 12709-12710 and Squad.update line 12330-12331) while the enemy stays in ATTACK. Consequently every branch keyed on `this.state===SUPPRESS` is unreachable: the suppress POSE at line 8383 (`else if(this.state===SUPPRESS)poseState='suppress';`) never fires, the SUPPRESS locomotion 'run' mapping at line 6148 never fires, and the awareness-propagation guard `a.state===PEEK_FIRE` at line 12866 is always false (redundant with the ATTACK check beside it).
evidence:
const PATROL=0,...,HOLD_CORNER=6,PEEK_FIRE=7,REPOSITION=8,SUPPRESS=9;  // line 6063
... else if(this.state===SUPPRESS)poseState='suppress';  // line 8383 — state never equals SUPPRESS
... if(!(a.state===CHASE||a.state===ATTACK||a.state===PEEK_FIRE))continue;  // line 12866 — PEEK_FIRE never assigned
fix: Decide one of two paths. (A) If suppress is meant to be a real visible pose: in the ATTACK case where _isSuppressing is computed (line 11811) set this.state=SUPPRESS while suppressing and restore to ATTACK when suppressBurstsLeft hits 0, so the dedicated 'suppress' pose at 8383 and the run locomotion at 6148 actually drive. (B) If suppress is intentionally a flag-only overlay, delete the dead `this.state===SUPPRESS` pose branch (8383), the SUPPRESS term in the locomotion map (6148), and the `a.state===PEEK_FIRE` term (12866) to remove the contradiction. Path A gives a visible AAA win (distinct hunkered suppress stance); path B is the zero-risk cleanup.
risk: Path A changes which animation pose plays for suppressing enemies — verify the 'suppress' pose exists in ENEMY_POSE_STATES and reads well; keep the existing flag-based fire-gating untouched so suppression fire behavior is unchanged. Path B is cosmetic dead-code removal, no behavioral change. Either keeps build/probes green.

title: RUN_STATS per-weapon/per-enemy tracking is never populated; compileFullRunStats() returns empty breakdowns
description: recordKillStat(), recordShotStat() and resetRunStats() (lines 29983/29996/30001) have NO callers anywhere (grep confirms only their definitions). The live reset path uses a DIFFERENT function _resetRunStats() at line 37584 which does NOT touch RUN_STATS. Consequently RUN_STATS.perWeapon / perEnemyType / perBuilding stay empty for the whole run, and compileFullRunStats() (29053) — itself uncalled — copies empty objects into stats.perWeapon/perEnemyType. This is a fully orphaned stats subsystem masquerading as live telemetry.
evidence: grep recordKillStat => only 'function recordKillStat' (def). grep resetRunStats => only def at 30001; real reset is _resetRunStats() (37584) which sets P.kills/headshots etc. but never clears RUN_STATS. stats.perWeapon=Object.assign({},RUN_STATS.perWeapon) // always {}
fix: Either delete RUN_STATS + recordKillStat/recordShotStat/resetRunStats/compileFullRunStats (29977-30091, 30001-30005) as dead; OR wire it: call recordShotStat(P.weaponIdx,hit) in the shoot/hit path, recordKillStat(...) where P.kills++ happens (e.g. near the cinematicKill call sites at 14490/21433/26448), and add RUN_STATS reset inside _resetRunStats() at 37584. Naming collision (resetRunStats vs _resetRunStats) is the trap.
risk: Wiring adds per-shot bookkeeping in the hot fire path — keep it O(1) object writes (it is). Deletion risk near-zero. Watch the _resetRunStats vs resetRunStats name collision when refactoring.

title: DOUBLER powerup (doubleScore) has zero effect — never read anywhere
description: POWERUP_DEFS includes {id:'doubleScore',name:'DOUBLER',desc:'×2 score chain · 12s'}. _grantPowerup pushes {id:'doubleScore'} onto POWERUPS.active, but a repo-wide search shows nothing reads hasActivePowerup('doubleScore') (or 'doubleScore' at all outside the def). The promised ×2 score/combo chain never applies, so DOUBLER is a no-op buff that only shows a toast.
evidence: {id:'doubleScore',name:'DOUBLER',desc:'×2 score chain · 12s',dur:12,col:0xffd060}  // grep 'doubleScore' returns only the def line; no hasActivePowerup('doubleScore') consumer
fix: Either (a) wire it: in the combo/score award path (e.g. comboKill / money award sites), multiply the granted score/combo credit by 2 when hasActivePowerup('doubleScore'), or (b) if scoring multiplier is out of scope, drop 'doubleScore' from POWERUP_DEFS so the player is not handed a dead buff. Minimal surgical option is (b).
risk: Low. (b) removes a never-functioning option; (a) adds a multiplier only while buff active.

title: extraFocus unlock applies +0.0 — a no-op; 'Enhanced focus (Lv 5)' reward does nothing
description: The Lv-5 unlock 'extraFocus' is advertised in the unlock list (38817 '✓ Enhanced focus (Lv 5)') and stored/migrated in PROGRESS.unlocks, but applyUnlocks() implements it as `P.focus=Math.min(1,(P.focus||1)+0.0)`. Adding 0.0 to a meter that is always clamped to [0,1] is a literal no-op. The feature is half-wired: the unlock is earned, persisted, shown as completed, yet has zero gameplay effect. By contrast the autoFocus perk meaningfully bumps P._focusRegen (31082). extraFocus has no analogous effect — it never touches P._focusRegen, FOCUS_FEEL.regen, or any focus cap.
evidence: if(u.extraFocus)P.focus=Math.min(1,(P.focus||1)+0.0);   // line 35939  — vs autoFocus: if(hasPerk('autoFocus'))P._focusRegen=1.35; (line 31082)
fix: Give the unlock a real effect. Cheapest faithful fix: make it boost focus regen like autoFocus, e.g. replace 35939 with `if(u.extraFocus)P._focusRegen=Math.max(P._focusRegen||1,1.2);` (applied alongside applyPerks2 ordering) OR start each building with a partial focus charge, e.g. `if(u.extraFocus)P.focus=Math.min(1,(P.focus||0)+0.35);`. Whichever matches design intent of 'Enhanced focus'. Keep it idempotent so it survives the per-building applyUnlocks() call.
risk: Low. Pure additive buff. If implemented as a regen bump, ensure it composes with autoFocus's 1.35 rather than being overwritten by applyPerks2 (31082 unconditionally sets P._focusRegen=1.0 when autoFocus absent). Order matters: applyUnlocks runs before/independent of applyPerks2 in some paths — set it inside applyPerks2 to avoid being clobbered.

title: Authored M4 viewmodel GLBs (~7.6MB) are loaded every session but can never be shown
description: _loadAuthoredM4Viewmodels() runs unconditionally at module init (main.js:19506). It fetches/parses/clones/validates weapon.rifle (public/assets/weapons/m4/m4_viewmodel.glb, 6.4MB) and viewmodel.operative.hands (operative_hands.glb, 1.2MB) and parents them (invisible) to gunGrp. But every use is gated by _isAuthoredM4RuntimeActive(), which requires isPlayableWeaponIdx(0) AND P.weaponIdx===0. In src/data/weapons.js WEAPONS[0] (M4A1) is {playable:false, removed:true}, so PLAYABLE_WEAPON_INDICES = [1..7] and isPlayableWeaponIdx(0) is permanently false. The authored M4 runtime therefore can never activate; the GLB load, GLTF parse, SkeletonUtils clone, validation, scaling and GPU upload are pure waste on every load. Consistent with the project's 'GLB paths disabled by design' rule, but the disable is done at the weapon-data layer while the loader still pays the full cost.
evidence: main.js:18808 `return !!(isPlayableWeaponIdx(0)&&m4AuthoredWeapon&&m4AuthoredWeapon.ok&&...&&P&&P.weaponIdx===0&&!(G&&G.splitScreenActive))` ; weapons.js:3 `{name:'M4A1',...,playable:false,removed:true,...}` ; main.js:19506 `_loadAuthoredM4Viewmodels();` (unconditional). Verified at runtime: isPlayableWeaponIdx(0) === false, START_WEAPON_IDX === 1.
fix: Guard the loader: wrap the call site `_loadAuthoredM4Viewmodels();` (main.js:19506) in `if (isPlayableWeaponIdx(0)) _loadAuthoredM4Viewmodels();` so the 7.6MB fetch/parse is skipped while M4A1 stays removed. Do NOT flip M4A1's removed/playable flags (that would revive a disabled GLB path per the hard rules). This only short-circuits dead work; runtime visuals are unchanged because the rig is already never shown.
risk: Very low. The branch never produces visible output today; skipping it cannot change in-game visuals. Must keep the GLB available on disk so asset probes (validate:weapons, asset-registry-probe) still pass — they load by manifest id directly, not via this function, so they are unaffected.

title: EXTRA_ELEMENTS[1] and ROUTE_COMPLETION_ELEMENTS_BY_BN[1] are never executed (B01 returns early)
description: applySequenceLayout returns immediately after applyB01DesignedDockLevel(ctx) for bn===1 (line 62-65), BEFORE the loops that consume EXTRA_ELEMENTS[bn] (lines 99-103) and ROUTE_COMPLETION_ELEMENTS_BY_BN[bn] (lines 108-112). Yet EXTRA_ELEMENTS[1] (lines 3480-3547, ~37 elements) and ROUTE_COMPLETION_ELEMENTS_BY_BN[1] (lines 3393-3398, 4 kits) are fully authored. They are dead code. Worse, they reuse the SAME geometryIds as the hand-authored dock (e.g. 'west_service_run', 'dock_threshold_strip', 'relay_partition_north', 'relay_partition_west', 'relay_offset_door', 'manifest_office_window', 'east_compression_corridor', 'foreman_cage_wall', 'foreman_glass', 'catwalk_to_cage_window', 'intake_apron_divider', 'mid_spine_pinch', 'cage_vestibule', 'relay_side_slit', 'alarm_interact_lane'), so if anyone moved the early-return or special-cased B01 differently the level would get duplicated/competing geometry with conflicting ids.
evidence: if (bn === 1) { applyB01DesignedDockLevel(ctx); return; }  …  const extras = EXTRA_ELEMENTS[bn] || []; (never reached for bn===1)
fix: Delete EXTRA_ELEMENTS[1] (lines 3480-3547) and ROUTE_COMPLETION_ELEMENTS_BY_BN[1] (lines 3393-3398) since they are superseded by applyB01DesignedDockLevel, OR add a comment at the early return making clear B01 intentionally skips both tables. If removing, double-check no tooling/audit script enumerates EXTRA_ELEMENTS[1] (grep scripts/*.mjs).
risk: Pure dead-code removal; no runtime behavior change for B01 today. Risk only if an external audit script reads these arrays — verify before deleting; otherwise keep but annotate.

title: logBuildingClear()/BUILDING_CLEAR_LOG never called and never restored from save
description: logBuildingClear is defined but never invoked (the real building-advance flow is advanceBuilding() at line 37053). It also writes PROGRESS._buildingClearLog and calls saveProgressFile(), but _buildingClearLog is never read back on load, so even if it were called the stats would be a write-only, non-persisted blob. This is a feature half-wired so it never triggers AND a state-desync (written-but-never-read).
evidence: function logBuildingClear(bn){...PROGRESS._buildingClearLog=BUILDING_CLEAR_LOG;saveProgressFile();}  // grep: logBuildingClear appears only at its definition; _buildingClearLog is only ever written, never read.
fix: If a per-building clear log is desired, call logBuildingClear(G.building) inside advanceBuilding() (37053) and hydrate BUILDING_CLEAR_LOG from PROGRESS._buildingClearLog at load time (merged against defaults to preserve save compat). Otherwise delete 28482-28494.
risk: Wiring it adds a saveProgressFile() write per building clear; keep the merge-against-defaults rule for clearance_progress. Deleting is fully safe.

title: RECOIL_PATTERNS is a dead duplicate of the live RECOIL_PATTERNS_LEARNABLE table
description: RECOIL_PATTERNS (per-weapon up/horiz/recovery/bloom) is defined but never read; the actual recoil system uses RECOIL_PATTERNS_LEARNABLE (defined at 25662, consumed at 25907) and RECOIL_STATE. Two recoil-pattern tables coexist with different values; the second one is inert. Risk: a future edit could 'tune recoil' in the dead table and see no effect, or someone could wire the wrong one and silently change recoil for every weapon.
evidence: 28917: const RECOIL_PATTERNS={0:{up:.04,horiz:.015,...}, ...};  // grep -nE "RECOIL_PATTERNS\\b" (excluding _LEARNABLE) finds only this definition. Live system: 25662 RECOIL_PATTERNS_LEARNABLE, used at 25907.
fix: Delete RECOIL_PATTERNS (28916-28925) to remove the ambiguity, or rename/merge into the learnable table if its values are the intended tuning. Do not wire it without reconciling values against RECOIL_PATTERNS_LEARNABLE.
risk: Deleting is safe (no readers). Reconciling could change weapon recoil feel — verify against the live table first.

title: Color-grade pass applies a Reinhard tonemap that double-tonemaps with the renderer's ACES + OutputPass
description: renderer.toneMapping is ACESFilmicToneMapping (main.js line 14732) and the composer chain ends with OutputPass, which re-applies the renderer's tone mapping + sRGB at the end. But makeColorGradeShader's fragment also tone-maps: it multiplies by exposure then does Reinhard `col = col / (col + 0.72)`. So scene HDR is compressed once by the grade pass and again by OutputPass/ACES. Double tone-mapping flattens contrast, crushes/desaturates highlights, and makes the image read less 'punchy' the moment you load. This is the single biggest cheap contrast/saturation win in the pipeline.
fix: Remove the `col = col / (col + vec3(0.72));` line from the grade fragment so the grade pass only does exposure/contrast/saturation/warm-cool/vignette/grain/sharpen, and let OutputPass do the single ACES tonemap. Keep the exposure multiply (it pre-exposes before ACES, which is correct). Verify in one building load that highlights/skylines look richer, not blown; if blown, scale the configure() exposure clamp slightly down. Low code risk, isolated to one shader line.
risk: Image will get noticeably brighter/more contrasty; tuned grade.exposure values (0.78..1.24) may need a small downward nudge to avoid clipping the brightest emissives. No build/probe break (shader string only).

title: Bullet/melee _pushImpulse nudges enemy TOWARD the shooter, opposing the stagger knockback
description: this.staggerDir is set to lastPlayerDir.negate() (line 7906), i.e. it points AWAY from the player — the direction the body should fly after a hit. The stagger knockback consumer correctly pushes along +staggerDir (line 10120: group.position.addScaledVector(this.staggerDir,...)). But the bullet-hit _pushImpulse is built with the OPPOSITE sign: x:-this.staggerDir.x, z:-this.staggerDir.z (lines 8091-8092), and the consumer adds it directly (lines 8090/9829-9830 + 9824-9831). The melee version has the same negation (lines 8000-8001). Net result: every bullet/melee hit applies a small impulse pulling the enemy toward the shooter, directly fighting the stagger knockback and contradicting the inline comment 'nudge the body in the bullet direction' (bullet direction == away from player == +staggerDir). The dropkick path is built correctly with +fx/+fz (away from player, line 27649), proving the intended convention and the asymmetry.
fix: Flip the sign so the impulse runs along +staggerDir (away from the shooter, matching the stagger knockback and the dropkick convention): set x: this.staggerDir.x*push, z: this.staggerDir.z*push at lines 8091-8092, and likewise x:this.staggerDir.x*pushScale*impactWeight, z:this.staggerDir.z*pushScale*impactWeight at lines 8000-8001. Magnitudes are small so save/balance impact is minimal, but impacts will read noticeably punchier.
risk: Low. Changes only the direction of a small (~0.06-0.4u over ~130ms), brief positional nudge. No save-compat impact. Could very slightly increase enemies being shoved into walls — mitigated because _tryMove still collision-checks the resulting position (the impulse moves group.position directly without collision in 9829, but stagger already does the same, so net risk is unchanged and bounded by the small magnitude).

title: Nightclub disco flare meshes tagged discoFlareVisual but never animated
description: For bn===3 four corner glow spheres are created and tagged `flare.userData.discoFlareVisual=true`, and the matching fake lamp gets `userData:{baseIntensity:1.2,discoFlare:true}`. Neither flag is read anywhere in the codebase (grep: discoFlareVisual / discoFlare have no consumers). The disco ball itself rotates and hue-cycles via dynProps 'disco', but these four side flares are static, non-pulsing additive spheres. In a nightclub the most expected motion is pulsing/strobing accent lights, so this is a half-wired feature: the intent (animated flares) was tagged but the tick was never written.
evidence: fakeCeilingLamps.push({...userData:{baseIntensity:1.2,discoFlare:true}}); ... flare.userData.discoFlareVisual=true; — no reader exists for either flag.
fix: In tickDynProps (or the lighting tick) pulse these: register them like other dynProps, e.g. push `dynProps.push({type:'discoFlare',grp:flare,phaseX:Math.random()*6.28})` and add a branch: `else if(dp.type==='discoFlare'){ dp.grp.material.opacity=.30+0.35*Math.abs(Math.sin(now*3.4+dp.phaseX)); dp.grp.material.color.setHSL((now*.5+dp.phaseX)%1,.95,.55); }`. Cheap, high on-screen payoff for the club level.
risk: Adds a few per-frame opacity/color writes for B3 only. Material.opacity already transparent. No state/save impact.

title: cinematicKillEnhanced (boss/lieutenant kill flash + slow-mo) and _flashScreenColor are never called — boss kills get no extra punch
description: cinematicKillEnhanced(hitPt,enemy) wraps the live cinematicKill() and adds type-specific flair: a gold full-screen flash + slow-mo on boss kills, red flash + slow-mo on lieutenant kills, and a streak flash on 10+ combos. But every kill site calls plain cinematicKill(...) (14490, 20166, 21433, 21505, 23128, 26448, 27667) — cinematicKillEnhanced has no callers. Its only consumer, _flashScreenColor (29659), is therefore also transitively dead. Result: boss/lieutenant kills lack the intended cinematic emphasis.
evidence: function cinematicKillEnhanced(hitPt,enemy){cinematicKill(hitPt); if(enemy.isBoss){_flashScreenColor(0xffd060,800);triggerKillCamSlowMo(.20,2.5);} ...} // grep cinematicKillEnhanced => def only; all kill sites call cinematicKill(
fix: At boss/lieutenant kill sites, swap cinematicKill(pos) for cinematicKillEnhanced(pos, enemy) (the kill paths already have the enemy object in scope, e.g. 14490/21433/26448). One-line swaps give an immediate, high-visibility gold flash + brief slow-mo on lieutenant/boss kills. Fix _flashScreenColor z-index note below before enabling.
risk: triggerKillCamSlowMo on every boss/LT kill must not stack with an existing boss-death cinematic elsewhere — verify no double slow-mo. Low risk; visible payoff is large for boss moments.

title: _flashHitMarker, _flashKillBeat, spawnVictoryFireworks, spawnRainParticles, spawnSnowParticles are all defined but never called (duplicate/inert feedback)
description: Several player-feedback/particle helpers are orphaned: _flashHitMarker (29644) — the live hit marker uses the hm-/hs class system (22622-22627) + G.hitMarkTimer (43749), so this older direct-opacity version would conflict if wired; _flashKillBeat (29652) — kill-beat is driven inline at 26925/32443/36606/22858; spawnVictoryFireworks (29686), spawnRainParticles (29702), spawnSnowParticles (29711) have no callers. Rain/snow ambience and victory fireworks are finished-but-unwired atmosphere.
evidence: grep _flashHitMarker/_flashKillBeat/spawnVictoryFireworks/spawnRainParticles/spawnSnowParticles => each returns only its own definition line.
fix: Visible win: call spawnVictoryFireworks(P.pos) on campaign clear / boss-down victory screen, and emit spawnRainParticles() a few times per frame in outdoor buildings (yacht=7, dock=1) gated by a per-frame budget to add weather ambience. Delete _flashHitMarker (conflicts with live hitmarker) and _flashKillBeat (redundant). spawnRainParticles uses RH+WT (defined globals) so it is safe to call.
risk: Rain/snow push into G.trails every frame — gate by CONFIG.visual.particleCap and a per-frame count or it leaks meshes/materials and tanks FPS. Fireworks at victory is one-shot, safe.

title: _initMenu3D (main-menu world-behind props) never called; if wired would leak boxes
description: _initMenu3D adds 8 faux building boxes to the scene for a 'world behind the menu' look and pushes them into MENU3D.particles, but the function is never called. Besides being dead, there is no teardown: MENU3D.particles meshes/geometry are never removed/disposed when the game starts, so if it were ever wired in it would leak geometry + leave menu props in the gameplay scene.
evidence: 31797 `function _initMenu3D(){` with no caller; 31811 `b.position.set(...);scn.add(b);MENU3D.particles.push(b);` and no disposal/removal path for MENU3D.particles anywhere.
fix: Either delete _initMenu3D + MENU3D (dead) or, if used for menu polish, add a teardown that scene.remove()s and geometry.dispose()s every MENU3D.particles entry when G.started becomes true, and call _initMenu3D only on the menu screen.
risk: Low. Currently inert. Only relevant if someone wires it; flag prevents a future leak.

title: Weapon skins unlock toasts but are never applied to any weapon visual
description: _grantSkin stores PROGRESS._skin_<id> and shows a 'SKIN UNLOCKED' toast, driven from the saveProgress wrapper (30751-30763). But nothing ever reads WEAPON_SKINS or _skin_* to change a weapon's material/appearance (grep across all src finds no equip/apply path; only a telemetry count at 29812). The player is promised cosmetic unlocks that never visibly appear — a half-wired feature.
evidence: 30745 `const s=WEAPON_SKINS[id]; if(s)attachToast('... SKIN UNLOCKED ...');` and grep for WEAPON_SKINS/_skin_ shows only grant + telemetry, no render-time application.
fix: Either implement skin application (read an equipped/highest-tier _skin_* and tint the viewmodel material in the weapon build/switchWeapon path) for a real visible reward, or remove the 'SKIN UNLOCKED' toast so the game doesn't promise something it never shows. The former is the AAA win.
risk: Low for removing the toast. Implementing application is medium (must not touch the disabled GLB paths or add material.skinning).

title: SHAKE_PROFILES + shake(profile) helper is never called; all shake remains scattered ad-hoc
description: A clean named-profile shake system (SHAKE_PROFILES with shoot/bigHit/explosion/takedown/land/etc and a shake(profile) helper writing PP.shakeX/Y and PP.shakeDecay) is defined but never called (grep: only def at 30800 and PP write inside it). Every shake in the game instead pokes PP.shakeX/PP.shakeY inline (dozens of sites 11350..33575), and PP.shakeDecay stays at its init value 11 forever (only set inside the never-called shake()). The intended per-event decay tuning never takes effect.
evidence: 30800 `function shake(profile){ ...PP.shakeX+=...;PP.shakeY-=...;PP.shakeDecay=p.decay; }` no caller; PP.shakeDecay read only at 44524-44525, written only inside shake() — so decay is permanently the init 11.
fix: Wire shake('explosion'|'bigHit'|'takedown'|'land'|'vault') into the corresponding events (grenade/explosion, heavy hit, takedown, landing, vault) to get distinct, AAA-feeling impact decay, OR delete SHAKE_PROFILES+shake if you keep the inline model. Cheap visible upgrade: route the big events (explosion/bigHit/land) through shake() for punchier, faster-settling camera kicks.
risk: Low. Adding calls only adds shake on top of existing; setting PP.shakeDecay per event changes settle speed — verify it feels right and probes still green.

title: Extended SFX library and per-type enemy hit particles defined but unused
description: sfxRicochet, sfxNearMiss, sfxDistantShot, sfxCasingClatter, sfxBodyFall, and the per-enemy-type _enhancedHitParticle (heavy spark burst / drone cyan arc) are fully implemented but never called (only sfxKnifeWhoosh from this block is used, at 14300/19872). sfxImpactFor (31369) routes to sfxRicochet/sfxBodyFall but sfxImpactFor itself is never called either. These are ready-made, low-cost audio/visual juice computed and discarded.
evidence: grep shows no callers for sfxRicochet/sfxNearMiss/sfxDistantShot/sfxCasingClatter/sfxBodyFall/sfxImpactFor/_enhancedHitParticle; _enhancedHitParticle 31375 builds AdditiveBlending sparks into G.trails as isParticle (a live system).
fix: Wire _enhancedHitParticle(hitPoint, enemy.type) into the central enemy-hit handler (near the bullet-hit/blood-spray site) for armored spark bursts on heavy/riot/shielded and cyan arcs on drones. Wire sfxCasingClatter to the eject point on fire, sfxNearMiss when a bullet passes close to the camera, sfxBodyFall on enemy death/ragdoll. Each is a cheap, immediately-visible/audible AAA upgrade.
risk: Low-medium. _enhancedHitParticle pushes into G.trails which already self-disposes via timer; ensure the spawn rate is gated (it spawns 5-8 meshes per hit). Audit that trails cleanup disposes geometry/material (verify isParticle path).

title: Enemy muzzle flash comment claims 'additive' but the material is normal-blended
description: The enemy muzzle flash material `_mfM` is documented as 'The plane sprites below (additive, transparent) still produce a bright muzzle flash visual' (lines 7047-7048), but the material is created without `blending:THREE.AdditiveBlending` (line 7050) — same omission as the player flash. The code contradicts its own comment, and enemy muzzle flashes are weaker than intended (also tone-mapped). Cross-cuts the player-flash finding; fixing both makes ALL gunfire pop.
evidence: // The plane sprites below (additive, transparent) still produce a bright muzzle flash visual. ... const _mfM=new THREE.MeshBasicMaterial({color:0xffee88,transparent:true,opacity:0,depthWrite:false,side:THREE.DoubleSide});
fix: Add `blending:THREE.AdditiveBlending, toneMapped:false` to `_mfM` at line 7050 (the clones _mfMv/_mfMd inherit via .clone()). This makes the comment truthful and makes enemy gunfire read as a bright flash. Just outside the assigned range but the same defect class.
risk: Minimal; opacity is driven up to 0.92 and cleared by the existing visibility/opacity reset (12920-12922). Additive will read brighter — desired.

title: objectiveState.secondsInRelayRoom is always 0 (literal 'alarm_relay_room' never equals spec.roomId, which is the flow id 'bXX_alarm_relay')
description: _tickReinforcementTimers computes relaySec only when `spec.roomId === 'alarm_relay_room'`, but collectAlarmReinforcementSpecs sets spec.roomId = enc.room, and the alarm encounter's room is the FLOW id 'b01_alarm_relay' (not the floorplan-space id 'alarm_relay_room'). So the comparison never holds, relaySec stays 0, and objectiveState.secondsInRelayRoom is permanently 0. main.js:34395 reads it in _activeStoryObjectiveRuntime as `if(hold<=.001 && relaySec<=.05) return null;` — so the 'CUT ALARM' objective cue can only surface once the player is actively holding E, never from merely dwelling in the relay room as the dwell-based branch intends.
evidence: encounterDirector.js:769 `if (spec.roomId === 'alarm_relay_room') relaySec = Math.max(relaySec, acc);` vs campaignObjectives.js:14 `const roomId = enc.room;` and campaignEncounters.js:406-408 encounter room 'b01_alarm_relay'. `grep "'alarm_relay_room'"` in encounterDirector.js hits only line 769. Consumer: main.js:34395.
fix: Compare against the flow room id, not the floorplan literal. Replace the condition with a robust suffix test, e.g. `if (/_alarm_relay$/.test(String(spec.roomId))) relaySec = Math.max(relaySec, acc);` (covers b01..b12). Then the dwell-based objective prompt will appear when the player is in the relay room with the alarm live.
risk: Turns on an early objective HUD prompt that was previously suppressed — verify it does not double-fire with other objective cues. Trivial change; no save-compat impact.

title: def.lights `flicker` flag (and pend `flicker`) is stored but never animated — fakeCeilingLamps don't flicker
description: Per-building accent lights set userData {flicker:true, flickerPhase:…} when L.flicker is truthy (line 121) and push them through pushFakeAccent into fakeCeilingLamps. But the lighting controller (main.js:2309-2351) only reads F.position and F.color from fakeCeilingLamps for nearest-lamp chroma; it never reads flicker/flickerPhase/baseIntensity to modulate intensity. The actual flicker tick (main.js:44110-44114) operates on real THREE PointLights' .intensity, which fake lamps don't have. So the `flicker:true` entries in many def.lights (B1, B5, B6, B9, B10, B12) and `flicker` on pend lights produce no visible flicker from these accents.
evidence: const flick = L.flicker ? { flicker: true, flickerPhase: Math.random() * 10, sequenceDefLight: true } : { sequenceDefLight: true }; pushFakeAccent(ctx, x, y, z, col, baseIntensity, flick);  // flicker userData never consumed for fake lamps
fix: Either (a) drop the flicker plumbing from def.lights/pend to avoid implying an effect that doesn't fire, or (b) wire the lighting controller's tick to modulate the nearest fake lamp's effective intensity using F.userData.flicker/flickerPhase (add a small noise term to lampNear or pool intensity when the nearest fake lamp flickers). Option (b) is the AAA-positive choice for the medical/dock/subway 'failing fluorescent' mood.
risk: Option (b) touches the per-frame lighting tick (hot path) — keep it cheap (single sin/noise on the already-selected nearest lamp). Option (a) is zero-risk cleanup. Real ceiling PointLights still flicker, so current mood is only partially lost.

title: God-ray pass computes illuminationDecay per-sample but never weights samples by it (effect mostly discarded)
description: The radial-shaft loop accumulates illuminationDecay *= decay every iteration, but the per-sample contribution is `occ.rgb = min(occ.rgb, samp.rgb)` which ignores illuminationDecay entirely. illuminationDecay is only applied once, as a single scalar (decay^samples ~= 0.81 at 6 samples) to the final shafts. A real radial god-ray (Mitchell) sums per-sample texture contributions weighted by illuminationDecay; here samples are only min'd for occlusion, so the `decay` uniform is essentially a fixed dimming constant rather than a falloff. The shaft look is dominated by `weight` (driven to ~0.52 from reflectionProfile.rays at runtime) and the occlusion min, not the decay falloff it claims to implement.
fix: Either (a) accumulate proper shafts: `vec3 shaftAccum += samp.rgb * illuminationDecay;` and normalize by sample count, then use that instead of the occlusion-min approach; or (b) if the stylized occlusion-min look is intended, drop the per-sample `illuminationDecay *= decay` and the `decay` uniform to remove the misleading dead computation. Only enabled on high/ultra + volumetrics, so visible impact is limited.
risk: Changing to true accumulation alters the shaft look on high/ultra volumetric levels; should be tuned. Removing decay is zero-risk cosmetic cleanup. No build/probe impact.

title: God-ray density set by two competing formulas (configure vs tickPhotography) — tick silently wins
description: configure() sets godRayRuntime.uniforms.density from context.godRay (main.js _extrasForRenderStack supplies density = 0.32 + rays*0.48). tickPhotography() then sets the same uniform every frame from extras.godRayDensity (main.js supplies 0.3 + rays*0.45). Because tickPhotography runs each frame after configure, the configure value is immediately overwritten — the configure-time density write is dead and the two formulas disagree (0.32+0.48r vs 0.30+0.45r). Same pattern for weight.
evidence:
// configure(): godRayRuntime.uniforms.density.value = context.godRay.density;  (0.32+rays*0.48)
// tickPhotography(): godRayRuntime.uniforms.density.value = extras.godRayDensity; (0.3+rays*0.45)  // wins every frame
fix: Pick one owner. Easiest: drop the density/weight writes inside configure()'s godRay block (lines 950-953) since tickPhotography already drives them per-frame, or have main.js pass identical formulas in both call sites. Removes a confusing competing-write.
risk: None — final on-screen value is the tickPhotography one, unchanged. Cleanup only.

title: P._knifePairGrabPulse is set on the 'grab' beat and decayed each frame, but unlike sibling slice/impact/rip pulses it is never consumed for camera or viewmodel
description: _triggerKnifePairBeat sets P._knifePairGrabPulse=1 on the grab beat (line 13852) and _updateKnifePairRuntime decays it (line 14247). Its siblings P._knifePairSlicePulse/_knifePairImpactPulse/_knifePairRipPulse are all both set AND read at lines 14233-14235 (camera) and 14687-14689 (viewmodel). Grep shows _knifePairGrabPulse has only the write (13852) and the damp (14247) — no reader. The grab moment of the takedown therefore gets no dedicated camera/viewmodel pulse even though the code allocates and decays state for it; the grab reads weaker than intended.
fix: Mirror the slice pulse: where camera reads slicePulse (line 14234) and where the viewmodel reads slice (line 14688), add a small read of P._knifePairGrabPulse to add a brief inward camera dip / viewmodel anticipation on the grab. Keep coefficient ~half of slice's since grab is pre-impact.
risk: Low — adds a felt beat at the start of the takedown. Use small magnitude so it doesn't fight the bigger impact pulse milliseconds later. No save/build impact.

title: Cabinet drawer-pull loop comment says three, loop runs once
description: cabinet() comment reads 'Drawer pulls — three horizontal bumps' but the loop is `for(let i=0;i<1;i++)`, so exactly one pull row is drawn. The `i*.32` y-offset term is therefore always 0 and is dead. Either the loop bound was reduced (perf) and the comment/offset left stale, or it was meant to be 3. Visually the cabinets look bare vs the authored intent.
evidence:
// Drawer pulls — three horizontal bumps
    for(let i=0;i<1;i++){ box(x,WT+0.30+i*.32,z+(rotY?0:d/2-.01), .12,.04,.02, cabinetHdlM); ... }
fix: Decide intent: if three pulls are wanted, change to `for(let i=0;i<3;i++)` (the i*.32 offset then becomes live and the cabinets gain detail); if one is intended for perf, drop the loop and the stale comment. Recommend i<3 for the cheap visual gain.
risk: i<3 adds 4 tiny boxes per cabinet × 4 cabinets per non-B1 level. Negligible. Confirm no probe counts cabinet meshes.

title: Stun visor strobe is computed then immediately overwritten by the per-frame visor pulse
description: The _stunnedNow block sets this.visorM.emissive via setRGB(pulse*1.35,...) to give stunned enemies a distinct flickering visor (lines 9350-9353). But a few lines later the unconditional per-frame visor block (lines 10099-10114) recomputes visorM.emissive from this._visorBaseCol every frame regardless of stun state (line 10111). Because that block always runs after the stun block within the same _updateAnim call, the stun visor color is discarded and never appears on screen. The same applies to the sniper-overkill visorGlowM.opacity write at line 9392, which is overwritten by line 10112.
fix: Either delete the dead stun visor write (9350-9353), or make the per-frame visor block (10099) honor a stun override — e.g. add `else if(_stunnedNow){ ...white-hot stutter... }` ahead of the base pulse, or set a this._visorStunPulse value that the per-frame block reads and blends in. Simplest visible win: in the per-frame block add a stun term to `amp`/color when _stunnedNow is true so a stunned enemy actually flickers.
risk: Very low. Touches only emissive color of a cosmetic visor; no gameplay/save impact.

title: Directional key light (and hemi/ambient) get added to pulseLights and have their intensity modulated every frame
description: `pulseLights=ceilingLights.map(l=>({l,base:l.intensity||1,...}))` (line 38022) is built from `ceilingLights`, which includes the DirectionalLight key (37997), the HemisphereLight (37985) and the AmbientLight (37988) in addition to the GLB point lights. The tickDynProps pulse loop (38168-38176) then multiplies EVERY one of those by `base*(1+sin*amp)` each frame. The intent of pulseLights is clearly to flicker room/alarm point lights, not the global sun/fill. Today amp is only .06 so it's barely visible, but once shadows are enabled on the key light (see megaplex-no-shadows-flat) the entire scene's directional shadows and exposure will visibly shimmer at ~1.3Hz, and the hemi/ambient fill will breathe — an unintended global flicker.
evidence: const pulseLights=ceilingLights.map(l=>({l,base:l.intensity||1,phase:Math.random()*Math.PI*2})); ... for(const p of pulseLights){ ... p.l.intensity=p.base*(1+Math.sin(t*(alarm?5.2:1.3)+p.phase)*amp); }
fix: Build pulseLights only from point lights / room lights, e.g. `const pulseLights=ceilingLights.filter(l=>l&&l.isPointLight).map(...)`, or skip non-point lights inside the loop with `if(!p.l.isPointLight)continue;`. This isolates the flicker to room/alarm point lights and keeps the key/fill stable.
risk: Behavioral: hemi/ambient/key stop pulsing (desired). No save/perf impact. Low risk.

title: WEAPON_UNLOCK_GATES + isWeaponUnlocked is a dead second source of weapon-unlock truth that disagrees with the authoritative WEAPONS table
description: WEAPON_UNLOCK_GATES hardcodes idx0=M4A1 removed, idx1/2 always, idx3..7 gated by building number, and isWeaponUnlocked(idx) gates on PROGRESS._maxBuildingCleared. But the authoritative playable-weapon source is src/data/weapons.js (PLAYABLE_WEAPON_INDICES derived from WEAPONS[i].removed/.playable). isWeaponUnlocked() has NO callers (grep confirms), so this gate table is inert — yet it encodes a parallel, easily-drifting unlock policy (e.g. it asserts M4 idx0 removed while isPlayableWeaponIdx(0) is used as 'playable' at main.js:18808). Classic duplicate-config that will silently rot.
evidence: 0:{removed:true,name:'M4A1'} ... function isWeaponUnlocked(idx){...return (PROGRESS._maxBuildingCleared||0)>=gate.building;}  // grep isWeaponUnlocked => def only. Authoritative: weapons.js PLAYABLE_WEAPON_INDICES=WEAPONS.map(...!w.removed...).
fix: Delete WEAPON_UNLOCK_GATES + isWeaponUnlocked, or derive the gate names/states from the WEAPONS table at runtime instead of a hand-maintained literal so it cannot disagree. If a real unlock-gate UI is desired, have isWeaponUnlocked delegate to isPlayableWeaponIdx for base playability.
risk: None if deleted (dead). If kept and wired, ensure it doesn't override weapons.js gating — keep weapons.js authoritative.

title: Four competing difficulty tables with disagreeing values
description: DIFFICULTY_MODIFIERS (30864) says lethal enemyDamage:1.85; DIFF_DESCRIPTIONS (31669) says lethal mul:2.0; DIFF_HP_MUL (30974) lethal 1.65; the live damage scale _difficultyDamageScale (37124) uses 1.85; the live score scales use 1.45 (35202), 2.0 (36996), 1.85 (38463). The three tables in this scope (DIFFICULTY_MODIFIERS, DIFF_HP_MUL, DIFF_DESCRIPTIONS) are never read by gameplay and disagree with each other and with the live inline literals. Pure dead/contradictory metadata that will mislead future edits and any UI that reads DIFF_DESCRIPTIONS.
evidence: 30879 `enemyHp:1.65,enemyDamage:1.85,...` vs 31672 `lethal:{...mul:2.0}` vs 30974 `DIFF_HP_MUL={normal:1.0,hard:1.30,lethal:1.65}` vs 37124 `{normal:1.0,hard:1.25,lethal:1.85}`.
fix: Collapse to a single difficulty config object that the live code (_difficultyDamageScale, enemy hp scaling, score) reads from, and delete the unused DIFFICULTY_MODIFIERS/DIFF_DESCRIPTIONS/DIFF_HP_MUL duplicates. If a difficulty-select UI needs descriptions, point it at the single source.
risk: Low if you only delete the unread tables. If you unify and re-point live code, re-balance and re-verify probes.

title: TUTORIAL_SEQ / TUTOR / tickTutorialHints is a third, dead tutorial system overlapping ONBOARD
description: There are three onboarding systems: ONBOARD/tickOnboard (gated on PROGRESS.seenTutorialOnboard, actually ticked at 41612), the interactive TUTORIAL_STEPS/tickTutorial (gated on PROGRESS._tutorialSeen, ticked at 41614), and TUTORIAL_SEQ/TUTOR/tickTutorialHints (30807-30851). tickTutorialHints is never called and also reads PROGRESS.seenTutorialOnboard (the ONBOARD flag) — so even if called it would be suppressed once ONBOARD completes. It writes to the same #onboard-card element ONBOARD uses, which would conflict if both ran. It is pure dead, redundant code that can mislead future edits about which tutorial is authoritative.
evidence: 30828 `function tickTutorialHints(){ if(!TUTOR.active||PROGRESS.seenTutorialOnboard)return; ...}` no caller; targets `$e('onboard-card')` (30843) which is also driven by tickOnboard (32611).
fix: Delete TUTORIAL_SEQ, TUTOR, and tickTutorialHints (30807-30851). Keep ONBOARD (the live one) and the interactive TUTORIAL_STEPS path. Confirms no caller before deleting.
risk: Low. Removing dead code; verify no probe references TUTORIAL_SEQ/TUTOR.

title: Radial 'slow time while picking' is saved but never applied or restored
description: openRadial comments 'Slow time slightly while picking' and stores P._radialPrevScale=P.timeScale, but it never lowers P.timeScale, and closeRadial never reads _radialPrevScale back. The effect is computed (saved) then discarded — the radial does not slow time at all.
evidence: 31404 `// Slow time slightly while picking` 31405 `P._radialPrevScale=P.timeScale;` — grep shows _radialPrevScale is never read again; P.timeScale is never set in open/closeRadial.
fix: If desired, set P.timeScale to e.g. 0.35 in openRadial and restore `P.timeScale=P._radialPrevScale||1` in closeRadial. Otherwise delete the dead _radialPrevScale line. (Lower priority than making the radial clickable at all — see radial-menu-unusable-pointerlock.)
risk: Low. Touching timeScale interacts with focus/killcam time systems (26970/27014); restore carefully so it does not stick.

title: _checkLieuIntro, showLieutenantDeath, _maybeBarkOnAlert, getZoneName, showOperatorDetails are defined but never called
description: Several flavor helpers in scope are dead: _checkLieuIntro (30690) is never called (showLieutenantIntro IS, from 31694 inside it, but the gate fn itself never runs); showLieutenantDeath (31707) never called; _maybeBarkOnAlert (31726) never called; getZoneName/ZONE_NAMES (31560) never called; showOperatorDetails (31735) never called. These are not bugs, but they are unwired content (lieutenant death quotes, zone-clear names, operator detail panel) that the player never sees, and they bloat the contradiction surface.
evidence: grep callers: showLieutenantDeath, _maybeBarkOnAlert, getZoneName, showOperatorDetails, _checkLieuIntro all return zero non-definition matches.
fix: Wire the high-value ones: call showLieutenantDeath(G.building) when a lieutenant dies (alongside the existing death flow), call getZoneName on zone clear for a flavor banner, and add a menu button to showOperatorDetails. Delete the rest if not wanted. Each is content the team already wrote but isn't surfaced.
risk: Low. Adding calls surfaces existing content; verify the lieutenant-death hook fires once.

title: transitionSnapThreshold (1.35) makes the pose-snap detector unable to ever fire; stale 0.62 fallback disagrees
description: ANIMATION_FEEL_TUNING.locomotion.transitionSnapThreshold is 1.35. updatePlayerAnimTransitionHealth (playerAnimation.js line 99) compares the per-frame max resolved pose delta against `tuning.transitionSnapThreshold || 0.62`. Resolved camera/viewmodel/proxy values are tiny (typ. 0.01-0.2 rad/units; even large dropkick terms stay < ~0.3), so a single-frame delta can never reach 1.35. Therefore health.snapCount / lastSnapFrame are permanently 0 — the transition-snap diagnostic is dead. The inline `|| 0.62` fallback is also stale: it disagrees with the live 1.35 value and never executes because tuning.transitionSnapThreshold is always defined. The feel smoke probe asserts snapCount===0 (player-animation-feel-smoke.mjs lines 149/158), so the disabled detector is what keeps the test trivially green.
evidence: profiles.js: transitionSnapThreshold: 1.35  |  playerAnimation.js line 99: if (delta.maxDelta > (tuning.transitionSnapThreshold || 0.62)) { health.snapCount = ... }  |  resolved pose magnitudes are sub-0.3, so delta.maxDelta >> 1.35 is impossible.
fix: Lower transitionSnapThreshold in profiles.js to a value in the actual pose-delta range (e.g. 0.35-0.5) so genuine pose pops are caught, OR explicitly document/remove the detector. Also delete the dead `|| 0.62` fallback in playerAnimation.js line 99 since the tuning key is always present. Diagnostic-only change — verify player-animation-feel-smoke.mjs still passes (it should under normal locomotion if threshold ~0.4).
risk: Telemetry-only; no gameplay/visual effect. If threshold is lowered too far the smoke probe's snapCount===0 asserts could start failing during sprint start/stop — pick a threshold validated against the probe before committing.

title: 'braceDip' listed in bodyCarryWeight scaleKeys but absent from zeroAdditives().camera — silent no-op
description: applyFinalLocomotionTuning scales camera keys including 'braceDip' by tuning.bodyCarryWeight (line 161). However zeroAdditives().camera (lines 60-84) does not contain a braceDip field, and scaleKeys only multiplies keys whose value is typeof 'number' (line 152), so the braceDip entry is skipped — a dead reference. The player-animation braceDip (playerAnimation.js line 983, consumed in main.js line 42827 as _pa0.braceDip) is therefore never given any bodyCarryWeight scaling from the feel layer. Harmless, but it signals the scaleKeys list drifted out of sync with the additive schema.
evidence: locomotionFeelController.js line 161: scaleKeys(addv.camera, ['headBobX','headBobY','headPitch','headRoll','accelLagX','accelLagZ','braceDip'], tuning.bodyCarryWeight);  |  zeroAdditives().camera (lines 60-84) has no braceDip key.
fix: Remove 'braceDip' from the scaleKeys list at line 161 (it does nothing), OR if braceDip is meant to be a feel additive, add `braceDip: 0` to zeroAdditives().camera and emit it in updateLocomotionFeelState. Given braceDip is currently a player-anim-only camera term, removing it from the list is the safe cleanup.
risk: None — currently a no-op; either edit is behavior-neutral.

title: cam.dropkickYaw assigned in resolvePlayerAnimLayers but not declared in createPlayerAnimState resolved.camera schema
description: resolvePlayerAnimLayers writes cam.dropkickYaw (line 929) and it IS consumed in main.js (line 42952: camera.rotation.y += _pa0.dropkickYaw||0), so it functions. But the field is missing from the resolved.camera initializer in createPlayerAnimState (lines 235-271), unlike every neighboring dropkick* field (dropkickPitch/Roll/Dip/Forward are declared). On frame 0 before resolvePlayerAnimLayers runs, _pa0.dropkickYaw is undefined; main.js guards with `||0` so no crash, and the locomotion feel layer has no dropkickYaw additive so nothing else touches it. This is a schema/contradiction smell (the snapshot/health-diff code in copyPoseSnapshot iterates only over present keys, so dropkickYaw is excluded from transition-health pose-delta accounting) rather than a live bug.
evidence: playerAnimation.js line 929: cam.dropkickYaw = dropkickTwirlSide * (...);  |  createPlayerAnimState resolved.camera (lines 235-271) declares dropkickPitch, dropkickRoll, dropkickDip, dropkickForward but NOT dropkickYaw.
fix: Add `dropkickYaw: 0,` to the resolved.camera initializer in createPlayerAnimState (near line 256, alongside the other dropkick* fields) so the schema is complete and transition-health pose-delta accounting includes it.
risk: None — purely adds an initial 0 field; main.js already defends with ||0. No save-compat impact.

title: traverse_objective and objective trigger branches execute identical code (duplicate branch)
description: In the director-trigger handling, `trigger.type === 'traverse_objective'` (378-380) and `trigger.type === 'objective'` (381-383) run byte-identical bodies: completeTextForObjective + enqueue with the same key shape. Both director trigger types are real (encounterDirector emits 'traverse_objective' at line 739 and 'objective' at line 861), so this isn't unreachable, but the two branches are redundant and could collapse to one condition. Minor maintainability/contradiction smell, not a runtime bug.
evidence: Lines 378-383: `} else if (trigger.type === 'traverse_objective') { const c = completeTextForObjective(cues, trigger.id); enqueueCue(...:complete`); } else if (trigger.type === 'objective') { const c = completeTextForObjective(cues, trigger.id); enqueueCue(...:complete`); }` — identical.
fix: Collapse to `} else if (trigger.type === 'traverse_objective' || trigger.type === 'objective') { ... }`.
risk: None functional. Pure dedup.

title: WEAPONS fields recoilZ, breathHold, adsTimeMul are defined but never read
description: Several per-weapon tuning fields look load-bearing but are never consumed: recoilZ (all weapons) has zero readers in src/; recoilX is read ONLY to compute a cosmetic HUD label (main.js:32513 recoilLabel), not actual recoil — recoil is driven by shX/shY. breathHold:.4 on the AWM (idx 7) is never read as W.breathHold (the breathHold matches in main.js are an unrelated local 'knife-pair-tension' variable). adsTimeMul:.85 on the P226 (idx 6) has zero readers anywhere. These give a false impression that tuning these numbers changes feel.
evidence: grep over src/ (excluding weapons.js): `recoilZ` -> 0 hits; `recoilX` -> only main.js:32513 `const recoilLabel=w.recoilX>=.10?'HIGH':...`; `adsTimeMul` -> only the weapons.js definition; W.breathHold -> 0 hits (main.js:13451+ use a local `breathHold` from knife tension, not the weapon field).
fix: Either delete the unused fields (recoilZ everywhere, breathHold on AWM, adsTimeMul on P226) to remove the false tuning surface, OR wire them: e.g. multiply ADS lerp duration by W.adsTimeMul where ADS speed is computed, fold recoilZ into the per-shot camera/gun roll, and apply W.breathHold to sniper hold-breath steadiness. No-op-cleanup is the lowest risk.
risk: Very low if deleting (fields are unread, so nothing changes at runtime). Save compat unaffected (these are static defaults, not persisted). If wiring them instead, that changes feel and needs tuning.

title: COMPANION_PONG and HOST_DRONE_FRAME protocol constants are never used
description: COMPANION_MESSAGES.COMPANION_PONG ('companion:pong', protocol.js:14) and COMPANION_MESSAGES.HOST_DRONE_FRAME ('host:droneFrame', protocol.js:7) are declared but referenced nowhere in client.js, relay.js or main.js. Ping/pong is implemented entirely via RELAY_PING/RELAY_PONG, and drone video frames are sent as raw binary (ArrayBuffer) through the relay's binary forwarding, never as a HOST_DRONE_FRAME message. Additionally the relay emits RELAY_ERROR (relay.js:156,183) but neither client.js onMessage nor main.js _companionOnMessage handle it, so relay errors are silently dropped on both ends.
evidence: grep `COMPANION_MESSAGES.COMPANION_PONG` -> 0 hits; `COMPANION_MESSAGES.HOST_DRONE_FRAME` -> 0 hits across src/. Drone frame path: main.js:22285-22288 sends `blob.arrayBuffer().then(buf=>_companionSendBinary(buf))`; relay.js:173-178 forwards binary host->companion; client.js:455-457 decodes ArrayBuffer as image/webp. RELAY_ERROR handled by neither client.js (no branch in onMessage 454-493) nor main.js (_companionHandleCommand default:break, 21865).
fix: Remove the two unused constants (COMPANION_PONG, HOST_DRONE_FRAME) from COMPANION_MESSAGES to keep the protocol honest, OR, if you want diagnostics, add a client.js onMessage branch for RELAY_ERROR that surfaces msg.reason in the status pill (setStatus('error', msg.reason)). Pure cleanup; no runtime behavior depends on either constant.
risk: Very low. Constants are unreferenced; removing them cannot affect runtime. Adding a RELAY_ERROR handler is additive and isolated to the companion client.

title: Muzzle-spill color branch for weaponIdx===0 (M4) is unreachable
description: spawnAaaMuzzleWorldSpill picks the flash color from weaponIdx, including `wi === 0 ? 0xffe8cc`. weaponIdx 0 is the removed M4A1 (weapons.js: playable:false, removed:true) and is never a live player weapon, so that color branch (and the `wi === 3 ? 1.15 : 1` peak boost only applies to the shotgun which is fine). Minor: the wi===0 ternary arm and its peak multiplier path are dead.
evidence: aaaPresence.js:17-18 `const col = wi === 3 ? 0xffaa66 : wi === 7 ? 0xffddcc : wi === 0 ? 0xffe8cc : 0xffcc88;` Caller main.js:26225 passes `weaponIdx:pl.weaponIdx`; player weaponIdx is always in PLAYABLE_WEAPON_INDICES = [1..7], never 0.
fix: Drop the `wi === 0 ? 0xffe8cc :` arm (fold into the default), or, if a warmer rifle-style flash is wanted for the MK14 marksman (idx 5) / DMR, retarget the color to a live index. Cosmetic-only cleanup.
risk: Very low. The branch never executes today; removing it does not change any visible flash color.

title: _encPatrolAlarm and _encPatrolRoute flags are set but never read (write-only behavior flags)
description: applyEncounterEnemySpec sets enemy._encPatrolAlarm=true for behavior 'patrol_then_alarm' (line 76) and enemy._encPatrolRoute=true for behavior 'patrol_route' (line 96). Neither flag is read anywhere in the codebase (grep finds only these two writes). 'patrol_then_alarm' is the default fallback behavior assigned to custom-map authored enemies (main.js:12512), so this is reachable but inert — the 'alarm on patrol contact' intent the name implies is not implemented. (Note tickEncounterEnemyIntent has no 'patrol_then_alarm' or 'patrol_route' case; the only effect of those behaviors today is the peekRate bump at line 62.)
evidence: encounterBehavior.js:76 `enemy._encPatrolAlarm = true;` and :96 `enemy._encPatrolRoute = true;`. `grep -rn '_encPatrolAlarm|_encPatrolRoute' src` returns only encounterBehavior.js (no readers in main.js).
fix: If patrol-then-alarm is desired (cheap tension beat): add a tickEncounterEnemyIntent branch — when _encPatrolAlarm and the enemy in PATROL/SEARCH gains line-of-sight/lastKnownPos, trigger the existing alarm path (G.levelState.alarm / a bark) once. Otherwise delete the two dead flag writes.

title: BASE_PATROL_ROUTES entries 'fe_compression_loop' and 'spine_doorline' are never referenced by any encounter spec
description: The 7 BASE_PATROL_ROUTES are looked up via enemy.encounterPatrolTag (set from spec.patrol). Only intake_center_beat, drum_lateral, cage_left_arc, cage_right_shuffle, catwalk_window_beat are used by the B01 catalog (which B02-B12 inherit verbatim, see patrol-retag-namespace-mismatch). evidence: campaignEncounters.js patrol tags in use: intake_center_beat(373), drum_lateral(451), cage_left_arc(477), cage_right_shuffle(501), catwalk_window_beat(513). `grep "patrol: '"` shows no fe_compression_loop or spine_doorline. encounterPatrolRoutes.js:6-23 defines both.

title: hologramVisualVersionBundle() is exported but never imported or called
description: hologramVisualVersionBundle (lines 7-15) returns a static object of version strings. It is not in main.js's import-from-hologramVisuals block (lines 315-329, which alias the actually-used helpers) and a project-wide grep finds zero call sites.
