evidence: export function hologramVisualVersionBundle() {...} at line 7; grep 'hologramVisualVersionBundle' over src/main.js returns 0 matches.
fix: No action required for runtime. If trimming dead exports, delete the function. Otherwise leave as a harmless version manifest.
risk: None. Unused export; removal cannot affect runtime, build, or saves.

title: Element builders `spine`, `offsetRoom`, and `containerrow` are defined but never referenced
description: ELEMENT_BUILDERS.spine (line 1538), ELEMENT_BUILDERS.offsetRoom (line 1957), and ELEMENT_BUILDERS.containerrow (line 1588) are never used by any SEQUENCE_DEFS / EXTRA_ELEMENTS / ROUTE_COMPLETION table (verified by enumerating all `t:'…'` values vs defined builders). `gate` is used internally by `turnstiles`, so it is NOT dead. These three are harmless library functions but are pure dead weight in the bundle.
evidence: DEFINED-but-unused builders: containerrow, offsetRoom, spine (gate is used by turnstiles, so excluded).
fix: Either remove them, or keep them as an authoring kit and add a brief '// authoring kit (currently unreferenced)' comment so a future cleanup pass doesn't mistake them for live code. No urgency.
risk: Removal is safe (no references). Keeping them costs only a few KB. No save-compat/perf concern.

title: TAA scene-pass path is hard-disabled (useTaaBase=false), leaving an entire TAA configure branch unreachable
description: useTaaBase is a const literal false, so passes.scenePassKind is always 'render' and passes.render is never a TAARenderPass. Consequently the whole TAA configuration block in configure() (taaDesired computation lines 1008-1016 and the `if (passes.render && passes.scenePassKind === 'taa')` block lines 1017-1030) is dead. taaDesired is always false, which also makes the `!taaDesired` SMAA guard a no-op. This is intentional per the comment (TAA trips r170 missing-uniform edge cases on transient VFX materials) but the dead branch and the unused TAARenderPass import/param add noise and risk of future re-wiring confusion.
fix: Leave behavior as-is (TAA is deliberately off), but optionally collapse the dead TAA configure branch to a comment, or keep useTaaBase as a documented kill-switch. No functional change needed; flagging so an editor doesn't 'optimize' the false constant away and accidentally re-enable the unstable TAA path.
risk: None if untouched. Re-enabling TAA would risk the r170 uniform crashes the comment warns about — do NOT flip useTaaBase without revalidating VFX material uniforms.

title: GTAO enable guard tests q !== 'medium-low', a quality tier that never exists
description: passes.gtao.enabled is gated by `q !== 'medium-low'`, but the quality domain in main.js is strictly low/medium/high/ultra (SETTINGS.quality||'high' everywhere). 'medium-low' is never a value, so the guard is always true and never disables GTAO as apparently intended. Harmless today but the guard silently does nothing.
evidence: passes.gtao.enabled = postEnabled && aoQuality !== 'off' && q !== 'medium-low';
fix: Remove the dead `&& q !== 'medium-low'` clause, or if the intent was to disable GTAO on the 'medium' base quality, change it to `q !== 'medium'` / `q !== 'low'` to match real tiers. Cosmetic correctness only.
risk: If changed to a real tier, GTAO would actually disable on that tier (perf gain, AO loss) — verify intent before changing. Removing the clause is zero-risk. No build/probe impact.

title: blackFrameSelfTest teardown calls dispose() on lights, which is a no-op for AmbientLight/DirectionalLight
description: The self-test cleanup traverses the scene and calls o.dispose() for o.isLight. Three.js base Light and AmbientLight/DirectionalLight do not implement dispose() (only some lights like RectAreaLight do), so this branch never frees anything. It is harmless (guarded by typeof === 'function') but signals a misunderstanding; the geometries/materials it explicitly disposes are the only real resources, and those are handled.
fix: No action required for correctness. Optionally remove the light-dispose traversal to reduce noise, since the self-test scene's lights are GC'd with the local scene. Lights hold no GPU resources here.
risk: None.

title: P._knifePairTensionPulse is recomputed and damped every cinematic frame but is never read — wasted per-frame work
description: _updateKnifePairRuntime computes P._knifePairTensionPulse via a clamp over tension.wristLock/counterForce/bladeScrape and runs it through damp() every frame while the knife-pair cinematic is active. Grep across all of src/ shows this is the only reference: it is written and decayed but never sampled by camera, viewmodel, HUD, or enemy logic. It is computed-then-discarded state — harmless but pure dead work each frame of the takedown.
evidence: P._knifePairTensionPulse=damp(Math.max(Number.isFinite(P._knifePairTensionPulse)?P._knifePairTensionPulse:0,THREE.MathUtils.clamp((tension.wristLock||0)*.34+(tension.counterForce||0)*.22+(tension.bladeScrape||0)*.18,0,1)),0,8.5,dt);  // line 14251 — no reader anywhere
fix: Either delete line 14251 (zero behavioral change) or wire it into the camera/viewmodel — e.g. add a subtle handheld micro-shake while the blade is locked: in the pair camera block (~14237-14239) add a tiny side*tensionPulse*.004 jitter to cameraRoll. Wiring it would make the 'struggle' visibly read on screen, which is on-theme for this subsystem.
risk: Deletion is zero-risk. Wiring it in must use a very small coefficient or it competes with the existing impact/rip pulse camera kicks during the most camera-busy moment.

title: pair.strikeHand / pair.bladeTip are written every frame but never read; only the prev* copies are used
description: _updateKnifePairContactRig writes four Vector3 clones at end of frame: pair.strikeHand, pair.bladeTip (14100-14101) and pair.prevStrikeHand, pair.prevBladeTip (14102-14103). Only the prev* pair is read (the one-frame-lag motion-blur ghost at lines 13957-13962). Grep confirms pair.strikeHand and pair.bladeTip have no readers. Lines 14100-14101 are two extra Vector3 allocations per cinematic frame for no effect — minor GC churn during the takedown.
evidence:
pair.strikeHand=strikeHand.clone();   // line 14100 — no reader
pair.bladeTip=bladeTip.clone();        // line 14101 — no reader
pair.prevStrikeHand=strikeHand.clone();// line 14102 — read at 13958/13960 next frame
pair.prevBladeTip=bladeTip.clone();    // line 14103 — read at 13958/13961 next frame
fix: Delete lines 14100-14101. The prev* assignments (14102-14103) are the ones actually feeding the ghost trail and must stay. Saves two Vector3 allocations/frame during takedowns.
risk: Zero behavioral risk if only 14100-14101 are removed and nothing later in the same frame relies on them (confirmed none do). Build/save unaffected.

title: _skylineTex is defined but never referenced (superseded by _skylineTexB / _skylinePerBuilding)
description: The original single-palette night-city _skylineTex (lines 876-918) is allocated at module load (creates a 256x256 canvas + CanvasTexture) but is never used anywhere in the codebase. grep for `_skylineTex\b` returns only its own definition. The live per-building skylines are generated by _skylineTexB (line 1344) and _skylineTexBExt (line 1413) and stored in _skylinePerBuilding (line 1598). The dead version also harbors the rgba precedence bug above.
evidence: grep -n '_skylineTex\\b' src/main.js -> only line 876 (the definition).
fix: Delete lines 876-918. Frees the eager canvas/texture allocation and removes the buggy code path.
risk: None — confirmed unreferenced.

title: Header comment says light intensities are 'multiplied by π' but the actual boost is 1.82
description: The file header (lines 4-5) documents 'light intensities multiplied by π to match r128 pre-physical brightness'. The real implementation uses const _LIGHT_BOOST=1.82 (line 456), and the inline comment there explicitly says the π boost was abandoned because it blew out PBR materials. The header is stale and contradicts the live constant, which can mislead anyone reasoning about scene brightness/exposure tuning (the value materially affects how bright every authored light renders). Verified only a single boost is applied (no double-multiply).
evidence: header: '- light intensities multiplied by π to match r128's pre-physical brightness'   vs   line 456: const _LIGHT_BOOST = 1.82;  // comment: 'The old π boost made every authored source feel like a blown-out work light'
fix: Update the header comment line 5 to reference the 1.82 bridge factor (or drop the specific value and say 'a smaller bridge factor').
risk: None — comment-only.

title: addWindow computes unused `inset` variable
description: `const fT=.04,inset=faceDir.includes('x')?.0:.0;` — `inset` is always 0 (both branches .0) and is never referenced after declaration. Dead code / leftover of an abandoned inset attempt.
evidence: const fT=.04,inset=faceDir.includes('x')?.0:.0;
fix: Remove `,inset=faceDir.includes('x')?.0:.0` leaving `const fT=.04;`.
risk: None.

title: Dead legacy B01 block redeclares fM, shadowing the level floor material name
description: Inside the `if(bn===1&&legacyB01ProceduralDressing)` block (legacyB01ProceduralDressing is hard-coded false at line 2425, so the whole block is unreachable) there is `const fM=new THREE.MeshPhongMaterial({color:0xd0a020,...})` for the forklift, reusing the same identifier as the level floor material `const fM=_aaMat(floorKind,...)` declared at line 2779. The forklift fM is block-scoped so it does not corrupt the outer fM, but this is dead code (gated false) plus a confusing name collision. The whole legacy block (3750-3826) and the matching Sifu/debris legacy blocks (3336-3420 partly, 3907-3920) can never execute.
evidence: const legacyB01ProceduralDressing=false; (line 2425) ... if(bn===1&&legacyB01ProceduralDressing){ ... const fM=new THREE.MeshPhongMaterial({color:0xd0a020,shininess:30,specular:0x303030}); ... }
fix: Either delete the legacyB01ProceduralDressing-gated dead branches entirely (they are confirmed unreachable and B1 now uses applySequenceLayout + per-building verticality), or if kept for reference, rename the inner forklift material (e.g. fLiftM) to avoid the fM collision. Lower risk: leave behavior, just remove the dead branches to cut ~120 lines of confusion.
risk: Deleting dead code: confirm no other code references symbols defined only inside those blocks (none escape — all local). Build/probes unaffected since the branch never ran.

title: Visor base-color cache constructs a Color from visorM.color then immediately .copy() overwrites it
description: Line 10110 lazily caches `this._visorBaseCol = new THREE.Color(this.visorM.color).copy(this.visorGlowM.color)`. The `new THREE.Color(this.visorM.color)` constructor argument is pointless because `.copy(this.visorGlowM.color)` overwrites every channel on the next call in the same expression. The cached base ends up being the visorGlow color, not a blend — confusing and a wasted constructor read. Cosmetically the visor still pulses correctly so there is no visible bug, just dead/misleading code computed once per enemy.
evidence: const ts=this._visorBaseCol||(this._visorBaseCol=new THREE.Color(this.visorM.color).copy(this.visorGlowM.color));  // line 10110
fix: Drop the no-op argument: `this._visorBaseCol=new THREE.Color().copy(this.visorGlowM.color)` (or `this.visorGlowM.color.clone()`). If the intent was actually to blend visor + glow hues, do it explicitly with .lerp; otherwise the clone is the honest form.
risk: Zero behavioral change (cached value is identical); trivial. No perf or save concern.

title: Alive-path headshot hit-stop (dt slowdown) is unreachable because every headshot is fatal
description: takeDamage sets this.hp=isHead?0:... unconditionally (line 7904), and when hp<=0 it calls this.die() synchronously (line 8101) which sets this.dead=true. _headshotHitStopTimer is only ever set inside the if(isHead) block (line 8060). Therefore on the next frame update() always takes the if(this.dead){...return} branch at line 11186, and the alive headshot hit-stop block at 11187-11194 (which scales dt to slow the living enemy) can never execute. The death-side hit-stop in _updateDeath (line 10128) is the one that actually runs. The alive block is dead.
evidence:
this.hp=isHead?0:this.hp-dmg;            // 7904 — headshot always hp=0
...
if(this.hp<=0){this.die();return true;}   // 8101 — die() sets dead=true
...
if(this.dead){this.deathTimer+=dt;this._updateDeath(dt);return null;}  // 11186 — taken first
if(this._headshotHitStopTimer>0){ ... dt*=... }  // 11187 — never reached for headshots
fix: Remove the unreachable block at 11187-11194 to reduce confusion, OR (if a non-fatal headshot hit-stop is desired, e.g. for bosses/armored heads) introduce a real non-fatal headshot path so the block can run. As-is it is pure dead code.
risk: None if removed (unreachable). If instead enabling non-fatal headshots, that is a balance/gameplay change and out of scope for a surgical fix.

title: _shotRecoverTimer is written/decremented every frame but never read
description: this._shotRecoverTimer is initialized (line 6389), decremented each frame (line 8357), and set on fire (line 10916 in _markShotVisual), but it is never read anywhere. The actual shoot-recoil animation is driven entirely by this.shootRecoilTimer (lines 9447-9472). _shotRecoverTimer is a leftover/competing timer that does nothing — a state-desync where one timer (shootRecoilTimer) is the live one and a parallel one (_shotRecoverTimer) is dead.
evidence:
this._shotRecoverTimer=Math.max(0,(this._shotRecoverTimer||0)-dt);  // 8357 (no reader)
// _shotRecoverDur IS read (9448), but _shotRecoverTimer is not
fix: Delete the three references to _shotRecoverTimer (6389 init, 8357 decrement, 10916 set) to remove the dead per-frame work, OR wire shootRecoilTimer's reads to it if a unification was intended. Keep _shotRecoverDur and _shotRecoverSide (those are read).
risk: None. Removing a write-only field has no behavioral effect.

title: `if(!k.alive)` lifetime-expiry branch in updateKnives is unreachable
description: A knife only gets alive=false in _stickKnifeAtSurface (which also sets stuck=true) and _startKnifeReturn (which sets returning=true). updateKnives checks k.returning (19969) then k.stuck (20069) BEFORE reaching the `if(!k.alive)` branch at 20127. There is no code path that produces a knife with alive=false AND stuck=false AND returning=false, so this branch — including the `k.stuckLifetime||3.5` fallback expiry — can never execute. (Stuck knives also set stuckLifetime=Infinity at 19789, so even if reached the timer would never trip.)
evidence: k.alive=false assignments only at 19789 (`k.alive=false;k.stuck=true;...`) and 19802 (`k.alive=false;...k.returning=true;`). Dead branch: `if(!k.alive){ k.age+=dt; if(k.age>(k.stuckLifetime||3.5)){scene.remove(k.grp);...G.knives.splice(i,1);} continue; }`.
fix: Either delete the dead branch (lines 20127-20131) to remove confusion, or — if a thrown knife is ever intended to despawn after a timeout when it neither sticks nor returns — wire a real path that sets alive=false with stuck/returning both false. As-is it is harmless but misleading dead code.
risk: Removing it is safe (branch never runs). If kept, no functional effect. Don't add a real despawn path without confirming desired behavior — that WOULD change gameplay.

title: TK_VIEW_MESHES const is assigned but never read
description: `const TK_VIEW_MESHES=KNIFE_SLOT_REMOVED?[]:_buildKnifeMesh(throwGrp);` keeps the array of viewmodel knife meshes returned by _buildKnifeMesh, but the const is never referenced anywhere else in the file. Only the side effect of _buildKnifeMesh (attaching meshes to throwGrp) is used. The binding is dead state.
evidence: grep TK_VIEW_MESHES across src/main.js returns exactly one hit: the declaration on line 19534. No reads.
fix: Drop the binding and keep the side effect: `if(!KNIFE_SLOT_REMOVED)_buildKnifeMesh(throwGrp);`. Purely cosmetic / clarity. Leave as-is if minimizing diff; harmless.
risk: Negligible. Removing an unread const cannot change behavior.

title: MELEE comment claims a 4-hit combo chain but code implements a 2-hit chain
description: The MELEE state object comment at line 13326 says '// 4-hit combo chain', and four combo pips (cd0..cd3) plus four authored slash animations exist, but doMelee only ever produces a 0->1 light chain (plus heavy=3). The data structure, UI, and four animation cases are sized for 4 hits while the driver logic was cut to 2. This is the root cause of the overhead-slam dead code above.
evidence:
13326: // 4-hit combo chain
14271: MELEE.comboCount=(elapsed<MELEE.COMBO_WINDOW)?((MELEE.comboCount+1)%2):0;
fix: Either restore the intended N-hit chain at 14271 (see melee-overhead-slam-dead-code) or update the comment to '// 2-hit light chain + heavy stab' so future readers don't assume cd2/cd3 and the s===2/s===3 animations are reachable from light attacks.
risk: Comment-only change has zero runtime risk.

title: Adaptive AO/bloom/phase2 stepping calls _configureRenderStack() whose output is discarded under STABLE_RENDERING_MODE
description: _tickPerfAdaptive (called every frame at 41567) steps bloomHeldOff, aoAdaptiveSteps, and phase2*Held flags and calls _configureRenderStack() (15072,15075,15077,15084,15101) to reconfigure composer passes. Because STABLE_RENDERING_MODE forces the composer off (see post-stack-disabled-stable-mode) AND _forceStableVisualSettings already pins aoQuality/bloomQuality to off, this reconfiguration produces no visible change — the effect is computed then discarded. The pixel-scale branch (pendingPixelScale -> applyQuality at 15113) DOES still take effect (pixel ratio), so only the AO/bloom/phase2 stack-reconfig work is wasted, costing CPU traversal in createRenderSubsystem.configure for no output.
fix: Guard the stack-reconfig branches with `if(!STABLE_RENDERING_MODE)` (or early-return the AO/bloom/phase2 stepping under stable mode) while keeping the pixel-scale path live, so the governor only does the work that affects output. If the post stack is re-enabled per the previous finding, this becomes live work and the guard should be removed.
risk: Skipping reconfig in stable mode is safe today since output is discarded; only revisit if STABLE mode is relaxed. Keep the pixel-scale/applyQuality path untouched.

title: Dead duplicate peek-slot selector with a type-mismatch bug (`s.claimedBy !== agentX`)
description: cover-graph.js getBestPeekSlot (wrapped by `_getBestPeekSlot` at main.js line 12052) compares `s.claimedBy` (an enemy object) against `agentX` (a number coordinate) at line 251 `if (s.claimedBy && s.claimedBy !== agentX) continue;`. Since claimedBy is never a number, the condition is always true for any claimed slot, so every claimed slot is always skipped — the function can never reuse the agent's own slot. This is a buggy DUPLICATE of the LIVE selector Enemy._bestPeekSlot (main.js ~line 10826) which correctly does `if(s.claimedBy&&s.claimedBy!==this)continue;`. `_getBestPeekSlot`/`getBestPeekSlot` is never called from anywhere in src/ (only the wrapper definition + import alias exist), so it is dead code. The live path is unaffected.
evidence: main.js: `_getBestPeekSlot` defined at 12052-12054, zero call sites (grep `_getBestPeekSlot(` matches only the definition). cover-graph.js line 251: `if (s.claimedBy && s.claimedBy !== agentX) continue;` — claimedBy is an Enemy object, agentX is a float.
fix: Either delete the dead `_getBestPeekSlot` wrapper + its import alias and the cover-graph export, or, if it is meant to be revived, change its signature to take the agent object and fix line 251 to `s.claimedBy !== agent`. Lowest-risk: remove the dead wrapper to prevent a future caller hitting the broken comparison.
risk: Removing is safe (no callers). Reviving requires a signature change at all (zero) call sites. No runtime behavior changes today.

title: `_cellWallsAt` spatial-index point accessor is never called
description: `_cellWallsAt(idx,x,z)` is defined as the point-query accessor for the wall spatial index, but no code uses it. The actual hot-path consumers (main.js 10352-10363, 10391, 25047) index `_idx.cells[cellId]` inline instead of calling this helper. Harmless but dead, and a maintenance trap: the inline consumers and this helper compute the cell id with slightly different rounding (`((x-xMin)/cs)|0` here vs the inline DDA in canSee), so a future caller switching to this helper could silently diverge.
evidence: grep `_cellWallsAt` across src/ matches only the definition at line 11918. Hot paths instead do e.g. line 10360 `_cellWalls=_idx.cells[cellId];`.
fix: Delete `_cellWallsAt` (lines 11918-11924), or route the inline `_idx.cells[...]` lookups through it for a single source of truth. Prefer deletion since the inline DDA traversal is the perf-tuned path.
risk: Deletion is safe (no callers). No build/probe impact.

title: _stableFps frame limiter and applyOperatorConfig are dead; applyOperator (38833) is the real operator-config path
description: _stableFps(targetFps) (29122) is a frame-rate gate that is never called — the loop runs uncapped via setAnimationLoop. applyOperatorConfig() (29131) gives Havoc +1 grenade/+1 smoke, but the LIVE operator setup is applyOperator() at 38833 (called from all run-start paths 32582/32859/38548/38769/45177). applyOperatorConfig is a duplicate, partial, never-called version — competing-definition smell even though it can't fire.
evidence: function _stableFps(targetFps){...} // grep => def only. function applyOperatorConfig(){if(op==='havoc'){P.grenades+=1;P.smokes+=1;}} // grep applyOperatorConfig => def only; live path is applyOperator() (38833).
fix: Delete _stableFps (29120-29129) and applyOperatorConfig (29130-29141). Verify Havoc's +1 grenade/+1 smoke is actually applied inside the live applyOperator() at 38833; if it isn't, fold it there (don't keep two operator-config functions).

title: Cluster of never-called helpers: _xpProgress, _hudPulseColor, _flashEnemyAlert, updatePlayerFlags, squadChoreography, _checkPerfectBuilding, _gen* texture generators
description: Confirmed-orphan helpers (grep shows definition only, no callers): _xpProgress/_xpForLevel/XP_CURVE (29758-29771); _hudPulseColor (30007); _flashEnemyAlert (30017) — note it adds a setTimeout that restores visorM.emissive but is never triggered; updatePlayerFlags + PLAYER_FLAGS (29896-29912) — flags written here are read nowhere; squadChoreography (30027); _checkPerfectBuilding (30230); and the procedural texture generators _genGraffiti/_genTrashTexture/_genCarpetPattern/_genWoodGrain (30248-30333). These inflate the file and are prime candidates for the 'feature half-wired so it never triggers' risk. _genGraffiti also returns a raw canvas while the sibling _gen* return THREE.CanvasTexture — inconsistent contract if ever used.
evidence: grep _xpProgress/_hudPulseColor/_flashEnemyAlert/updatePlayerFlags/squadChoreography/_checkPerfectBuilding/_genGraffiti/_genTrashTexture/_genCarpetPattern/_genWoodGrain => each only its own def line. _genGraffiti returns canvas; _genTrashTexture returns new THREE.CanvasTexture(canvas).

title: _critMul computed then never used (downstream of _isCritHit)
description: Immediately after calling _isCritHit (in-scope at 25437), the consumer computes _critMul=_critInfo.crit?_critInfo.mul:(isHead?2.0:1.0) but never reads it; finalDmg recomputes its own factor inline. Dead local. Flagged because it is the direct evidence that the crit pathway is half-wired and supports the neck/spine bug above.
evidence: Line 26415: "const _critMul=_critInfo.crit?_critInfo.mul:(isHead?2.0:1.0);" — grep shows _critMul has zero other references.
fix: Either delete line 26415, or (preferred) use _critMul as the single source of truth in the finalDmg expression after correcting the body-crit math (see crit-neck-spine-nullified).
risk: None if deleted; if reused, couples with the crit math fix.

title: _aimRayDirWithSpread defined but never called (superseded by _aimRayDirWithSpreadFor)
description: _aimRayDirWithSpread is a single-camera spread helper that is never referenced anywhere in the repo; the live shoot path uses _aimRayDirWithSpreadFor (25897), which has a different, better spread model (polar disk sampling, yScale, bias) versus this function's square uniform spread. It also applies the camera quaternion after normalize (harmless mathematically) and uses uniform square spread, so its result would differ from the real path if it were ever wired up — a latent contradiction.
evidence: grep across src: only definition site "function _aimRayDirWithSpread(sp,out=new THREE.Vector3()){ return out.set((Math.random()-.5)*sp,(Math.random()-.5)*sp,-1).normalize().applyQuaternion(camera.quaternion); }" — zero callers (only _aimRayDirWithSpreadFor is called).
fix: Delete _aimRayDirWithSpread (25040-25042) to remove the competing/never-used spread model, or document it as unused. No call sites to update.
risk: None; removing unreferenced code keeps build/probes green.

title: EventBus is instantiated and exposed but never emitted to or subscribed
description: class EventBus is built, a singleton _eventBus is created, and it is exposed as window.__eventBus, but a repo-wide search shows _eventBus.emit / .on / .off and __eventBus.* are never called anywhere outside the class definition. The whole pub/sub layer is inert scaffolding.
evidence: const _eventBus=new EventBus(); window.__eventBus=_eventBus;  // grep -nE "_eventBus\.(emit|on|off)|__eventBus\." returns nothing
fix: Either delete EventBus + _eventBus + window.__eventBus (lines 28454-28463) as dead code, or actually wire it: e.g. call _eventBus.emit('kill',e) from the dropkick kill path and let HUD/audio subscribe. Lowest-risk: leave as a documented debug hook but mark it.
risk: Removing it is safe (no callers). If kept, no behavior change. Don't break: it is harmless to leave.

title: emitEvent() and EVENT_HOOKS telemetry ring buffer are never populated
description: emitEvent pushes into EVENT_HOOKS (capped at 200) and optionally into window.__game.events, but emitEvent is never called from anywhere. EVENT_HOOKS therefore stays permanently empty; the telemetry/debug hook is non-functional.
evidence: function emitEvent(name,data){ const ev={name,...}; EVENT_HOOKS.push(ev); ... }  // grep shows only the definition references emitEvent.
fix: Delete emitEvent + EVENT_HOOKS (28886-28893) or insert emitEvent calls at real game milestones (kill, building-clear, boss-phase). No runtime effect either way today.
risk: Safe to remove; nothing reads EVENT_HOOKS.

title: _applyMusicIntensityBoost writes MUSIC.intensity directly, contradicting the per-frame intensity lerp
description: _applyMusicIntensityBoost sets MUSIC.intensity=min(1, MUSIC.intensity+boost) directly. The live music driver (lines 13238-13241) every frame does MUSIC.intensityTarget=want; MUSIC.intensity += (intensityTarget-intensity)*lerp. So any direct boost to MUSIC.intensity would be immediately pulled back toward intensityTarget on the next frame — the two writers disagree about who owns MUSIC.intensity. The function is currently never called (dead), so it's a latent contradiction rather than an active bug.
evidence: 29050: MUSIC.intensity=Math.min(1,MUSIC.intensity+boost);  vs  13238-13239: MUSIC.intensityTarget=want; MUSIC.intensity+=(MUSIC.intensityTarget-MUSIC.intensity)*Math.min(dt*0.7,1);
fix: If music stingers are wanted, have _applyMusicIntensityBoost bump MUSIC.intensityTarget (and/or a transient floor) instead of MUSIC.intensity, so it survives the lerp. Otherwise delete the function + MUSIC_INTENSITY_BOOSTS table (29037-29051).
risk: Low. As long as it stays uncalled there is no behavior change; if wired, target the same field the frame loop reads (intensityTarget).

title: MOVEMENT_FLAGS / _refreshMovementFlags are dead; canDodge/canDoubleJump never updated and never read
description: MOVEMENT_FLAGS exposes canDodge/canDoubleJump initialized to false. _refreshMovementFlags() would set them from perks, but _refreshMovementFlags is never called, and MOVEMENT_FLAGS.canDodge/canDoubleJump are never read anywhere. Actual gating uses P._canDoubleJump (set at 31080 from hasPerk('doubleJump')) and hasPerk('dodgeRoll') (checked at 36734). So this is a fully redundant, never-refreshed shadow flag set — a contradiction-in-waiting (two sources of truth for the same capability).
evidence: 28993-28994: MOVEMENT_FLAGS.canDodge=hasPerk('dodgeRoll'); MOVEMENT_FLAGS.canDoubleJump=hasPerk('doubleJump');  but grep for MOVEMENT_FLAGS.can* reads returns only these writes; _refreshMovementFlags has zero callers. Live gating: 27805 if(P._canDoubleJump...), 36734 if(!hasPerk('dodgeRoll'))return;
fix: Delete MOVEMENT_FLAGS + _refreshMovementFlags (28982-28995), or make them the single source of truth and route the live checks through them. Do not leave both.
risk: Safe to delete; nothing reads the flags. Consolidating risks subtle gating changes — verify double-jump/dodge still gate correctly.

title: Large block of 'COMPREHENSIVE' helper functions are defined but never called
description: A contiguous 'comprehensive' block contains many functions that are defined once and never invoked anywhere: pickOperatorReflection (28480), _broadcastSquadBark (28496), _enemyAtCover (28503), _enemiesNearPosition (28509), _allEnemiesInZone (28518), generateRunMemoir (28821), _giveEnemyPersonality (28806), _hpLabel (28856), _weaponStatRadar (28946), _findActiveSynergies (28938), _shouldBark (29029), compileFullRunStats (29053), _formatStatsForDisplay (29092). All show exactly one occurrence (their own definition). This is the bulk of the new uncommitted scaffolding; it inflates the file and creates many landmines (e.g. _giveEnemyPersonality mutates e.speed/idealDist/_sit/shootTimer/burstMax and would change AI tuning if ever wired).
evidence: grep -c per symbol: pickOperatorReflection 2 (def+OPERATOR_REFLECTIONS list ref), _findActiveSynergies 1, _weaponStatRadar 1, generateRunMemoir 1, _giveEnemyPersonality 1, _hpLabel 1, _broadcastSquadBark 1, _enemyAtCover 1, _enemiesNearPosition 1, _allEnemiesInZone 1, _shouldBark 1, compileFullRunStats 1, _formatStatsForDisplay 1 — i.e. definition only.
fix: Treat the whole 28480-29092 region as a quarantine: confirm with grep (done) and either remove the unused functions or wire the few that are intended (e.g. show generateRunMemoir on the run-end screen, call _findActiveSynergies in the loadout/pause UI). Keep the data tables that ARE used (ENEMY_POSE_STATES at 8392/8398 is live, RECOIL_PATTERNS_LEARNABLE is live — do NOT delete those).
risk: Deleting genuinely-unreferenced functions is safe and shrinks main.js. Be careful NOT to delete ENEMY_POSE_STATES (used at 8392) or anything actually referenced; verify each symbol with grep before removal.

title: Two near-identically-named killcam systems coexist: triggerKillCamSlowMo (live) vs triggerKillcamOrbit/KILLCAM (dead)
description: triggerKillCamSlowMo + _killCamT/_killCamScale/_killCamDur is the real, heavily-used bullet-time-on-kill system (called from ~10 sites incl. shoot() lines 26484-26485). Immediately below it lives the dead KILLCAM/triggerKillcamOrbit orbit system (see killcam-orbit-dead-feature). The almost-identical names ('KillCamSlowMo' vs 'KillcamOrbit', '_killCamT' vs 'KILLCAM.t') are a maintenance trap: a future edit can easily wire or break the wrong one. Flagged as a contradiction/clarity hazard adjacent to the dead-code finding.
evidence: `function triggerKillCamSlowMo(scale,dur){ _killCamT=dur||0.85; ... }` (used) directly above `const KILLCAM={active:false,...}; function triggerKillcamOrbit(enemy){...}` (unused).
fix: When resolving killcam-orbit-dead-feature, either delete the orbit system or rename it unambiguously (e.g. KILLCAM_ORBIT / triggerKillcamOrbit clearly documented) so the two systems can't be confused. No behaviour change required beyond the orbit decision.
risk: None if only renaming/removing dead symbols; build/probes unaffected.

title: _collectGamepads is a dead duplicate of _gatherPadsOrdered
description: _collectGamepads (32635) and _gatherPadsOrdered (34143) are byte-for-byte the same logic (enumerate navigator.getGamepads(), keep connected pads, sort by index). _gatherPadsOrdered is the one wired into tickGamepad (34281). _collectGamepads is defined but never called anywhere (grep confirms only its own definition line).
evidence: function _collectGamepads(){ ... out.sort((a,b)=>(a.index||0)-(b.index||0)); return out;}  // vs function _gatherPadsOrdered(){ ... out.sort((a,b)=>(a.index|0)-(b.index|0));return out;} — only _gatherPadsOrdered() is called (line 34281).
fix: Delete _collectGamepads (lines 32635-32645). No callers, purely dead. Keeps the build green and removes a divergent copy that could drift from the real implementation.
risk: Negligible. No references; removal cannot affect runtime.

title: Radar enemy plotting computes rx_/rz_/ratio that are never used
description: In tickRadar enemy loop, rx_ and rz_ are computed (rotation by +P.yaw) and then immediately discarded; the actual plotting recomputes lx/lz with rotation by -P.yaw (which is the correct orientation, verified: enemy directly ahead plots above center for both yaw=0 and yaw=PI). `ratio=d/RADAR_RANGE` is also computed but never used. The interleaved comments (34854-34860) are stale/confused leftovers from iterating on the orientation math.
evidence: const rx_=Math.cos(ry)*dx+Math.sin(ry)*dz; const rz_=-Math.sin(ry)*dx+Math.cos(ry)*dz; // never used; const ratio=d/RADAR_RANGE; // never used; const px=cx+(lx/RADAR_RANGE)*RADAR_R; const py=cy+(lz/RADAR_RANGE)*RADAR_R;
fix: Remove the dead `ry`, `rx_`, `rz_`, and `ratio` lines and the stale comment block; keep only the `ang=-P.yaw` / lx / lz / px / py computation. Pure cleanup — the visible radar output is unchanged.
risk: Negligible. Removing unused locals; verified orientation math relies only on lx/lz.

title: attachDeagleGlbModel() and deagleSlideBone / restPos are unreachable dead code
description: `DEAGLE_GLB` is hardcoded `const DEAGLE_GLB=null;` (line 573, intentionally disabled per the comment at 567-568). `attachDeagleGlbModel()` opens with `if(deagleGlbRig||!DEAGLE_GLB)return;` — `!null` is always true, so the entire body (16034-16088) never executes. Consequently `deagleSlideBone` (declared line 16031) and the `restPos` it stashes (line 16082) are written only inside this dead function and are never read anywhere else in the file. The live skinned-USP path is `attachDeagleStaticModel` (16184), which does not use deagleSlideBone at all.
evidence: function attachDeagleGlbModel(){ if(deagleGlbRig||!DEAGLE_GLB)return; ... }  // DEAGLE_GLB===null (line 573) => always returns. deagleSlideBone/restPos written but never read (grep shows only 16031/16080/16081/16082).
fix: Optional cleanup: delete attachDeagleGlbModel (16032-16088) and the deagleGlbRig-unrelated globals deagleSlideBone (16031) + restPos write. Low priority — it is harmless dead weight, not a correctness bug. Do NOT revive the GLB path (forbidden by project rules).
risk: Removing is safe (truly unreferenced), but since it touches the disabled-GLB seam, leaving it is also fine. No functional change either way.

title: Entire CONFIG balance object is a dead, competing source of truth (0 reads anywhere)
description: const CONFIG={player:{moveSpeed:5.0,sprintSpeed:9.8,jumpHeight:5.8,gravity:14.0,maxHp:100,hpRegen:1.5,hpRegenDelay:5.0},combat:{headshotMul:2.0,backstabMul:3.0,closeRange:3.0,...,explosiveRadius:5.2,explosiveDmg:120},enemy:{aggroRadius:18.0,sightRadius:22.0,hearingRadius:14.0,...},ai:{...}} reads as the canonical design-intent table, but `grep -c '\bCONFIG\.' src/main.js` returns 0 — nothing in the runtime ever reads it. Every value it 'owns' is actually hardcoded inline somewhere else with potentially different numbers: player movement caps live in the per-archetype locomotion table (main.js:6123-6135), enemy sightRadius/aggro/spd live in the inline EM roster (main.js:6296+ e.g. soldier spd:2.6+diff*.50, sniper rng:22+diff*1.2), headshotMul is the inline 2.0 at main.js:25450/26415, explosiveRadius is the inline RADIUS=5.2 (main.js:23110) for grenades vs RADIUS=4.2 (main.js:33152) for barrels. So CONFIG is a phantom second source of truth that silently disagrees with (and is overridden by) the real inline values. The operator-region agent flagged only CONFIG.player.hpRegen/hpRegenDelay as unused; the cross-cutting truth is that the WHOLE object is inert. A future edit to CONFIG (e.g. nerfing headshotMul or sightRadius) would have zero effect, a classic 'I changed the config but nothing happened' trap.
evidence: const CONFIG={player:{moveSpeed:5.0,sprintSpeed:9.8,...}, combat:{headshotMul:2.0,...,explosiveRadius:5.2,explosiveDmg:120}, enemy:{aggroRadius:18.0,sightRadius:22.0,...}}  // grep -c '\bCONFIG\.' src/main.js == 0
fix: Either (a) delete CONFIG and the few dead helpers that pretend to consume it (tickHealthRegen at 29881, _adjustEnemyHp) to remove the misleading second truth, or (b) make it real by wiring the inline values to read from CONFIG (e.g. enemy roster uses CONFIG.enemy.sightRadius as the base for canSee, grenade explodeGrenade uses CONFIG.combat.explosiveRadius/explosiveDmg, headshot mul reads CONFIG.combat.headshotMul). Option (a) is lower risk and keeps the build green; option (b) is a larger refactor. At minimum, add a comment marking CONFIG as design-reference-only so nobody edits it expecting gameplay to change.
risk: Deleting CONFIG is safe (no readers) but must also remove the dead functions that reference it (tickHealthRegen, _adjustEnemyHp, DIFF_HP_MUL consumers) or they'll throw ReferenceError. Wiring it live risks changing tuned gameplay numbers — must diff each CONFIG value against the inline value it would replace. Keep static-probe scripts green.

title: SETTINGS.gradeIntensity has three disagreeing 'default' values in the same IIFE (.9 vs .9 vs 1)
description: Within the SETTINGS bootstrap IIFE the same key is defaulted three different ways: the base defaults object sets gradeIntensity:.9 (line 23307); the visual-patch version-bump reset block sets gradeIntensity:.9 (line 23336); but the per-key null-backfill sets `if(s.gradeIntensity==null)s.gradeIntensity=1;` (line 23396). So a save that explicitly stored null for gradeIntensity ends up at 1, while a fresh install or a version-bump migration ends up at .9 — the 'default' is path-dependent. It is inert in the current shipping build because STABLE_RENDERING_MODE forces colorGrade off (and _forceStableVisualSettings doesn't even touch gradeIntensity, so the value just sits unused), but it is a real constant-defined-twice-with-different-values contradiction that would surface the moment color grading is re-enabled.
evidence: 23307: smaa:false,pbrMaterials:true,vignette:false,gradeIntensity:.9,\n23336:       gradeIntensity:.9,\n23396:  if(s.gradeIntensity==null)s.gradeIntensity=1;
fix: Pick one canonical default and use it in all three spots. Change line 23396 to `if(s.gradeIntensity==null)s.gradeIntensity=.9;` to match the base default and the migration block.
risk: None today (grade disabled by STABLE mode). Future-proofing only; no save-compat concern (only affects the null-coalesce branch).

title: Five SETTINGS perf knobs are written into defaults/saved JSON but never read anywhere
description: maxPointLightsEffective (23298), perfHud-adjacent aiSkipFramesModulo (23299), reducedBloomish (23301), maxParticlesBlood and maxParticlesSmoke (23300) each appear exactly once in the entire codebase — only in the SETTINGS defaults object. They are serialized into clearance_settings and survive load, but no runtime code consults them. There is no particle-cap logic keyed off maxParticlesBlood/Smoke and no AI frame-skip keyed off aiSkipFramesModulo (grep confirms zero read sites). These are competing/abandoned config knobs: they imply behavior (light cap, blood/smoke caps, AI throttle) that is actually hardcoded elsewhere, so toggling them in a saved settings JSON does nothing — a silent contradiction between the settings surface and real behavior.
evidence: grep -c per key: maxPointLightsEffective=1, aiSkipFramesModulo=1, reducedBloomish=1, maxParticlesSmoke=1, maxParticlesBlood=1 — all single hits are the default declarations at 23298-23301. No reader exists.
fix: Either delete these keys from the defaults block (safe — they were never read, removing them cannot regress behavior; saved JSON keeps them harmlessly via Object.assign but new saves drop them) OR wire them to the systems they name. Lowest-risk: remove the dead keys to stop advertising config that does nothing. Do NOT remove keys that ARE read (raycastSpatialIndex=4, perfHud=2, aimAssist=2 are live).
risk: Very low. Removing write-only keys cannot break readers (there are none). Save-compat preserved: load still merges saved values onto defaults; an old save that contains these keys simply carries dead fields. No probe depends on them.

title: FIRE_VISUAL and MOTION_VISUAL tables omit weapon index 2 (knife) — silently fall back to rifle profile
description: FIRE_VISUAL (lines 133-141) and MOTION_VISUAL (lines 143-151) are keyed by weapon index but have no entry for index 2 (knife per WEAPON_INDEX_TYPE in profiles.js). getFireVisualProfile (line 158) and getMotionVisualProfile (line 154) both fall back to index 0 (rifle). When the knife is equipped, the throw/melee gets rifle-tuned kick (FIRE_VISUAL[0]: kickRX 0.28) and rifle bob/inertia (MOTION_VISUAL[0]). This is a feel inconsistency rather than a crash; knife throw is also driven mostly by the dedicated throw notify path (playerAnimEmitNotify 'throwStart'/'throwRelease' in main.js), so the visible effect is small.
evidence: playerAnimation.js: FIRE_VISUAL has keys {0,1,3,4,5,6,7} — no 2; MOTION_VISUAL has keys {0,1,3,4,5,6,7} — no 2. getFireVisualProfile: const base = FIRE_VISUAL[weaponIdx] || FIRE_VISUAL[0];
fix: Add a knife-tuned entry FIRE_VISUAL[2] (low/short kick, e.g. dur 0.16, kickRX 0.10) and MOTION_VISUAL[2] (lighter bob/inertia) if knife-specific viewmodel feel is desired; otherwise leave as intentional rifle fallback and document it. Low priority.
risk: Adding entries changes knife viewmodel kick/bob slightly — cosmetic only, no gameplay authority. Verify no probe asserts FIRE_VISUAL key count.

title: Alarm reinforcement entry alternates FE/FW per building, but the spawn toast always says 'East flank response incoming'
description: mergeNativeEncounterTactics sets r.entry = bn%2===0 ? 'spawnDoor_FE' : 'spawnDoor_FW' so reinforcements alternate east/west door per building. _spawnB01AlarmReinforcements (main.js line 35167-35169) correctly picks the west door for FW and east for FE. But the on-screen toast (main.js line 35196) is hardcoded to 'East flank response incoming' regardless of entry. For odd buildings (FW = west door) the enemies enter from the west while the banner claims east, contradicting the visible spawn direction.
evidence: nativeEncounterTactics.js line 309 `const entryAlt = bn % 2 === 0 ? 'spawnDoor_FE' : 'spawnDoor_FW';`. main.js line 35196 `attachToast('...East flank response incoming',2500);` is unconditional. The entry token is honored for door selection (35167-35169) but not for the toast copy.
fix: In _spawnB01AlarmReinforcements (main.js ~35196) derive the side from the resolved `door`/`entry` and word the toast accordingly (e.g. west vs east). Alternatively keep the alternation but make the entry default deterministic so the toast stays truthful. (Toast line itself is in main.js, outside this module, but the contradiction originates in the tactics module setting the alternation.)
risk: Very low. Copy-only change in main.js; no logic/state impact.

title: Cover-scatter set and mood-light color tables only defined for buildings 1-8
description: _coverSets only has keys 1..8 and falls back to _coverSets[1] (wooden crates) for bn 9-12 via `const cset=_coverSets[bn]||_coverSets[1];`. Likewise moodCol map `({1:..,..,8:..})[bn]||0xffd060` falls back to amber. So Act III buildings (9 Border, 10 Cathedral, 11 Freighter, 12 Spire) scatter wooden crates (cset name 'crate') and amber mood dots regardless of theme — a cathedral and a chrome spire both get warehouse crates as procedural cover. This reads as a half-finished extension when Act III was added (BUILDING_DIMS/pal/lightProfile/_texProfile all go to 12, but cover/mood tables stopped at 8).
evidence: const _coverSets={1:..,...,8:{name:'rack',...}}; const cset=_coverSets[bn]||_coverSets[1]; ... const moodCol=({1:0xff8040,...,8:0x40c8ff})[bn]||0xffd060;
fix: Add entries 9-12 to _coverSets (e.g. 9 sandbag/crate desert, 10 'pedestal'/'plinth' marble, 11 'rack'/'crate' steel, 12 'pillar' chrome) and to moodCol (9 0xffb060, 10 0xffe8b0, 11 0x80b0d0, 12 0xc8e0ff to match accentColors). Low effort, removes the warehouse-crate-in-a-cathedral incongruity.
risk: applySequenceLayout already provides the primary themed props for 9-12, so this scatter is supplementary; ensure new cover doesn't collide with sequence cells. Confirm probes don't assert cset for bn>8.

title: Dropkick sets _pushImpulse but it is never consumed (melee branch wins, bullet branch is gated out)
description: The dropkick handler sets e._pushImpulse (line 27649) in addition to e._dropkickPushImpulse (27626) and e._dropkickFlyImpulse (27627). But _pushImpulse is only consumed inside the else-if(this.bulletHitTimer>0) branch (lines 9824-9831). A dropkick sets meleeHitTimer=.10 (line 27645), so the FIRST if(this.meleeHitTimer>0) branch (line 9602) wins and the bullet branch never runs during the dropkick; bulletHitTimer is typically 0 for a dropkick anyway, so _pushImpulse (until=+250ms) expires unconsumed. The actual dropkick displacement is done by _dropkickPushImpulse + _dropkickFlyImpulse, making this third impulse redundant dead state.
evidence: e._pushImpulse={x:fx*(onLanding ? .50 : .64),z:fz*(onLanding ? .50 : .64),start:impactNow,until:impactNow+250};  // 27649 — never read for a dropkick
fix: Remove the _pushImpulse assignment at 27649 (the dropkick already has its two dedicated impulses), to avoid leaving stale impulse state that could mis-fire if a bullet hit lands within 250ms of a dropkick.
risk: Low. Removing an unconsumed write. Slim chance some other code reads _pushImpulse for a dropkicked enemy; grep shows it is only read in the bullet-hit branch, so risk is minimal.

title: Boss `peekBurst` comment says 'temporarily' but peekRate is buffed permanently (no restore)
description: The peekBurst boss command stores `boss._peekRateOrig` and multiplies `boss.peekRate` by cmd.mul, with the comment 'Bump peek rate temporarily for the duration of the phase'. There is no timer or revert that restores peekRate after the phase, and boss phases fire exactly once (`ph.fired`). So the buff is permanent, contradicting the comment. Functionally a permanent enrage is probably fine, but the stored `_peekRateOrig` is written and never read back, i.e. an effect set up for restoration that never happens.
evidence: line 12775-12777: `boss._peekRateOrig=boss._peekRateOrig||boss.peekRate; boss.peekRate=boss._peekRateOrig*(cmd.mul||2.0);` — no code reads `_peekRateOrig` to restore, and the comment claims it is temporary.
fix: Either drop the misleading 'temporarily' from the comment (accept permanent enrage), or actually make it temporary by recording an expiry (e.g. `boss._peekRateRestoreAt=performance.now()+ph.durMs`) and restoring `boss.peekRate=boss._peekRateOrig` in EnemyManager.update when that time passes. Documentation-vs-code mismatch only; no crash.
risk: Low. If made temporary, verify no other code already restores peekRate; if left permanent, just a comment edit.

title: Ammo-type penetration multiplier (pen) is computed but never applied
description: AMMO_TYPES advertise penetration behavior ('Better through cover', 'breaks on cover') and getAmmoMul() returns {dmg,pen,falloff}. The shoot path uses _ammoMul.falloff (line 26410) and _ammoMul.dmg (line 26417) but never uses _ammoMul.pen. So Armor-Piercing's 1.6× penetration and Hollow-Point's 0.4× penetration descriptions are unfulfilled — the only real differences between ammo types are raw damage and falloff. The headline 'through cover' promise is dead.
evidence: pen:t?t.penetrationMul:1.0,  // in getAmmoMul; but only _ammoMul.falloff and _ammoMul.dmg are read in the firing code (26410,26417); grep for _ammoMul.pen / penetrationMul application returns nothing.
fix: If wallbang/penetration logic exists for the weapon's through-cover damage, multiply that penetration strength (or post-penetration damage retention) by _ammoMul.pen at the penetration site. If penetration is out of scope, soften the AMMO_TYPES descriptions so they don't advertise unimplemented cover behavior. Low priority since dmg/falloff differences still make ammo types meaningful.
risk: Low. Either a small multiply at the penetration site or a copy-only desc edit.

title: B01 alarm-pair reinforcement spawn is unreachable in the shipping B01 (megaplex) level
description: _spawnCampaignReinforcement -> _spawnB01AlarmReinforcements is only invoked from the reinforcement-drain loop (main.js 41638-41648), which is gated by `G.encounterDirector && hasEnc(encounterDef) && authCE`. But B01 always uses buildMegaplexB01Map, which returns disableEncounterDirector:true, encounterDef:null and spawnDoors:[] — so _syncEncounterDirectorFromLevel sets G.encounterDirector=null (line 6050-6052) and the drain loop never runs for B01. Even if it were reached, _spawnB01AlarmReinforcements reads G.levelData.spawnDoors (empty for megaplex) and returns immediately at `if(!z0.length)return;` (line 35164), so it would never spawn the pair nor show the 'WIDE ALERT' toast. The b01_alarm_pair squad authored in campaignEncounters.js (lines 428, 552) and its story cue thus never fire in the live game.
evidence: function _spawnB01AlarmReinforcements(...){ ... const doors=(G.levelData&&G.levelData.spawnDoors)||[]; const z0=doors.filter(d=>d.zoneId===0); if(!z0.length)return; ...}  // B01 megaplex returns spawnDoors:[] and disableEncounterDirector:true
fix: Two options: (1) If alarm reinforcements should fire in B01, give buildMegaplexB01Map a small set of zone-0 spawnDoors (with ax/az/inwardX/inwardZ) and wire a megaplex-specific reinforcement trigger (since the encounter director is disabled), or (2) accept it as intentionally retired and delete the unreachable _spawnB01AlarmReinforcements + the b01_alarm_pair authoring to remove the contradiction. Recommend confirming design intent before touching campaignEncounters.js.
risk: Option 1 changes B01 difficulty/feel and needs spawn-door geometry; option 2 is data deletion that could affect tests/probes referencing b01_alarm_pair. Verify the 32 static probes after either.

title: Death-variant selection duplicated with divergent logic between enemyAnimationController and importedClipController
description: deathVariantFromEnemy (enemyAnimationController.js lines 50-56) and semanticClipForEnemyStatus (importedClipController.js lines 99-104) both decide deathBack/deathSide/deathForward from staggerDir.x/lastPlayerDir.x with the same 0.45 side threshold, but semanticClipForEnemyStatus additionally treats state.includes('back') as deathBack while deathVariantFromEnemy does not. They can therefore disagree on the chosen death variant for the same enemy. deathVariantFromEnemy feeds status.deathVariant / status.channels.additive (display + procedural cue), while semanticClipForEnemyStatus drives imported-clip selection. Imported animation is flag-gated OFF by default (animationFeatureFlags.importedAnimationEnabled=false in profiles.js line 7), so the clip path is dormant and the divergence is latent, but it is a real duplicate-definition contradiction waiting to surface if the flag is enabled.
evidence: enemyAnimationController.js deathVariantFromEnemy: if (side > 0.45) return 'deathSide'; return 'deathForward';  (no 'back' check)  vs importedClipController.js semanticClipForEnemyStatus: if (enemy._deathByDropkick || state.includes('back')) return 'deathBack'; if (side > 0.45) return 'deathSide'; return 'deathForward';
fix: Extract a single shared deathVariant helper (e.g. in importedClipController.js or a small shared module) and have both call sites use it, so the display variant and the clip variant always agree. Keep the union of conditions (the 'back' check from semanticClipForEnemyStatus).
risk: Low — both paths are tiny and one is dormant. Refactor must keep enemy-intent-animation-static-probe.mjs green.

title: validateWeaponViewmodel hardcodes rifle-specific required nodes, ignoring entry.mechanicalParts/type
description: validateWeaponViewmodel() always enforces requiredNodes=['WeaponRoot','visual','sockets','mag','trigger','chargingHandle'] regardless of weapon type, even though it accepts an `entry` with type/mechanicalParts and the manifest declares per-weapon mechanicalParts (e.g. weapon.knife=['blade'] with no trigger/mag/chargingHandle, weapon.shotgun=['trigger','pump','shell','ejectionPort'] with no chargingHandle). Any future authored knife/grenade/shotgun GLB validated through this path would always fail on mag/trigger/chargingHandle. Currently latent: main.js only ever calls validateWeaponViewmodel for weapon.rifle (the M4), for which the list is correct.
evidence: weaponViewmodelLoader.js:150 `const requiredNodes = ['WeaponRoot', 'visual', 'sockets', 'mag', 'trigger', 'chargingHandle'];` then :153 `for (const name of requiredNodes) if (!nodes.has(name)) errors.push(...)`. The function signature takes `entry` (with entry.mechanicalParts) but never uses it for requiredNodes. Sole caller: main.js:19445 for weapon.rifle only.
fix: Derive requiredNodes from the entry when present: `const requiredNodes = options.requiredNodes || ['WeaponRoot','visual','sockets', ...(entry.mechanicalParts || ['mag','trigger','chargingHandle'])];` (or split into structural nodes WeaponRoot/visual/sockets plus entry.mechanicalParts). Keeps current M4 behavior identical while making the validator type-correct for future authored weapons.
risk: Low. Only path in use today is the rifle, which already supplies trigger/mag/chargingHandle, so M4 validation result is unchanged. Touches a pure validation helper, no render path.

title: Floorplan-based enterRoom() can never match an encounter (floorplan-space ids vs flow-room ids), so its activeEncounterId/lastTrigger assignments are dead and it can transiently null activeEncounterId
description: tick() runs the floorplan block first and calls enterRoom(id) where id comes from pickFloorplanSpaceId — a FLOORPLAN-SPACE id (dock_intake, alarm_relay_room, ...). enterRoom does `encountersCatalog.find(e => e.room === roomId || e.room === parentRoom)`, but every catalog encounter's `room` is a FLOW id (b01_intake_peek, ...). The find never hits, so enterRoom always leaves activeEncounterId=null (after setting it null on line 157). The real activeEncounterId comes from the later flow block via enterFlowRoom->startEncounter. On a frame where only the floorplan space changes (but not the flow room), enterRoom nulls activeEncounterId and it stays null until the next flow transition. activeEncounterId is consumed only by snapshot() (debug HUD) and the dev console, so the only effect is a transient/incorrect debug 'active encounter' value — no gameplay impact.
evidence: encounterDirector.js:160 `this.encountersCatalog.find((e) => e && (e.room === roomId || e.room === parentRoom))` with roomId from pickFloorplanSpaceId (line 345). Encounter rooms are flow ids (campaignEncounters.js:357,382,408,439,464). `grep activeEncounterId src/main.js` -> only debug setters (45112-45113) and snapshot read.
fix: Either drop the encounter-matching half of enterRoom() (keep only the room-transition logging it shares with tick) since enterFlowRoom is the live path, or map the floorplan space id to its flow room before matching. Lowest risk: leave behavior, but stop nulling activeEncounterId in enterRoom when no floorplan match is possible (guard the null-set so the flow-driven id is not clobbered) to keep the debug HUD honest.
risk: Debug/tooling only; no gameplay or save-compat impact. Keep snapshot() shape unchanged.

title: Vestigial deagle mesh aliases declared but unused (deBarrelTip/deBarrelV1-3/deRearCap/deGasCyl/deTopRib1-2 etc.)
description: Lines 16021-16025 declare a block of const aliases pointing existing pistol meshes at old-Deagle part names (deTopBlk=deBreech, deBarrel=deSuppr, deBarrelV1=deSuppr, deRearCap=deBreech, deGasCyl=deSuppr, deSafety=deDecocker, deRailG4=deRailFwd, deHammerCr=deHammer). A grep shows several of these (deBarrelTip, deBarrelV1-3, deRearCap, deGasCyl, deTopRib1/2) are only ever defined here and never read elsewhere, so they are dead aliases kept for a now-removed animation contract. They are harmless (no double gunGrp.add) but add confusion; note that deBarrel=deSuppr means any code that DID move 'deBarrel' would actually move the suppressor mesh.
fix: Remove the aliases that grep confirms are unreferenced (deBarrelTip, deBarrelV1-3, deRearCap, deGasCyl, deTopRib1, deTopRib2) after confirming no references exist file-wide; keep only those actually read by the pistol animation tick (verify deBarrel/deSafety/deRailG4/deHammerCr usage before deleting). Comment-clarify any retained alias.
risk: Must grep-confirm zero references before deleting each alias or the build breaks (ReferenceError). Several may still be referenced by the deagle animation routine outside this scope — verify first. Low risk if grep is exhaustive.

title: Compiled custom map key light has no shadow camera frustum, so shadows are invisible/badly clipped
description: The compiler creates the directional key light with `new THREE.DirectionalLight(0xffd49a, 0.92)`, sets `key.castShadow=false`, and pushes it into `shadowCasters`. main.js's `_applyShadowQuality()` (line 23431-23434) then flips `light.castShadow=true` for every entry in `shadowCasters` when shadows are enabled. But the compiler NEVER configures `key.shadow.camera.left/right/top/bottom/near/far`, `key.shadow.mapSize`, or `key.shadow.bias`. A THREE.DirectionalLight defaults to a shadow frustum of left/right/top/bottom = +/-5 and near 0.5. The custom map bounds are x:+/-18, z:+/-54. So shadows only render in a tiny +/-5 box around origin and are clipped/absent everywhere else. The campaign level explicitly configures this (main.js `_configureLevelShadowLight`, lines 3160-3163: left/right=+/-22, top/bottom=+/-24, far=52, plus mapSize/bias). Custom maps therefore look conspicuously flat and ungrounded versus the campaign the moment you load one.
evidence: compiler: `const key = new THREE.DirectionalLight(0xffd49a, 0.92); ... key.castShadow = false; ... shadowCasters.push(key);` with no `key.shadow.*` configuration. main.js _applyShadowQuality: `for(const light of levelData.shadowCasters){ if(light)light.castShadow=enabled; }`. Campaign reference main.js:3160 `light.shadow.camera.near=.5; light.shadow.camera.far=52; light.shadow.camera.left=-22;...`
fix: In customMapCompiler.js right after creating `key` (line 870), configure its shadow to cover the map: `key.shadow.mapSize.set(1024,1024); key.shadow.bias=-0.00018; key.shadow.normalBias=0.018; key.shadow.camera.near=0.5; key.shadow.camera.far=120; key.shadow.camera.left=-Math.max(24,(geo.map.bounds.x1-geo.map.bounds.x0)/2+6); key.shadow.camera.right=-key.shadow.camera.left; key.shadow.camera.top=Math.max(40,(geo.map.bounds.z1-geo.map.bounds.z0)/2+6); key.shadow.camera.bottom=-key.shadow.camera.top; key.shadow.camera.updateProjectionMatrix();`. Leave castShadow=false here (main.js toggles it on). This gives compiled custom maps real grounding shadows.
risk: Low. Pure additive shadow config; no save-compat impact. Larger shadow frustum slightly lowers shadow resolution density but 1024 over a 36x108 area is acceptable; could bump to 1536 on high. Keeps build/probes green (no API/contract change).

title: Megaplex B01 level casts ZERO shadows — directional key light has castShadow=false and is never registered as a shadow caster
description: The only level-wide light that could cast a sun/key shadow is the DirectionalLight `key`. It is built with `key.castShadow=false`, a full 2048x2048 shadow camera is then configured (all dead config), and `key` is pushed into `ceilingLights` but NOT into the `shadowCasters` array. The `shadowCasters` array (declared line 37733) is returned (line 38207) but is NEVER pushed to anywhere in this builder, so it is always empty. All GLB point lights are also forced `object.castShadow=false` (line 37875). `_applyShadowQuality()` (line 23431-23435) only toggles castShadow on lights in `levelData.shadowCasters`, so even with shadow quality on High the megaplex renders completely shadowless. The whole loading-dock megaplex therefore looks flat/CG with no grounding contact shadows — the single biggest 'not AAA' tell on load. Compare buildAimDemoMap (line 38314-38319) which sets key.castShadow=true and pushes key into shadowCasters.
evidence: const key=new THREE.DirectionalLight(0xffd49a,.95); ... key.castShadow=false; key.shadow.mapSize.set(2048,2048); key.shadow.camera.left=-75;...; localObjects.push(key,key.target);ceilingLights.push(key);  // shadowCasters[] declared at 37733 but never pushed; returned empty at 38207
fix: Set `key.castShadow=true` (the shadow camera is already sized -75..75 / -135..135 near 1 far 180, covering the level) and add `shadowCasters.push(key);` right after the existing `localObjects.push(key,key.target);ceilingLights.push(key);` line. This lets `_applyShadowQuality` enable/disable it per quality setting and gives the level real directional shadows. Keep point lights non-shadow-casting for perf.
risk: Shadow rendering perf cost on this large level. Mitigated because _applyShadowQuality gates castShadow by SETTINGS.shadowQuality/quality (off on low). Confirm static probes don't assert shadowCasters.length===0 for this map; visualStats already advertises csmSplits:0 so a single shadowed directional is consistent. Does not touch save data.

title: Player muzzle flash uses normal blending + tone-mapped color, so it reads dull on every shot
description: The player's first-person muzzle flash planes share `_pmfMat` (a MeshBasicMaterial with color 0xffee99, opacity peaks at only 0.55 in _pulseMuzzleFlashForSlot). It is NOT additive and NOT toneMapped:false, while the renderer runs ACESFilmicToneMapping at exposure 1.06 (lines 14731-14732). ACES compresses the warm yellow and, without additive blending, the flash blends over the scene like an opaque pale card instead of glowing. Every other glow in the game (dropkick streaks line 17235, light pools, fiber lights) uses THREE.AdditiveBlending. This is the single most-seen VFX in the game (fires on every shot) and currently looks flat/weak.
evidence: const _pmfMat=new THREE.MeshBasicMaterial({color:0xffee99,transparent:true,opacity:0,depthWrite:false,side:THREE.DoubleSide});  // no blending:AdditiveBlending, no toneMapped:false ... and _pulseMuzzleFlashForSlot sets mat.opacity=0.55*suppressedMul
fix: Add `blending:THREE.AdditiveBlending, toneMapped:false` to the `_pmfMat` definition at line 16812 and the `_pmfMatP2` definition at line 16821, and bump the peak in _pulseMuzzleFlashForSlot (line 16852) from 0.55 to ~0.9. Optionally brighten color to 0xfff0b0. One-line material edits, covers all 6 flash planes since H/V/D each share their slot material.
risk: Additive bright flash could look slightly hot at very high fire rates; opacity is already gated by setTimeout so it self-clears. No save-compat or build impact. Keep depthWrite:false (already present) so it composites correctly.

title: Primary tactical-glass `window` builder uses flat MeshPhongMaterial while ctx.aaPhysicalGlass (transmission glass) sits unused
description: The `window` builder is the dominant glass element across all 11 procedural buildings (every EXTRA_ELEMENTS list and serviceHall/glassPreview/vestibuleThreshold kits funnel through it). It hard-codes a plain MeshPhongMaterial with opacity 0.22 and no transmission/refraction. Meanwhile ctx.aaPhysicalGlass (the real MeshPhysicalMaterial with transmission/IOR, used by the rarely-instanced `glass` builder at line 1152 and the B01-only addB01Glass at line 333) is available in ctx but never used here. The result: almost all in-game windows read as a flat tinted plane, while the few `glass` partitions look like real glass — an inconsistency the player sees immediately on every level.
evidence: const glassM = new THREE.MeshPhongMaterial({ color: e.col || 0xa8c8e0, transparent: true, opacity: 0.22, shininess: 220, specular: 0xffffff, depthWrite: false });  // ctx.aaPhysicalGlass available but not called
fix: Mirror the `glass` builder's quality gate: at line 1653, if (ctx.settings?.quality === 'high' || 'ultra') && typeof ctx.aaPhysicalGlass === 'function', build glassM = ctx.aaPhysicalGlass({color:e.col||0xa8c8e0, shininess:220, specular:0xffffff, transparent:true, opacity:0.22}, {transmission:0.42, thickness:0.06, roughness:0.12}); else fall back to the existing phong. Keep userData.glassPane=true so the solids filter still includes it (transmission materials are transparent and would otherwise be excluded — main.js:37925 keeps glassPane in solids).
risk: MeshPhysicalMaterial/transmission is more expensive; gate behind quality like the `glass` builder already does. Verify breakability still works: pane keeps glassPane/breakable userData so _shatterMesh path is unaffected. No save-compat impact.

title: Explosion corona disc is never billboarded — the blast's brightest element is edge-on / invisible from most angles
description: spawnExplosionFx builds the bright additive corona as a flat PlaneGeometry(2,2) at corona.position.copy(pos) with the default world orientation (facing +Z). It is pushed into G.trails as {isFlash:true} WITHOUT faceCameraBillboard:true and is never passed through _orientVfxBillboard. The trail updater (line 44277) only re-orients a flash plane when faceCameraBillboard is set, so the corona stays world-axis-aligned. Whenever the player isn't looking roughly along ±Z, the corona renders edge-on (a thin sliver) or back-facing — so the single biggest visual punch of a grenade blast is usually invisible. Every other corona/flash in the file (e.g. muzzle corona line 24341, impact ring line 24064-24066) is correctly billboarded.
evidence: const corona=new THREE.Mesh(new THREE.PlaneGeometry(2.0,2.0),coronaM); corona.position.copy(pos); scene.add(corona); G.trails.push({mesh:corona,mat:coronaM,timer:.20,maxTime:.20,isFlash:true});  // no faceCameraBillboard, no _orientVfxBillboard
fix: Add faceCameraBillboard:true to the corona trail entry and orient it once at spawn: after `corona.position.copy(pos);` add `_orientVfxBillboard(corona,camera,Math.random()*Math.PI);` and change the push to `G.trails.push({mesh:corona,mat:coronaM,timer:.20,maxTime:.20,isFlash:true,faceCameraBillboard:true,growRate:6});` so it always faces the camera (matching the muzzle corona at 24341).
risk: Negligible. Reuses existing billboard helper and the same per-frame path used by every other flash. No save/perf/state impact; only makes an already-spawned mesh visible from all angles. Slightly larger apparent flash, which is the intent.

title: Outgoing thrown knife has NO motion trail — return arc is lavish, throw is a bare spinning box
description: Every addTrail call in updateKnives lives inside the k.returning branch (knife-return halo, knife-return-magnetic spiral, cross, catch-snap — 4 trail types). The forward physics tick for an alive, in-flight knife (the part the player watches most) adds zero trail. At 50 m/s with tumble=Math.PI*9 the thrown knife reads as a gray tumbling cube with no whoosh/streak, then suddenly sprouts a gorgeous glowing recall arc on the way back. This asymmetry is both a visible-on-screen AAA miss and a visual inconsistency.
evidence: Physics tick: `k.vel.y-=16*dt; k.lastSafePos=prev.clone(); k.grp.position.copy(next); k.grp.rotateOnAxis(new THREE.Vector3(1,0,0),k.tumble*dt);` — no addTrail. Meanwhile the return branch (20023-20058) issues addTrail for kinds knife-return / knife-return-magnetic / knife-return-catch-snap.
fix: In the physics tick (after `k.grp.position.copy(next)` around line 20180), add a throttled motion trail mirroring the return style, e.g.: `addTrail(prev,next,{kind:'knife-throw',haloColor:0x80e8ff,coreColor:0xffffff,haloRadius:.030,coreRadius:.007,life:.085,haloOpacity:.55,coreOpacity:.95});`. Per-frame segLen at 50 m/s (~0.83m) clears addTrail's len<.05 guard. Optionally gate to every other frame via k._lastFlightTrailAt like the return path to keep trail-pool pressure low.
risk: Low. addTrail is the same pooled VFX used by the return arc and bullets; one call per frame per in-flight knife (usually 0-1 knives) is negligible. No state change, purely additive visual. Keep haloRadius modest so it doesn't overpower the recall arc.

title: Ballistic tracer is a fixed 0.30m stub that teleports in large gaps for fast rounds
description: spawnProjectile builds a CylinderGeometry of fixed length 0.30m and tickProjectiles only calls _alignCyl (orientation + midpoint position, no scaling). DMR=680 m/s and Sniper=920 m/s travel ~11-15m per 60fps frame, but the visible tracer stays 0.30m long and is centered on the segment midpoint, so the streak appears as a tiny dash hopping in big gaps far from the bullet's actual swept path. The spawn code clearly intended a streak (it pre-aligns along dir*0.30).
evidence: "const tr=new THREE.Mesh(new THREE.CylinderGeometry(.012,.012,.30,5,1,true),trM);" and in tick: "if(p.mesh){_alignCyl(p.mesh,prev,p.pos);}" where _alignCyl never sets scale. BALLISTICS: 5:{speed:680...}, 7:{speed:920...}.
fix: After _alignCyl in tickProjectiles, stretch the tracer along its local Y to cover the swept segment: compute segLen=p.pos.distanceTo(prev); then p.mesh.scale.set(1, Math.max(1, segLen/0.30), 1). (CylinderGeometry's length axis is Y, which _alignCyl aligns to the travel dir.) Optionally clamp to a max so it doesn't span the whole map: Math.min(segLen/0.30, 60).
risk: Purely visual; very low risk. Reusing one geometry with per-frame scale is cheap. No disposal change needed (geometry already disposed on removal).

title: Enemy gunfire casts NO dynamic light — flat additive sprite only; player gun has a PointLight muzzle flash
description: Enemy muzzleLight is hardcoded null (line 7049) 'for perf', so enemy muzzle flashes are pure additive plane sprites that never illuminate the surrounding geometry. The player's own weapon DOES get a PointLight muzzle flash (line 16811). In a dark room-clearing shooter, an enemy firing from a shadowed corner should briefly strobe light onto nearby walls/floor — this is one of the highest-impact 'looks AAA instantly' cues and its absence reads as flat. A single pooled, budgeted light shared across all enemies (lit only at the nearest firing enemy for one frame) avoids the original per-enemy-light perf cliff.
fix: Add ONE shared scene PointLight (e.g. G._enemyMuzzleLight, intensity 0, distance ~5, color 0xffcc66) created once. In EnemyManager.update, when a shot fires, position it at `mp` (getMuzzlePos), set intensity ~3.2*_flashMul, and decay it to 0 over ~60ms in the frame loop (or via the same setTimeout that hides the sprites at line 12919). This bounds dynamic lights to exactly one regardless of enemy count, sidestepping the shader-hitch reason the per-enemy light was removed.
risk: One extra PointLight in the lighting budget — verify it does not push past the renderer's max-lights and trigger a shader recompile; keep intensity/decay short. Tone-mapping/exposure unchanged. Keeps probes green (no API surface change).

title: addRouteOverlay recompiles the entire map geometry once per route waypoint, every render
description: Inside `addRouteOverlay`, for each waypoint (index>0) it calls `collectCustomMapGeometry(map, kit())` again to test if the segment is wall-blocked. `collectCustomMapGeometry` is the full compile pass (aperture cutouts, wall splitting, perimeter walls, tactical graph, player-spawn repair). With several patrol/flank routes of N points each, renderViewport triggers O(total route points) full recompiles. Combined with the recompiles in addCompiledObjects (1135), addAnalysisOverlay (913), and placementQuality/ghost (415), a moderately complex map can recompile geometry dozens of times per renderViewport. renderViewport runs on every mousemove (3069) and during paint/move drags, producing visible editor jank exactly when authoring routes.
evidence: `const blocked = kit() && collectCustomMapGeometry(map, kit()).walls.some((wall) => { ... });` inside `pts.forEach((p, index) => { ... if (index > 0) { ... } })`.
fix: Compute geometry once at the top of renderViewport and thread it (or a cached walls array) into addCompiledObjects/addMarkers/addRouteOverlay/addAnalysisOverlay/placementQuality, rather than each helper re-calling collectCustomMapGeometry. Minimal version: hoist `const geo = kit() ? collectCustomMapGeometry(map, kit()) : null;` into renderViewport and pass `geo.walls` to addRouteOverlay so line 1298 reuses it instead of recompiling per point.
risk: Low-medium. Must ensure the cached geo reflects the current map mutation each render (it does, since renderViewport runs after every edit). No save-compat impact; build/probes unaffected.

title: All SFX connect raw to ctx.destination with no master limiter — heavy auto-fire clips/distorts; a single DynamicsCompressor is a cheap AAA audio polish
description: sfxShoot stacks main crack (gain .55) + slap-back delay (.25) + low thump (.30) + HF crackle (.18) per shot, all connected directly to c.destination (no shared bus). With an auto weapon that is several overlapping shots, plus the music master, all summing into the hardware output un-limited. There is no DynamicsCompressorNode anywhere in src (grep: 0 hits) and 104 direct c.destination connections in main.js alone. During intense combat the output clips, producing audible crackle/distortion that immediately reads as 'amateur audio'. A single shared limiter on the output is the classic one-node fix that makes the whole mix feel produced.
evidence:
s.connect(f);f.connect(g);g.connect(c.destination);s.start();  // line 12966
... dly.connect(g2);g2.connect(c.destination);  // 12976
... lo.connect(lg);lg.connect(c.destination);  // 12988
... cg... cg.connect(c.destination);  // 12997 — four sources per shot, no limiter; grep createDynamicsCompressor => 0
fix: Minimal-touch route: in audio.js getAC(), create the context AND a shared limiter once: AC=new AudioContext(); const comp=AC.createDynamicsCompressor(); comp.threshold.value=-8; comp.ratio.value=12; comp.attack.value=0.002; comp.release.value=0.18; comp.connect(AC.destination); AC._masterBus=comp; return AC. Then expose AC._masterBus and have the hot, layered emitters (at minimum sfxShoot's four .connect(c.destination) at 12966/12976/12988/12997, plus REVERB.dryGain/REVERB.conv in musicInit at 13134-13135) connect to c._masterBus instead of c.destination. Even routing ONLY sfxShoot's four nodes through the limiter audibly tames combat clipping with near-zero risk.
risk: Adding a compressor on the existing summed output can never break audio (it only sums + limits). Routing only the loudest/most-frequent emitter (sfxShoot) keeps the diff tiny and the static probes green. Do not move all 104 destination connects at once — surgical subset is enough and lower-risk.

title: Per-building convolution reverb is wired ONLY to the music master; gunshots/melee never get the room reverb, so every environment sounds acoustically identical
description: musicInit builds a per-building convolution reverb (REVERB.conv / sendGain / dryGain) and reverbSetBuilding swaps a hand-authored IR per environment (dock metallic .55s, subway tunnel 3.2s, cathedral 3.6s, etc.). But the reverb send is fed only by MUSIC.masterGain (lines 13131-13132). Every SFX one-shot — including the loudest, most-heard sound, the gunshot — connects directly to c.destination and bypasses the convolver entirely. The result: a shot in the dock sounds exactly like a shot in the cathedral. The single most impactful 'this place sounds real' AAA cue (gunshot tail length changing per room) is computed (the IRs are built and switched) but never applied to weapons — an effect-built-but-not-wired.
fix: Expose the reverb send (e.g. window-less module ref REVERB.sendGain) and add a parallel tap from the loud impact SFX: in sfxShoot after building g, add a wet send 'if(REVERB.sendGain){const wg=c.createGain();wg.gain.value=cfg.gain*0.35; g... wg... g connects to both c.destination and wg; wg.connect(REVERB.sendGain);}'. Cheapest version: feed only the main crack node (line 12966) into REVERB.sendGain at ~0.3 gain. Guard with if(REVERB.sendGain&&REVERB.conv.buffer) so it no-ops before musicInit.
risk: Reverb is additive and gated by sendGain wet level — worst case is too-wet shots in long-IR rooms (subway/cathedral); start with a low send (~0.25-0.35) and per-weapon scaling. Must null-check REVERB.sendGain because sfxShoot can fire before musicInit. Keep the change inside sfxShoot to limit blast radius and keep probes green.

title: Megaplex base lighting is very dim/flat (hemi .42, ambient .18, key .95, no shadows) and point lights hard-capped to 3 visible
description: The runtime base lights for the megaplex are HemisphereLight .42, AmbientLight .18, DirectionalLight key .95 (and the key casts no shadow per megaplex-no-shadows-flat). On top of that, updateManagedLights (38116-38123) hard-caps to `cap=3` visible point lights within a 52m radius, and each GLB point light intensity was already crushed to `Math.min(1.55,Math.max(.18,intensity*.006))` (line 37877). Net result is a uniformly dim, low-contrast, low-key-fill scene with almost no local pools of light — reads as flat/unfinished rather than the moody high-contrast look the rest of the project targets. This compounds the missing shadows.
evidence: const hemi=new THREE.HemisphereLight(0x9fb8d4,0x17130f,.42); ... const ambient=new THREE.AmbientLight(0x8190a0,.18); ... const key=new THREE.DirectionalLight(0xffd49a,.95); ... const cap=3,hard=52*52;
fix: Cheap visible win: bump the key DirectionalLight to ~1.6-2.2 and enable its shadow (see megaplex-no-shadows-flat) for directional grounding, and raise the managed-light `cap` from 3 to ~5-6 (still budgeted) so room pools of light are visible as the player moves. Optionally raise per-point-light floor from .18. Keep hemi/ambient low so the key/point contrast reads. All values are tunable constants; no structural change.
risk: Lighting/perf tuning — raising cap adds active point lights (still bounded by distance hard=52^2). Validate against visualStats/light-budget probes which advertise realPointLights:managedRoomLights.length. Avoid exceeding the 12-light triage threshold in _perfTriage (line 41536). Medium confidence on exact numbers; direction is sound.

title: Rich per-cue 'tone' metadata (danger/boss/success/objective) is authored but only mapped to a data-attribute — high-value, low-risk styling hook
description: Every cue carries a semantic tone ('story','danger','objective','success','boss'). The renderer only forwards it as root.dataset.tone (main.js 34361).
